title: Digitalgipfel in Berlin: Merz fordert mehr digitale Souveränität
content_c:
Digitalgipfel in Berlin Deutschland soll zur "KI-Nation 2030" werden
In Sachen KI hängt Deutschland international hinterher. Bei einem Digitalgipfel in Berlin forderte Kanzler Merz daher einen schnellen und energischen Ausbau der KI-Fähigkeiten. Doch viel Zeit bleibt dafür nicht mehr, sagen Experten.
Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz hat im internationalen KI-Wettbewerb für mehr Geschwindigkeit in Deutschland und Europa geworben. "Wir können und ich finde, wir müssen in Deutschland und in Europa viel schneller und besser darin werden, digitale Technologien zu entwickeln und sie auch wirklich zu nutzen", sagte Merz beim Digitalgipfel der Bundesregierung in Berlin. "Wir müssen, wir wollen Spitzenreiter werden."
Er kündigte eine Doppelstrategie an: Kurzfristig solle die Entwicklung industriell nutzbarer KI-Modelle gefördert werden, um die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit der Unternehmen zu sichern. Parallel dazu werde die Forschung an KI-Modellen der Zukunft, etwa im Bereich der physischen KI, vorangetrieben.
Ziel: Abhängigkeiten von USA reduzieren
Ziel sei es, technologische Abhängigkeiten - von den Tech-Riesen in den USA und China - zu reduzieren. Dabei setzt Merz auf internationale Kooperation, etwa mit Frankreich und Kanada, um Wissen zu teilen und Lieferketten zu diversifizieren.
Die Regierung will vor allem die industrielle KI vorantreiben - also die Anwendung in Unternehmen und Fabriken. KI werde die Arbeitswelt fundamental verändern und die Produktivität verbessern, sagte Merz. Es gebe zwar Risiken, mit denen dürfe man aber nicht ängstlich umgehen. "Wenn wir uns dieser Technologie verweigern, ist der Abstieg vorprogrammiert."
Er mahnte allerdings auch, dass die Entwicklung Künstlicher Intelligenz sich an menschlichen Werten orientieren müsse. Er sprach sich daher für eine Technologie-Politik aus, die "im Einklang mit unseren Werten und Sicherheitsinteressen" durchgesetzt werden müsse.
Taskforce legt Plan für "KI-Nation 2030" vor
Bei der zweitägigen Konferenz beraten Regierungsvertreter, Experten und Tech-Unternehmer aus verschiedenen Ländern über Chancen, Risiken und Auswirkungen von KI. Nach Erwartung der Bundesregierung werden die nächsten eineinhalb Jahre darüber entscheiden, ob Deutschland im internationalen KI-Wettbewerb den Anschluss hält.
Deshalb war im Sommer eine KI-Taskforce unter Leitung des Digitalministeriums vom Nationalen Sicherheitsrat der Bundesregierung eingesetzt worden. Ihr Papier gibt als Ziel aus, Deutschland bis 2030 zur "KI-Nation" zu machen, zahlreiche Zielvorgaben werden gemacht, damit Deutschland vorn mitspielen kann.
So sollen bis 2030 mindestens 80 Prozent der Großunternehmen und 55 Prozent der kleineren und mittleren Unternehmen KI einsetzen, die Zahl der KI-Start-ups soll sich verdreifachen, und der Anteil der Wirtschaftsleistung, der KI-basiert erwirtschaftet wird, soll mehr als zehn Prozent betragen.
"Das Zeitfenster, um Abstand zu verringern, schließt sich"
Doch laut den Experten drängt die Zeit: Deutschland drohe "trotz einer starken Ausgangsposition insbesondere in der Forschung" in eine Situation zu geraten, in der sich der Abstand zu den führenden KI-Standorten USA und China stetig vergrößere.
"Das Zeitfenster, um diesen Abstand zu verringern, schließt sich bald", heißt es im Abschlussbericht der KI-Taskforce, der beim Digitalgipfel vorgelegt wurde. Die nächsten zwölf bis achtzehn Monate seien für die Weichenstellung entscheidend.

"Das Zeitfenster, um diesen Abstand zu verringern, schließt sich bald", heißt es im Abschlussbericht der KI-Taskforce, der beim Digitalgipfel vorgelegt wurde. Die nächsten zwölf bis achtzehn Monate seien für die Weichenstellung entscheidend.

title: У російському Ярославлі палає НПЗ (відео)
content_c:
У російському Ярославлі палає НПЗ (відео)
У Ярославлі після повідомлень про атаку спалахнула пожежа на території нафтопереробного заводу.
У російському Ярославлі повідомляють про атаку на місцевий нафтопереробний завод та пожежу в промисловій зоні.
Про це пише Telegram-канал Exilenova+ із посиланням на місцевих жителів.
За їхніми повідомленнями, на території Ярославського НПЗ виникли три осередки займання. Канал також оприлюднив кадри пожежі.
Масштаби пошкоджень та інформація про можливих постраждалих наразі невідомі. Незалежного підтвердження ураження об’єкта немає.
За даними Exilenova+, повідомлення про атаки на російську нафтову інфраструктуру надходять п’яту ніч поспіль. Канал згадує Новокуйбишевський НПЗ у Самарській області 30 жовтня, НПЗ в Уфі 31 жовтня, завод у Кстово 1 листопада та лінійну виробничо-диспетчерську станцію «Самара» 2 листопада.
Нагадаємо, у ніч проти 22 жовтня на території Росії пролунала серія вибухів. Місцеві жителі повідомляли про атаки безпілотників одразу в кількох регіонах, зокрема в Московській області.
Раніше ми писали, що завдяки точним ударам по критично важливих і важкозамінних вузлах переробки російської нафти Україна вивела з ладу суттєву частину російських НПЗ, а західні санкції та величезна територія РФ унеможливлюють їх швидкий ремонт і захист.

title: «Я знаю, что он идиот»: генеральный директор Ryanair вновь высмеял Маска
content_c:
Генеральный директор Ryanair Майкл О'Лири в понедельник заявил, что не намерен мириться с технологическим магнатом Илоном Маском после длительной публичной ссоры, начавшейся в январе. Об этом пишет Politico.
Конфликт разгорелся после того, как бюджетная авиакомпания отказалась устанавливать спутниковые интернет-системы Starlink Маска на своих самолетах после более чем года переговоров. В Ryanair утверждали, что оснащение самолетов лоукостера системами Starlink не будет прибыльным для компании.
Маск не согласился с этим утверждением и заявил, что Ryanair «ошибается в своих расчетах» относительно рентабельности установки Starlink на самолетах.
Спор обострился, когда 15 января О'Лири назвал Маска «идиотом». В ответ на следующий день основатель SpaceX назвал его «полным идиотом» и призвал уволить.
В интервью в понедельник О'Лири заявил, что не имеет ни малейшего желания мириться с Маском.
«Я не имею ни малейшего намерения мириться с ним. Он считает меня идиотом, а я знаю, что идиот — это он», — сказал О'Лири в интервью Bloomberg.
Он добавил, что в начале этого года воспользовался случаем, запустив акцию, чтобы высмеять Маска. В рамках акции «Большая распродажа билетов для идиотов» предлагали 100 тысяч билетов по цене от 16,99 фунта стерлингов в одну сторону.
«Он обеспечил Ryanair бесплатную рекламу на сумму примерно 30–40 миллионов долларов, а количество наших бронирований росло в течение двух-трёх недель», — рассказал О'Лири Bloomberg.
«Если нам удастся снова его разозлить, тем лучше», — пошутил он.

title: Польща через масовану атаку РФ на Україну задіяла сили ППО – Оперативне командування
content_c:
Польща через масовані удари Росії по Україні задіяла сили та засоби протиповітряної оборони, повідомляє Оперативне командування Збройних сил Польщі.
"У відповідь на масовані удари Російської Федерації по об'єктах на території України, завдані з використанням різноманітних засобів повітряного нападу, було задіяно відповідні сили та засоби системи протиповітряної оборони Республіки Польща", – йдеться в повідомленні командування в соцмережі Х.
У командуванні зазначили, що заходи мають превентивний характер і спрямовані на захист повітряного простору Польщі, насамперед прикордонних районів.

title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured
content_c:
Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured
- Published
Warning: This article contains graphic details that some people may find distressing
South African police have arrested five people in connection with a brutal attack on a cattle farmer, who was assaulted and tortured in what has been described as a "senseless and barbaric" act.
Donovan Marx, 50, was attacked during a house robbery on his farm in Ventersdorp, a small town in South Africa's North West province, last Wednesday.
Marx was ambushed as he returned home, shot and stabbed and had his ears cut off in the horrific ordeal, police said.
All five of his alleged attackers were arrested over the weekend, a move welcomed by Marx's wife and family.
They added that the "legal process must [now] take its course".
The horrific attack has caused widespread outrage in a country which is used to high levels of violence.
Police last week explained how the attack on Mark happened.
A group of masked men armed with guns approached a worker at Mark's house as he was mowing the lawn, they said in a statement.
The attackers then demanded to know where Marx was before tying the worker's hands and feet with cable ties.
When Marx returned home, police said two of the suspects allegedly approached him and shot him in the upper body.
"They [then] dragged him inside the house, tied his hands and feet with cable ties, and allegedly stabbed him."
The suspects then ransacked the house and took three firearms from a safe before escaping with Marx's van.
The ordeal ended after the farm worker managed to free himself and call for assistance.
Marx was rushed to hospital, where he remains, but may need prosthetic ears after surgeons were unable to save his own, local news site IOL reported.
South Africa's Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp condemned the attack on Marx, adding there was no "place in our country for such senseless and barbaric acts".
The chair of parliament's police committee, Ian Cameron, praised police for the swift arrests and called for a "strong, properly investigated case" to follow.
The five suspects, aged between 26 and 56, will appear in local courts on Tuesday and face house robbery, attempted murder and illegal possession of firearms and ammunition charges.
Some right-wing groups have used such attacks on white farmers, who are often from the Afrikaner community, to say there is a genocide against white people in the country - a claim that has been widely discredited.
Although the claims have been dismissed by every political party in the country, including those representing Afrikaners, US President Donald Trump has repeated them and has offered white Afrikaners asylum in the US.
South Africa's latest crime statistics, covering the period between April and June 2026, do not specify how many attacks took place on farms and only recorded one robbery in a rural area.
However, police data show most victims of crime in South Africa, including on farms, are black.

title: Israel has ‘historic’ opportunity to change direction, says leader of Arab coalition
content_c:
The leader of Israel’s main Palestinian coalition, which holds the balance of power after Tuesday’s elections, has said the country is facing a historic opportunity to change direction.
Yousef Jabareen, the head of the Joint List, said he was ready to join forces with the “Change” bloc to oust Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition, and to wrest control of the Knesset.
Turnout among Arab Israelis (Palestinians with Israeli citizenship, 20% of the population) more than doubled to about 80%, transforming the political landscape. Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Gaza had no vote.
Jabareen said the first demand of the roughly 840,000 Palestinian Israeli voters was to get rid of the Netanyahu government, and in particular its most extreme members, Itamar Ben-Gvir, the national security minister, and Bezalel Smotrich, the finance minister.
“This has been an awful four years … in all areas of life: in terms of house demolition, criminal gangs within the Arab community without any [intervention] from the police; not allocating the needed resources for our municipalities, for our education, for our youth in general; racism in all areas of life – physical attacks against Arabs, the brutality of the police,” Jabareen told the Guardian in one of his first interviews since the election. “So this has been really a very dangerous period.”
He said the next few days would be critical. Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, is due to summon political leaders as early as Wednesday to canvass their recommendations on who should be given the first chance to form the next government, with no single grouping commanding a clear claim on power.
Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority, dropping from 68 to 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. The Change bloc of Zionist parties led by the retired general Gadi Eisenkot has 48 seats, leaving the Arab-Israeli parties as potential kingmakers with a record 19 seats. The Joint List has 11, while the more conservative, Islamist Ra’am has eight.
Eisenkot and his partners have pledged not to form a unity government with Netanyahu, but Eisenkot has also put conditions on any potential coalition with Arab parties: they have to recognise that Israel is a Jewish state, accept compulsory national service – either civil or military – and denounce Hamas as a terrorist organisation.
Ra’am and its leader, Mansour Abbas, have signalled it is ready to join an Eisenkot coalition. The Joint List has no intention of joining such a government, but Jabareen said the coalition was ready to keep it afloat from the outside with tactical voting in the Knesset.
“The conditions that [Eisenkot] speaks of are more relevant for parties who would be in the coalition. We are not planning to be in the coalition … for very clear reasons,” Jabareen said at his family home in the northern city of Umm al-Fahm. “As long as the occupation of our people in the West Bank continues, we cannot be part of a government.
“However, in order to use our political power to get rid of the extreme Netanyahu government, we said that we will consider the possibility of supporting from outside. This is an opportunity to change policies, to change attitudes, including towards the Arab community and towards the Palestinian people.
“This is really a historic moment and I hope that there will be partners within the opposition to go ahead with that. We are thinking that this could be the start of a change.”
Jabareen, 54, a former law professor and the leader of the socialist Hadash party, has yet to talk to Eisenkot since Tuesday’s elections, but he confirmed that informal discussions among opposition parties were under way.
Forming a new government was unlikely to be straightforward. The party leaders in the Change bloc have to agree on a candidate for prime minister. They would also have to accept partnership with Arab parties, either in coalition or from outside. The rightwing opposition leader, Avigdor Lieberman, is said to be the most resistant. Joint List officials said it was unclear whether partnership with Palestinians really crossed Lieberman’s red lines, or whether he was just holding out for a top cabinet position.
Even before a new government could be formed, Jabareen argued, the 67 opponents of Netanyahu in the new Knesset could use their clear majority to wrest control of legislative power. “That would start by changing the speaker of the Knesset,” he said, adding that the opposition could also take control of the committee that oversees the legislative agenda.
“That could be very crucially important … even before we reach conclusions on the issue of a coalition and a new government,” he said, adding that one of the priorities of the new Knesset should be to repeal laws passed by the outgoing majority that infringed the independence of Israel’s judiciary.
To allow an opposition coalition to oust Netanyahu and function as a minority government, Jabareen made clear it would also have to address deep-seated inequality in Israeli society.
“We have suffered from systemic discrimination for years, so if Eisenkot speaks of change, I believe that the change should come also for our community. We need to be treated equally,” he said. “We also ask for a political horizon. We would like to see the war stopped and the resumption of negotiation with the Palestinian leadership. We would like to see a start of a change.”
The Joint List leader said he was concerned over what Netanyahu might do to keep his grip on power. The prime minister has already made allegations, without evidence, that the Arab parties had used Qatari funds illegally in the election campaign, which Jabareen dismissed as a bid to “delegitimise the political power of the Arab community” and “a dangerous incitement”.
One of Jabareen’s concerns was that the Israeli leader would join Donald Trump in the resumption of war on Iran as a pretext for putting off political transition.
“This is really a critical period,” he said. “There should be a clear voice from the opposition to go against any attempt by him to initiate war … or dictate a new military agenda in Israel.”

“This is really a historic moment and I hope that there will be partners within the opposition to go ahead with that. We are thinking that this could be the start of a change.”
Jabareen, 54, a former law professor and the leader of the socialist Hadash party, has yet to talk to Eisenkot since Tuesday’s elections, but he confirmed that informal discussions among opposition parties were under way.
Forming a new government was unlikely to be straightforward. The party leaders in the Change bloc have to agree on a candidate for prime minister. They would also have to accept partnership with Arab parties, either in coalition or from outside. The rightwing opposition leader, Avigdor Lieberman, is said to be the most resistant. Joint List officials said it was unclear whether partnership with Palestinians really crossed Lieberman’s red lines, or whether he was just holding out for a top cabinet position.
Even before a new government could be formed, Jabareen argued, the 67 opponents of Netanyahu in the new Knesset could use their clear majority to wrest control of legislative power. “That would start by changing the speaker of the Knesset,” he said, adding that the opposition could also take control of the committee that oversees the legislative agenda.
“That could be very crucially important … even before we reach conclusions on the issue of a coalition and a new government,” he said, adding that one of the priorities of the new Knesset should be to repeal laws passed by the outgoing majority that infringed the independence of Israel’s judiciary.
To allow an opposition coalition to oust Netanyahu and function as a minority government, Jabareen made clear it would also have to address deep-seated inequality in Israeli society.
“We have suffered from systemic discrimination for years, so if Eisenkot speaks of change, I believe that the change should come also for our community. We need to be treated equally,” he said. “We also ask for a political horizon. We would like to see the war stopped and the resumption of negotiation with the Palestinian leadership. We would like to see a start of a change.”
The Joint List leader said he was concerned over what Netanyahu might do to keep his grip on power. The prime minister has already made allegations, without evidence, that the Arab parties had used Qatari funds illegally in the election campaign, which Jabareen dismissed as a bid to “delegitimise the political power of the Arab community” and “a dangerous incitement”.
One of Jabareen’s concerns was that the Israeli leader would join Donald Trump in the resumption of war on Iran as a pretext for putting off political transition.
“This is really a critical period,” he said. “There should be a clear voice from the opposition to go against any attempt by him to initiate war … or dictate a new military agenda in Israel.”

title: Will renewed conflict derail Ethiopia's economic growth?
content_c:
Will renewed conflict derail Ethiopia's economic growth?
November 2, 2026
Ethiopia's economy is growing strongly. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecasts real growth of 9.2% for the 2025–26 fiscal year. But renewed fighting in the north, high reconstruction costs and climate-related crop problems are threatening the country's economic recovery.
London-based financial analyst Abdulmenan Mohammed warns of the consequences of further escalation. "If there is a major conflict [...] the current economic growth will not be sustainable," he told DW.
The costly legacy of the Tigray war
The war that raged in Tigray and other parts of Ethiopia between 2020 and 2022 inflicted extensive damage. Infrastructure was destroyed, businesses lost production capacity and agricultural land could no longer be cultivated in some areas.
A World Bank-backed damage and needs assessment puts the damage caused by several conflicts in Ethiopia between November 2020 and December 2021 at more than $22.6 billion (€20.2 billion). Economic losses amounted to around $6 billion. The estimated bill for reconstruction and economic recovery stands at approximately $19.7 billion, which covers the total funding needed, not annual costs or damage caused by the current escalation.
A reconstruction plan covered the period from 2023 to 2028. However, it remains uncertain whether the work can be fully funded and completed within that timeframe.
Financial analyst Abdulmenan Mohammed believes the economic consequences of the Tigray war were even more severe. In addition to the direct destruction, he points to lost economic output, high inflation and foreign currency shortages at the time. International trade conditions also deteriorated: in 2022, Ethiopia lost its benefits under the US African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), which had allowed certain African exports to enter the US market duty-free.
Growth despite the crisis
Following the Pretoria peace agreement in November 2022, the economy began to recover. According to the IMF, it grew by 7.2% in 2022–23 and 8.1% in 2023–24. The organization puts growth at 9.2% for 2024–25 and forecasts a further 9.2% for 2025–26. Agriculture, mining and electricity generation are among the main drivers.
This does not contradict the economic damage caused by the war. Gross domestic product (GDP) measures the total economic output of a country. If major sectors outside conflict-affected areas continue to expand, the overall economy can grow even while individual regions are still suffering the consequences of violence.
However, high growth rates do not mean that the country's economic problems have been resolved. Reconstruction remains a major challenge, inflation continues to put pressure on households and the government has to service its debt. In late 2023, Ethiopia defaulted after missing an interest payment on a Eurobond. Reforms supported by an IMF program launched in 2024 are intended to address structural weaknesses in the economy.
More military spending, less money for development
A renewed escalation could put additional pressure on public finances. The government would have to spend more on military personnel, equipment and logistics. At the same time, economic activity and, consequently, tax revenues could decline in the affected regions.
"A substantial share of government resources would be tied up in military spending that would otherwise be available for infrastructure, education and social services," warned Abdulmenan Mohammed. The extent of this impact would depend on the scale and duration of any renewed conflict.
A prolonged war could also prompt businesses to postpone investments. International lenders and donors might become more cautious, while the government would need additional funds for security and humanitarian assistance. This could leave less money available for roads, energy infrastructure and other development projects.
Inflation and foreign currency shortages
The IMF forecasts an average inflation rate of 11.7% for 2025–26. Prices are therefore expected to continue rising, although at a slower pace than in previous years.
Abdulmenan Mohammed expects a further escalation to intensify inflationary pressures. "If the conflict escalates further, inflation is likely to rise," he said. To finance additional spending, the government might resort to more domestic borrowing. This could crowd out private businesses by making it harder for them to access credit and finance investments.
The military also needs foreign currency to purchase equipment from abroad. If this demand increases, fewer foreign exchange reserves could be available to private businesses for imports. This would put further pressure on the birr exchange rate and drive up the cost of imported goods, fuel and industrial inputs.
The extent of these effects on the BRICS member state would also depend on export earnings, monetary policy and developments in international markets. A new surge in inflation is therefore a risk, but not an inevitable consequence of the escalation. A combination of rising prices and uncertain incomes would be particularly difficult for poorer households.
Agriculture and tourism particularly vulnerable
Abdulmenan Mohammed sees agriculture, as well as the tourism and hospitality sectors, as particularly vulnerable. "Agriculture is especially exposed because much of the fighting takes place in rural areas where farmers work," he said.
Insecurity around farmland, disrupted transport routes and shortages of agricultural inputs can undermine production. At the same time, parts of the country are experiencing insufficient rainfall and poor harvest prospects. Failed harvests reduce farmers' incomes, while lower food supplies can push prices even higher.
Tourism is also highly sensitive to security risks. Travel advisories and reports of fighting can deter visitors, reducing revenues for hotels and tour operators.
Could neighboring countries benefit from the crisis?
When making investment decisions, international investors consider not only market size but also political stability, security and the reliability of state institutions. A further escalation could therefore delay investment decisions or prompt companies to consider alternative locations.
However, there is currently no concrete evidence that companies are already withdrawing investments from Ethiopia because of the fighting and relocating them to neighboring countries such as Kenya. Abdulmenan Mohammed also sees no demonstrable economic advantage for Kenya at this stage. Beyond security, factors such as tax administration, public services and governance also play a decisive role.
This article was originally published in German.

title: Steve Witkoff kündigt neue Gespräche mit Kyjiw und Moskau an
content_c:
Friedensverhandlungen für Ukraine Witkoff kündigt neue Gespräche mit Kyjiw und Moskau an
Im Ringen um ein Ende des russischen Angriffskriegs gegen die Ukraine sollen nach US-Angaben nächste Woche Vertreter aus Kyjiw, Moskau und Washington zu Verhandlungen zusammenkommen. Das trilaterale Treffen auf Arbeitsebene solle nächste Woche Dienstag und Mittwoch in Abu Dhabi, der Hauptstadt der Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate, stattfinden, teilte der US-Sondergesandte Steve Witkoff auf der Plattform X mit.
»Die Gespräche werden sich um Sicherheitsvereinbarungen für die Zeit nach dem Krieg, Deeskalation, humanitäre Hilfsmaßnahmen und die nächsten Schritte auf dem Weg zum Frieden drehen«, erklärte er.
The United States will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia on November 10–11 in Abu Dhabi, advancing President Trump’s mission to end the war. Discussions will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps…
— Special Envoy Steve Witkoff (@SEPeaceMissions) November 2, 2026
Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung.
Zudem sollen Witkoff zufolge US-Gesandte diese Woche mit Vertretern aus Deutschland, Frankreich, Großbritannien, der Nato sowie der EU zusammenkommen. Bei den Gesprächen in Brüssel soll es um die Themen Sicherheitsgarantien für die Ukraine, Europas Sicherheitsordnung nach dem Krieg sowie um den Wiederaufbau gehen.
Putin bereit für Verhandlungen
Kremlchef Wladimir Putin hatte sich vergangenen Monat nach einem Gespräch mit Witkoff über ein Ende des Ukrainekriegs verhandlungsbereit gezeigt. »Wir haben vereinbart, dass wir bereit sind, unsere dreiseitigen Kontakte wieder aufzunehmen«, sagte Putin mit Blick auf frühere Gespräche. In dem Dreierformat USA, Russland und Ukraine hatte es zuletzt im Februar in Genf Verhandlungen gegeben, davor zweimal in Abu Dhabi.
Andeutungen aus dem Kreml hatten jüngst bereits nahegelegt, dass sich die Delegationen der drei Länder Mitte November in Abu Dhabi zu einer Fortsetzung ihrer Gespräche treffen würden. Der russische Außenminister Sergej Lawrow hatte dabei jüngst die Haltung der Europäer kritisiert. »Sie versuchen, sich in den Friedensverhandlungsprozess in der Ukraine einzumischen«, sagte er vor ein paar Tagen.
Der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj hatte vergangene Woche dagegen die Hoffnung geäußert, dass bei den Gesprächen mit Russland und den USA auch die EU teilnehmen werde. »Wir finden hoffentlich einen Weg, Europa einzubeziehen«, sagte Selenskyj in Den Haag.
Die Ukraine wehrt sich seit mehr als viereinhalb Jahren mit westlicher Unterstützung gegen den Angreifer Russland.
Mehr zum Ukrainekonflikt: Erst Diesellieferungen, jetzt die Freilassung eines US-Bürgers aus russischer Haft – Kremlherrscher Putin hält sich US-Präsident Trump gewogen. Zu wirklichen Kompromissen im Krieg gegen die Ukraine ist er nicht bereit .
description: Die USA, Russland und die Ukraine haben zuletzt im Februar im Dreierformat miteinander gesprochen. Kommende Woche wollen sie wieder zusammenkommen. US-Vermittler Steve Witkoff hat konkrete Verhandlungsziele.

title: Afghanistans Kindern droht ein tödlicher Winter
content_c:
Hungernde Kinder in Afghanistan "Die kämpfen wirklich nur ums Überleben"
Die humanitäre Lage in Afghanistan gehört zu den größten Krisen weltweit. Besonders betroffen: Kinder. Nun schlagen Hilfsorganisationen wie UNICEF Alarm. Die Zahl der akut mangelernährten Mädchen und Jungen steige.
Es ist ein Bild, dass Shagufa Abdul, nicht vergessen wird: Im August besuchte die Mitarbeiterin der Hilfsorganisation Save the Children eine Klinik im Norden Afghanistans, die auch von der deutschen Bundesregierung unterstützt wird. Dort sah sie eine abgemagerte Mutter mit ihrem ebenfalls unterernährten Säugling. Vier Stunden lang sei die Mutter mit ihrem Kind im Arm, bei 45 Grad Hitze, unterwegs gewesen, um die Klinik der Hilfsorganisation zu erreichen, berichtet Abdul. Alternativen gab es für die Familie wohl nicht.
Solche Fälle sind für die in Stuttgart aufgewachsene humanitäre Helferin keine Ausnahme mehr. Seit diesem Jahr arbeitet sie für Save the Children in der afghanischen Hauptstadt Kabul. Fünf Jahre nach der erneuten Machtübernahme der Taliban hat fast ein Drittel der Bevölkerung keinen verlässlichen Zugang zu Nahrung. In den 70 Kliniken der Hilfsorganisation werde das ganze Ausmaß der Krise täglich sichtbar, berichtet Abdul. Millionen Mädchen und Jungen seien akut mangelernährt und können nicht genügend Nährstoffe aufnehmen.
Eine Million Kinder leidet an schwerer Mangelernährung
Abdul sagt, dass unter den Kindern wohl eine Million an schwerer Mangelernährung leiden: "Das sind kleine Kinder im Alter von sechs Monaten bis fünf Jahren, die eigentlich momentan spielen müssen, die sich entwickeln müssen, die sich gesund ernähren müssen und momentan kämpfen die wirklich nur ums Überleben", sagt die Helferin.
Vor allem zwei Entwicklungen treiben die Katastrophe unaufhaltsam voran: Zum einen wurden in den vergangenen Jahren Millionen Afghaninnen und Afghanen aus den Nachbarländern Iran und Pakistan zurückgedrängt. Zum anderen haben die internationalen Geberländer - darunter auch Deutschland - die Mittel stark gekürzt.
UN befürchten Hungersnot
Und so dürfte sich die Situation mit Beginn des Winters weiter verschlechtern. Die Zahl der Menschen, die nicht wissen, woher ihre nächste Mahlzeit kommt, werde voraussichtlich auf über 19 Millionen steigen, warnte Olga Cherevko vom UN-Büro für die Koordinierung humanitärer Angelegenheiten. Für fünf Millionen Menschen werde die Situation bis zum Frühjahr voraussichtlich zu einer katastrophalen Notlage - Afghanistan sei dann nur noch einen Schritt von einer Hungersnot entfernt, so die UN-Sprecherin.
"Wir müssen handeln, bevor der Winter kommt - nicht erst, wenn Familien bereits alle Möglichkeiten ausgeschöpft haben", sagt Cherevko. "Das bedeutet auch, Menschen in Not mit Nahrungsmittelhilfe zu versorgen, Viehbestände und produktive Vermögenswerte zu schützen, Landwirtinnen und Landwirte zu unterstützen, bevor entscheidende Aussaatzeitfenster verstreichen, und den Zugang zu grundlegenden Gesundheits-, Ernährungs- und Wasserversorgungsleistungen sicherzustellen."
Gelder reichen nicht aus
Doch die von der internationalen Gemeinschaft zur Verfügung gestellten Mittel reichen laut Cherevko nicht ansatzweise für die Krise aus. Die Situation sei besorgniserregend, sagt auch Shagufa Abdul. Wegen fehlender Finanzierung drohe allein Save the Children in diesem Jahr die Schließung von 40 Gesundheitseinrichtungen weltweit. Die Organisation ist seit 1976 in Afghanistan tätig, betreibt dort unter anderem Ernährungszentren und mobile Gesundheitsteams in Regionen Afghanistans, in denen es sonst keinerlei Hilfe gibt.
So gebe es mittlerweile auch Situationen, in denen mangelernährte, kleine Kinder in der Klinik von Save the Children keine Nahrung mehr bekommen könnten, weil der Hilfsorganisation das Geld gestrichen worden sei, sagt Abdul. Sie appelliert: "Wenn morgen dann so langsam auch der Arzt wegfällt oder die Klinik schließen muss, dann haben die Familien keine anderen Alternativen. Das bedeutet dann einfach, dass das Kind dann - man muss es hart sagen - stirbt."

Das bedeutet dann einfach, dass das Kind dann - man muss es hart sagen - stirbt."

title: Харків під комбінованим ударом: пошкоджений медзаклад, є постраждалі

Харків під комбінованим ударом: пошкоджений медзаклад, є постраждалі
У Немишлянському районі Харкова внаслідок удару по медичному закладу постраждали четверо людей.

title: Аэропорты Москвы: два закрыты, ещё два работают с ограничениями
content_c:
Все московские аэропорты ограничили работу. В начале сентября их уже закрывали после того, как президент Украины Владимир Зеленский предупредил авиакомпании об опасности полетов в российском воздушном пространстве. В настоящее время Внуково и Домодедово закрыты, а Шереметьево и Жуковский работают с ограничениями, сообщает Exilenova+.
В Росавиации сообщили о приостановке работы Домодедово и Жуковского. По их данным, Внуково принимает и отправляет рейсы «по согласованию с соответствующими органами», а Шереметьево по состоянию на 00:48 по московскому времени работало в штатном режиме. Ограничения ввели из соображений безопасности, добавили в ведомстве.
Обычно такие ограничения вводят из-за ударов БПЛА по регионам России. Однако мэр Москвы Сергей Собянин и руководство Подмосковья о налете беспилотников не сообщали.
Этой ночью режим «Ковер» ввели и в Самарской области, о чем сообщила Росавиация. Ранее в регионе объявили об угрозе атаки БПЛА.
В сентябре Зеленский предупредил авиакомпании и страховщиков, что российское небо становится опасным из-за дронов. Он также заявил, что Украина не представляет угрозы для гражданской авиации и не собирается атаковать пассажирские самолеты. По его словам, российские власти официально об этом не сообщают, но воздушное пространство над страной закрывается из-за войны.
Еще в августе бывший министр обороны Украины Михаил Федоров подтвердил, что Киев планировал операцию M&M’s с применением дронов на базе искусственного интеллекта против московских аэропортов. Он добавил, что этот замысел все еще могут реализовать.

title: Фінляндія не гратиме проти Росії, доки триває війна в Україні, і збирає "єдиний фронт" у IIHF
content_c:
Федерація хокею Фінляндії не гратиме проти збірної Росії, доки триває війна проти України, і намагається об'єднати інші національні федерації, щоб не допустити Росію до чемпіонатів світу, заявив голова федерації Гейккі Хієтанен.
"Наша позиція полягає в тому, що ми не гратимемо проти Росії, доки триває загарбницька війна проти України", – йдеться в повідомленні на сайті Фінської федерації хокею.
"Зараз ми працюємо над тим, щоб об'єднати якомога більше країн у єдиний фронт і заявити IIHF: за нинішніх обставин ніхто з нас не гратиме проти Росії. Це має значно більшу вагу, ніж якби ми висловлювали свою позицію поодинці", – зазначив Хієтанен.
Поштовхом стало рішення Спортивного арбітражного суду (CAS) від 30 жовтня. Протягом вихідних фінська федерація контактувала з іншими членами IIHF, ці консультації триватимуть і цього тижня. Правління федерації в понеділок вирішило залишити на столі всі можливі варіанти.
2 листопада розпочалося дводенне засідання Ради IIHF, головною темою якого стало питання Росії. Хієтанен представляє Фінляндію в раді.
Як повідомлялося, міністр закордонних справ України Андрій Сибіга розкритикував рішення CAS про допуск російських збірних до чемпіонатів світу IIHF, назвавши його "плямуванням льоду українською кров'ю".

title: Wizz Air flight from Luton in emergency landing after bomb threat
content_c:
Wizz Air flight from Luton in emergency landing after bomb threat
- Published
A Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia has been escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet to Budapest after a mid-air bomb threat.
The aircraft was forced to make an emergency landing at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International.
Authorities there "carried out the necessary security checks on the aircraft and passengers", a spokesperson for Wizz Air said.
The airline later confirmed an inspection had been "completed and nothing was found", adding that the plane would depart again shortly. Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendis confirmed his country provided the fighter jet to escort the flight.
According to flight tracking website FlightAware, Wizz Air flight 4302 departed Luton at 08:33 GMT and was due to arrive in the Bulgarian capital at 13:25 local time (11:25 GMT).
But the website said it landed in Budapest at 12:09 local time (11:09 GMT).
In a post on social media, Ruszin-Szendis said that after receiving the bomb threat, the Wizz Air flight had requested permission to land at the airport in Budapest.
"Within minutes, a Hungarian Defence Forces Gripen fighter jet took to the skies and provided an escort for the passenger aircraft", he said.
After this, the jet returned to its base and police took charge of the incident, he added.
The airline said that after the plane made the emergency landing, it taxied "to a designated stand" where the security checks were carried out.
Wizz Air added that it was "cooperating fully with the authorities", and that the safety of passengers and crew "remains our highest priority".

title: AI-powered malware ‘highly likely’ to be used to hack UK infrastructure by 2028
content_c:
AI-powered malicious software is “highly likely” to be used in hacking attacks against the UK’s power stations, airports and hospitals by 2028, according to the state cybersecurity body.
The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) said AI will probably enable a ransomware attack against critical national infrastructure [CNI] between now and 2028. The UK’s definition of CNI covers a range of facilities and services across sectors including energy, transport, defence, food, health and finance.
The warning from the NCSC, part of the GCHQ spy agency, was published in the organisation’s annual review, which also warned that Russia and China will start using AI “routinely” in cyber-attacks.
“It is … highly likely that between now and 2028, AI-powered malware will have been used in a ransomware attack on UK CNI,” said NCSC.
Ransomware has become a cornerstone of the criminal hacker’s repertoire and is a signature ploy of gangs that typically operate out of former Soviet Union states.
After gaining access to a victim’s IT systems, the attackers then encrypt files with bespoke malicious software – or malware – and then demand a payment in cryptocurrency to unlock the crippled systems and return any stolen data. UK ransomware victims include Royal Mail, outsourcing firm Capita and various public bodies, including councils.
AI is set to enhance the ransomware threat by helping attackers with tasks such as scouting targets, locating weaknesses in IT networks and writing malicious code, said the NCSC.
Last month, the government urged Britons to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in order to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, said as the Be Ready campaign was launched that Britain needed to prepare for the threat of “state-sponsored terrorism” by Russia or other hostile powers targeting everyday infrastructure.
NCSC’s chief executive, Richard Horne, will warn the public in a speech accompanying the review on Tuesday that AI is going to unleash a wave of cyber-attacks imminently.
“In the coming months, we face a real prospect of an unprecedented rise in the number of cyber incidents,” he will say.
Horne will attribute the threat to the technology’s ability to uncover weaknesses in IT systems that have been “tolerated for far too long”.
An example of AI’s capacity to root out previously undetected vulnerabilities came last month, when the technology helped discover a critical weakness in PHP, a computer language used by almost 70% of the world’s websites.
Alan Woodward, a professor of cybersecurity at Surrey University, said NCSC’s warning underlined the need for nation states and companies to access cutting-edge AI technology.
“AI can help people find these flaws and patch them, but if we don’t get the access the bad guys will beat them to it,” he said. So far, leading AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have given some companies advanced access to their most powerful models in order to help them identify serious IT glitches.
Horne will also say in his speech that communications networks used by the British military are subjected to daily attacks that are “persistent” and “sustained”.
Horne will say Russia was one of the perpetrators, but the attacks have deliberately not crossed the line into warfare, with Moscow carrying out “notable campaigns” that “intentionally fall below the threshold of armed conflict as they escalate their attempts at hybrid warfare”.
Horne will add that recent cyber-attacks on supermarket fridges in Europe, which have seen fridge temperatures raised by hackers to more than 50C, are a warning to companies and organisations to invest strongly in cyber resilience.
“For decades we have collectively got away with tech on the cheap,” he will say.

title: For US Democrats, climate policy is now about energy bills
content_c:
For US Democrats, climate policy is now about energy bills
November 2, 2026
President Donald Trump's administration has gutted US climate policy. Yet, even as wildfires, record heat waves and flooding hit communities across the country, Democrats are keeping quiet about global warming on the midterm campaign trail.
Instead, candidates are packaging climate policy as an affordability issue, stressing how Americans are struggling to afford gas, groceries and to insure their homes against climate-fueled weather extremes.
Take James Talarico, who represents the Democratic Party's best chance at winning a senate race in the Republican stronghold of Texas in nearly 40 years. Though he makes some mention of climate change on his campaign's "energy and environment" page, that is not his focus.
His pledges center on lowering energy costs, providing emergency relief for spiking utility bills, making data centers pay for their own grid upgrades and growing energy sector jobs.
This aligns with analysis from nonprofit news organization Inside Climate News showing that the Democrats have dramatically reduced mentions of climate change in their press releases and campaign messaging.
"We've entered an interesting space where climate policy doesn't need to be called climate policy to be climate policy," Max Frankel, executive director of the SEEC Institute, a nonprofit that helps guide climate policy in Congress, told DW.
What would a Democratic win mean for climate policy?
Most forecasts project Democrats winning the House and a narrow majority in the Senate in the November 3 election. But without control of the White House, passing any legislation will be difficult and almost any climate policy will have to be a bipartisan endeavor, say analysts.
Given that and the Democrats' messaging-shift to affordability over climate, few experts expect a fully resurrected Inflation Reduction Act. Introduced under the Democrats to create incentives for building clean energy projects, the legislation was largely decimated by President Trump's major tax law.
But Democrats may try to bring back some climate-friendly IRA provisions, particularly measures aimed at lowering household energy costs, analysts told DW. Those include incentives for home energy-efficiency upgrades and appliances like heat pumps to replace oil and gas heaters that typically help bring down household energy bills.
Politicians could also expand an IRA manufacturing tax credit for solar, batteries, and critical minerals that largely survived. One bipartisan bill proposes extending it to include nuclear fusion components.
"It's not going to be anything at the scale of the IRA," Adrian Deveny, founder of Climate Vision, a policy firm dedicated to decarbonization, told DW. "It's like singles and doubles as opposed to a home run, which is still worth doing."
A first bipartisan test over building infrastructure
In a rare area of agreement between the parties, some Democrats and Republicans are already backing a reform bill they're hoping to pass before a new Congress is sworn in January.
If enacted, the bill could make it significantly easier to build major infrastructure projects in the US, including long-distance transmission lines that carry electricity between regions but that currently take years to build because of complex permitting rules.
"The biggest beneficiary of building more transmission will be wind and solar power, because the best and cheapest way to generate wind and solar energy tends to be far away from cities," said David Spence, a political scientist at the University of Texas who researches the politics of energy regulation. "And so, they need transmission to get their product to market."
But environmental groups say the bill could also speed up the approval of fossil fuel projects.
If Democrats win big in the midterms there might be some "peeling off their support for that bill because they think they can do better in the next Congress," said Spence.
Looking to the 2028 presidential elections
Major new federal climate legislation is a long shot before the 2028 presidential election. And afterwards it would likely require Democrats winning the White House, the Senate and the House. While no 2028 platforms have been released yet, policy experts expect a few ideas to feature prominently.
One is data centers. Opposition to the energy-guzzling infrastructure being built en masse to power the AI boom is mounting across the country. Half of Americans are now against data centers being built close to their homes, according to a pollfrom news outlet Politico.
"I'm sure every candidate is going to have a platform with a focus on data center constraints on some level, as a way to address affordability," Deveny, who led negotiations on the IRA, said. "And that's the entry point for climate policy."
There are several ideas currently circulating — including a proposal by Democrats Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to pause data center construction — as well as ending tax breaks for data centers and imposing new taxes on their electricity use.
Democrats may also seek to restore the IRA's clean energy tax incentives. This year, more than 150 legislators co-sponsored the so-called Energy Bills Relief Act designed to reinstate IRA clean energy tax incentives, reform how transmission permits are granted, and make data centers pay for the grid upgrades they need. The bill is unlikely to pass anytime soon but offers a window into what Democrats might support.
"By far, the biggest consensus — to the extent there's anything remotely resembling a consensus — is restoring a lot of the clean energy tax incentives from the IRA," Deveny said. "Not everybody supports that but it is a highly supported idea amongst most congressional Democrats."
Support for other proposals include a new federal program to help insurers cover climate-driven disasters and bring down hefty premiums, as well as so-called climate superfunds. This would require fossil fuel companies to contribute to the costs of damage caused by extreme weather and adapting to the risks of climate change.
Vermont and New York both passed legislation to create funds, although a federal judge blocked New York's.
The 2028 presidential race is expected to begin a few weeks after the midterms end, bringing a fresh round of policy ideas and debates. A new president typically gets to drive the legislative agenda in the beginning of their term if their party also wins Congress.
"As long as the consensus is that clean energy is the cheaper source of energy, and it's going to provide stability over the long term for high energy costs — there's a million ways you can propose solutions through that lens," Deveny said.
description: Climate change has all but disappeared from Democrats' campaign pitches, replaced by promises to lower electricity bills. So what would the party really do for climate policy should it win control of Congress?
content:
For US Democrats, climate policy is now about energy bills
November 2, 2026
President Donald Trump's administration has gutted US climate policy. Yet, even as wildfires, record heat waves and flooding hit communities across the country, Democrats are keeping quiet about global warming on the midterm campaign trail.
Instead, candidates are packaging climate policy as an affordability issue, stressing how Americans are struggling to afford gas, groceries and to insure their homes against climate-fueled weather extremes.
Take James Talarico, who represents the Democratic Party's best chance at winning a senate race in the Republican stronghold of Texas in nearly 40 years. Though he makes some mention of climate change on his campaign's "energy and environment" page, that is not his focus.
His pledges center on lowering energy costs, providing emergency relief for spiking utility bills, making data centers pay for their own grid upgrades and growing energy sector jobs.
This aligns with analysis from nonprofit news organization Inside Climate News showing that the Democrats have dramatically reduced mentions of climate change in their press releases and campaign messaging.
"We've entered an interesting space where climate policy doesn't need to be called climate policy to be climate policy," Max Frankel, executive director of the SEEC Institute, a nonprofit that helps guide climate policy in Congress, told DW.
What would a Democratic win mean for climate policy?
Most forecasts project Democrats winning the House and a narrow majority in the Senate in the November 3 election. But without control of the White House, passing any legislation will be difficult and almost any climate policy will have to be a bipartisan endeavor, say analysts.
Given that and the Democrats' messaging-shift to affordability over climate, few experts expect a fully resurrected Inflation Reduction Act. Introduced under the Democrats to create incentives for building clean energy projects, the legislation was largely decimated by President Trump's major tax law.
But Democrats may try to bring back some climate-friendly IRA provisions, particularly measures aimed at lowering household energy costs, analysts told DW. Those include incentives for home energy-efficiency upgrades and appliances like heat pumps to replace oil and gas heaters that typically help bring down household energy bills.
Politicians could also expand an IRA manufacturing tax credit for solar, batteries, and critical minerals that largely survived. One bipartisan bill proposes extending it to include nuclear fusion components.
"It's not going to be anything at the scale of the IRA," Adrian Deveny, founder of Climate Vision, a policy firm dedicated to decarbonization, told DW. "It's like singles and doubles as opposed to a home run, which is still worth doing."
A first bipartisan test over building infrastructure
In a rare area of agreement between the parties, some Democrats and Republicans are already backing a reform bill they're hoping to pass before a new Congress is sworn in January.
If enacted, the bill could make it significantly easier to build major infrastructure projects in the US, including long-distance transmission lines that carry electricity between regions but that currently take years to build because of complex permitting rules.
"The biggest beneficiary of building more transmission will be wind and solar power, because the best and cheapest way to generate wind and solar energy tends to be far away from cities," said David Spence, a political scientist at the University of Texas who researches the politics of energy regulation. title: Midterms: Donald Trump scheitert im Kalifornien-Streit vor Supreme Court
content_c:
US-Midterms Trump scheitert im Streit über Wählerstimmen in Kalifornien vor Supreme Court
Die US-Regierung von Präsident Donald Trump ist einen Tag vor den Parlamentswahlen wegen angeblich falsch ausgegebener Stimmzettel in Kalifornien vor den Obersten Gerichtshof gezogen. Wenige Stunden später lag die Entscheidung vor – eine Niederlage für Trump.
Die Regierung wirft dem demokratisch regierten Bundesstaat Kalifornien vor, Stimmzettel an mutmaßliche Nichtstaatsangehörige ausgegeben zu haben. Bei Bundeswahlen dürfen nur US-Staatsbürgerinnen und Staatsbürger abstimmen.
Noch während des laufenden Berufungsverfahrens wollte die Regierung vor dem Supreme Court mit einem Eilantrag erwirken, dass Kalifornien Wahlzettel von rund 20.000 angeblichen Ausländern gesondert aufbewahrt, bis deren Identität geklärt ist. Das lehnte das Gericht in Washington nun ab. Zuvor war die Regierung schon in niedrigeren Instanzen gescheitert.
Am Dienstag wird in den USA über alle Sitze des Repräsentantenhauses sowie über rund ein Drittel der Sitze des Senats abgestimmt. In Kalifornien an der Westküste schneiden bei Wahlen traditionell die Demokraten stark ab.
Die Trump-Regierung schürt immer wieder Zweifel daran, dass US-Wahlen rechtmäßig ablaufen. Trump behauptet immer wieder, er habe die Präsidentschaftswahl 2020 gegen den Demokraten Joe Biden gewonnen. Das ist mehrfach widerlegt.
Trump sagte jüngst, die Wahlen in Kalifornien seien korrupt, ohne Belege vorzuweisen. Seiner Meinung nach gebe es Millionen ungültige Stimmen – auch hierfür legte Trump keinen Beweis vor. Der Präsident liefert sich schon lange eine Fehde mit dem demokratischen Gouverneur Kaliforniens, Gavin Newsom. Er gilt als möglicher Präsidentschaftskandidat der Demokraten für die Wahl 2028.
Die Midterms kurz vor der Mitte der vierjährigen Amtszeit des US-Präsidenten gelten traditionell als Referendum über dessen Politik. Historisch gesehen verliert die Regierungspartei bei den Zwischenwahlen fast immer Mandate im Kongress. Trump sagte bei seiner letzten Wahlkampfrede vor den Midterms: »Aus irgendeinem Grund gewinnt der amtierende Präsident die Midterms nicht.« Das gelte üblicherweise, egal wer Präsident sei – »Republikaner oder Demokrat, gut oder schlecht«. Zugleich bekräftigte Trump, dass seine Republikaner »alles« im Wahlkampf gegeben hätten. Die Midterms nannte er »die wichtigsten Zwischenwahlen unserer Lebenszeit«.
Sollten die Republikaner ihre knappen Mehrheiten in einer oder beiden Parlamentskammern verlieren, stellt sich die Frage, ob Trump diese Niederlage einräumt. Vergangene Woche sagte er, dass er das Ergebnis anerkennen würde, sofern die Wahlen »ehrlich« durchgeführt würden. Mehr dazu, was passiert, wenn Trump eine Niederlage nicht anerkennt, erfahren Sie hier .

title: Merz verurteilt Krawalle am Rande der Jugendproteste
content_c:
Merz zu Krawallen am Wochenende "Gewalt hat auf unseren Straßen nichts zu suchen"
Nach den Krawallen am Rande der Jugendproteste diskutiert die Politik über die Folgen - und darüber, von wem die Gewalt ausging. Kanzler Merz betont, man werde hart vorgehen. Zugleich zeigt er Verständnis für Forderungen von Demonstranten.
Mit Blick auf die Krawalle am Wochenende spricht sich Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz für ein hartes Vorgehen gegen die Gewalttäter aus. Gleichzeitig zeigt er Verständnis für einige Anliegen der jungen Demonstranten.
"Gewalt hat auf unseren Straßen nichts zu suchen, und meine Regierung wird hier keine Toleranz zeigen", heißt es im Redemanuskript des CDU-Vorsitzenden für die CDU-Kreisvorsitzendenkonferenz, die nichtöffentlich ist. Das Papier liegt den Nachrichtenagenturen dpa und Reuters in Auszügen vor.
Darin betont der Kanzler: "Wer Polizisten und Einsatzkräfte angreift und Geschäfte plündert, greift unsere Freiheit an, verhöhnt die Gesellschaft und die berechtigten Interessen der jungen Leute." Die Straftäter würden die Härte des Gesetzes spüren. Merz dankte ausdrücklich der Polizei, diese habe vorbildlich reagiert.
"Wollen den jungen Leuten gute Zukunft ermöglichen"
Er betonte aber auch, dass der Großteil der jungen Leute friedlich demonstriert habe. Als positive Botschaft vom Wochenende nehme er mit: "Die junge Generation ist politisch und sie sorgt sich um ihre Zukunft." Gerade beim Thema Wohnen gebe es Defizite und die Haushalte müssten entlastet werden, damit die Länder mehr in Bildung investieren könnten. "All die Themen stehen ganz oben auf unserer Arbeitsliste." Die zuständige Bildungsministerin Karin Prien (CDU) werde das Gespräch mit der jungen Generation jetzt weiterführen und vertiefen.
Die Proteste verliefen weitgehend friedlich - doch gegen Abend gab es in mehreren Städten Ausschreitungen.
"Wir wollen den jungen Leuten eine gute Zukunft ermöglichen, wir wollen ihnen ein ordentlich geführtes Land übergeben", so Merz. "Wir können der jungen Generation nicht die Lasten aufbürden, die eine alternde Gesellschaft nun einmal mit sich bringt." Die Regierung arbeite genau deshalb an Reformen."
Auch Regierungssprecher Stefan Kornelius betonte, Gewaltexzesse hätten "in unserem Land nichts verloren". Zugleich nehme der Kanzler die Forderungen der jungen Leute sehr ernst und halte sie für "legitime Anliegen".
Debatte um Dobrindt-Äußerung
Der Regierungssprecher und auch die Sprecherin des Bundesinnenministeriums verteidigten die Aussage von Innenminister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU), der nach den Ausschreitungen von "gewaltbereiten linken Gruppen und Chaoten aus dem migrantischen Milieu" gesprochen hatte. Merz teile Dobrindts Analyse, so Kornelius. Der Innenminister habe "die Lage umfassend dargestellt" und Merz schließe sich dem an.
Mit konkreten Daten kann die Bundesregierung die Aussagen jedoch noch nicht untermauern. Es gebe bisher "keine validen bundesweiten Zahlen" zu den Vorfällen, sagte die Sprecherin des Bundesinnenministeriums. Allerdings lägen dem Ministerium "Beobachtungen der Polizisten" vor Ort und teilweise auch von Verfassungsschutzbehörden vor. Kornelius verwies überdies auf Bildmaterial von den Ereignissen am Wochenende.
Prien: "Müssen auch auf die Ursachen schauen"
Auch Bildungsministerin Prien stellte sich hinter Dobrindt. Nach Abschluss der "weitestgehend friedlichen Demonstrationen" habe es Gewaltexzesse linksradikaler Gruppen gegeben, "aber eben auch von anderen, die wohl auch aus migrantischen Milieus stammen", sagte die CDU-Politikerin im Deutschlandfunk. "Hier geht es ja nicht darum, Ressentiments zu schüren, das wäre auch politisch falsch."
Es gehe vielmehr darum, die Realität zu betrachten und auch einen Eindruck davon zu bekommen, warum Menschen zu solchen Mitteln greifen. "Und wenn die aus migrantischen Milieus stammen, dann muss uns das Sorgen bereiten und dann müssen wir da auch auf die Ursachen schauen." Eine Frage sei, warum Integration in manchen Gruppen weniger gelinge als in anderen.
Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius ging hingegen auf Distanz zur Lesart der Unionspolitiker und verwies darauf, dass sich die Debatte um unklare Begriffe drehe. "Was sind denn migrantische Gruppen? Sind das Menschen, die in dritter Generation in Deutschland leben und deutsche Staatsangehörige sind? Wo hören wir auf, das zu differenzieren?“, fragte der SPD-Politiker im ZDF. Er glaube, das führe in die falsche Richtung.
Ähnlich äußerte sich die Integrationsbeauftragte der Bundesregierung Natalie Pawlik, ebenfalls von der SPD. "Täter sind zunächst Täter. Solche Gewaltausschreitungen immer gleich migrantischen Milieus zuzuschreiben, ist zu einfach“, sagte sie der Frankfurter Allgemeinen Zeitung.
Am Wochenende hatten Zehntausende junge Menschen zumeist friedlich demonstriert. Anschließend kam es aber zu teils schweren Krawallen. In Frankfurt am Main flogen Steine und Brandflaschen, Randalierer zerstörten Schaufenster, es gab Plünderungen. Auch in Köln, Hamburg und Berlin gab es nach überwiegend friedlichen Demonstrationen Ausschreitungen und Zusammenstöße mit der Polizei.

title: Путін панікує перед виборами у США: конгресмен пояснив причину
content_c:
Путін панікує перед виборами у США: конгресмен пояснив причину
На думку американського законодавця, Кремль прагне домогтися поступок від України до можливої зміни більшості в Конгресі США.
Російський диктатор Володимир Путін поспішає досягти вигідної Москві домовленості щодо України, оскільки проміжні вибори у США можуть обмежити можливості Дональда Трампа впливати на політику підтримки Києва.
Таку оцінку висловив конгресмен-демократ від Каліфорнії, член Комітету Палати представників зі збройних сил Джордж Вайтсайдс в авторській колонці для The Hill.
За його прогнозом, республіканці можуть втратити контроль над Палатою представників за результатами голосування 3 листопада. Вайтсайдс вважає, що це посилить можливості Конгресу протидіяти тиску на Україну після початку роботи нового складу в січні.
Саме цим автор пояснює спроби Вашингтона й Москви прискорити домовленості та схилити Київ до поступок.
Окрему увагу конгресмен приділив українським ударам по російських нафтопереробних заводах. На його думку, ця кампанія створює серйозні проблеми для Кремля, а прагнення припинити атаки свідчить про їхню ефективність.

title: Сегодня в Украине отмечают День инженерных войск
content_c:
Ежегодно 3 ноября отмечается День инженерных войск Украины. Во время войны именно эти войска занимаются инженерным обеспечением. Также они организуют инженерную разведку, расчищают дороги от завалов, строят переправы и безопасные проходы через минные поля, обустраивают территорию для дальнейшего наступления.
История праздника
Этот праздник был учрежден в Украине в 1999 году указом президента Леонида Кучмы. Его ввели «с учетом заслуг инженерных войск в укреплении обороноспособности государства».
Во время войны, начатой Россией, инженерные войска одними из первых вступают в бой: прокладывают безопасные проходы в минных полях для продвижения пехоты и техники, обезвреживают взрывные устройства, расчищают дороги от заграждений и завалов, наводят необходимые переправы через водные преграды.
Они также проводят инженерную разведку, фортификационное оборудование районов дислокации войск, маскировку войск (сил) и объектов.
Украинские земли загрязняются взрывоопасными предметами. Дошло до того, что с использованием обычных технологий для их гуманитарного разминирования потребуется более 700 лет. Однако новые технологии позволяют не только уничтожать компоненты ядерной триады агрессора, но и успешно и значительно быстрее разминировать украинский чернозем. Об этом в статье «БПЛА: разминирование украинских земель всего за 10–15 лет» рассказала аналитик систем в ГС «Цифровое развитие Украины» Екатерина Тарасова на ZN.UA.

title: Генштаб зафіксував 19 боїв на Костянтинівському напрямку від початку доби
content_c:
Від початку доби 2 листопада на фронті відбулося 191 бойове зіткнення, повідомляє Генштаб ЗСУ.
"Противник завдав 44 авіаційних ударів, скинув 146 керованих авіабомб. Крім того, залучив для ураження 4304 дрони-камікадзе та здійснив 1946 обстрілів населених пунктів і позицій наших військ", – йдеться в повідомленні.
Упродовж доби на північно-слобожанському та курському напрямках зафіксували вісім бойових зіткнень, на південно-слобожанському – 10, на куп'янському – 3, на лиманському – 6, на слов'янському – 1, на костянтинівському – 19, на покровському – 12, на гуляйпільському – 7, на оріхівському – 1.

title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
content_c:
Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
- Published
Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff and confirmed airfares will be "materially higher" next summer because of a sharp rise in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran.
The airline said it expects fuel prices to remain high "well into 2027" unless there is a "swift resolution" to the conflict.
Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be €2bn (£1.6bn) higher in the short-term and its boss, Michael O'Leary, said airfares would have to rise by "double-digits" to help cover the cost.
But the firm said that was unlikely to be enough and it is looking into pay freezes. Unite, the union representing Ryanair staff, said it had not been told of "any such proposals".
O'Leary also said the company would slow down hiring as airline's costs rise.
The airline said its pre-tax profits fell by 16% to €2.4bn during the six months to the end of September, largely due to fuel costs jumping by 15%.
The company said that although 80% of its fuel bill had been "hedged" – in effect, bought in advance at fixed prices – the cost of the remainder was elevated.
O'Leary reiterated forecasts from earlier this year Ryanair would "need a 20% fare increase" to cover the cost of jet fuel.
"I'm not sure we'll get to 20%," he said. "But we're certainly looking at double-digit fare increases across Europe from all airlines in 2027."
Aviation fuel prices have surged this year as a result of the US-Israel war with Iran, which has dramatically reduced the supply of refined products coming from the Gulf and increased competition for those produced elsewhere.
Ryanair also said it was weighing up whether to freeze pay, as multi-year wage deals with unions come to to an end. The policy could be implemented from April next year.
Oliver Richardson, national officer at Unite, said the union "hasn't been advised of any such proposals and we have a multi-year pay deal in place which covers next year. A number of Unions across Europe have the same".
He said: "Our pay agreement was not attached to, nor dependent on company performance. This was something that the Ryanair was at pains to emphasise. As such we would expect it to be honoured."
Ryanair also said it would increase its use of artificial intelligence within its back office and support functions.
Meanwhile, Ryanair has cut back on winter flights and said on Monday there would be more to come. It said this was happening across the airline industry, particularly with short-haul carriers.
O'Leary said: "We believe those cuts will continue into the summer of 2027. Over the medium term, we expect short-haul capacity will remain constrained out to the early 2030s."
  - Published11 September
  - Published21 July

title: PM to ask countries affected by UK’s role in slavery to help shape formal apology
content_c:
Andy Burnham will ask countries affected by Britain’s role in slavery to help shape an expected formal apology, Downing Street has indicated, arguing that their input is indispensable in crafting an enduring message.
The prime minister was en route to the Commonwealth heads of government summit (Chogm) in Antigua and Barbuda, which begins on Tuesday. No 10 said he would use the event to launch a “structured dialogue” into what form an apology might take.
UK officials already at the summit said other Commonwealth countries had responded positively to the move, and that it could help talks on separate issues such as trade and the climate.
In comments released by No 10 before Burnham’s arrival, the prime minister said discussion of an apology marked a new approach towards the UK’s relations with the Commonwealth.
Downing Street has ruled out the idea of paying reparations after an apology, but Burnham is expected to set out plans at the summit for a system of debt restructuring for countries facing higher debt costs.
“In today’s more divided, unpredictable world, the Commonwealth has the potential to be a powerful force for good, bringing together a third of the global population, and I believe it is key that the UK plays its full role in that,” Burnham said.
 
 
 “Britain is bringing a new approach to this meeting as we look to reshape a new era for the Commonwealth, as well as being open to discussions about the past.”
Burnham set out his intention to look at a possible apology in an article for the Guardian on Saturday, in which he said the UK should “show leadership again today” as it had done in efforts to end the transatlantic slave trade.
Asked why Burnham believed an apology was needed, his official spokesperson said: “The prime minister wants to strengthen the Commonwealth as a family of nations with shared values that can support growth around the world through trade and economic collaboration.” Having conversations about an apology would do this, and was also the right thing to do, he said.
Tony Blair expressed “deep sorrow” about the slave trade and Britain’s role in it in 2006, but stopped short of a formal apology.
Burnham intended to go further, his spokesperson said. “The prime minister, like his predecessors, has expressed his sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering caused by the transatlantic slave trade, and recognised the way it still shapes our world today.
“That is distinct from a formal apology. We are opening a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade, and listening to calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British state, and that will form an important part of that process.
“We think it’s right that a formal apology is discussed properly with the countries and communities most affected, rather than simply deciding unilaterally what form it should take. An apology of this significance should be informed by the people and countries most affected, as they have asked for.”
Burnham is scheduled to take part in a series of assemblies at Chogm, as well as bilateral meetings with other leaders.
There was no single event set aside to discuss slavery or an apology, but discussions would take place “throughout the next couple of days”, No 10 said, adding that the Foreign Office would lead talks over the form of an apology.
The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, is already at the summit. One Foreign Office official said other Commonwealth countries “are responding positively to our offer of a structured dialogue” on an apology.
“The conversations at Chogm have been focused on the positive work this alliance can do together on issues like climate and trade,” they said. “By not shying away from difficult discussions about our past, we are building trust with our allies to focus on the big issues of the future.”
No 10 denied that Burnham’s comments had potentially embarrassed King Charles, who is already in Antigua and Barbuda for a pre-Chogm visit.
Buckingham Palace “was made aware in a timely manner”, Burnham’s spokesperson said. “The prime minister believes that being true to British values of decency and honesty means not shying away from these conversations.”

title: US: 9 killed in Florida jet crash
content_c:
US: 9 killed in Florida jet crash
November 2, 2026
A private jet crashed in a residential area of Cresthaven in the US state of Florida's Palm Beach County on Sunday, killing all nine people on board.
The Learjet 60 business jet nose-dived into the south Florida neighborhood and exploded.
Videos circulating on social media, recorded by people from their vehicles, shows the plane making a loud whooshing sound as it rapidly descends to hit the side of a road and erupts into a large fireball.
The plane's descent in the footage resembled — as Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described — "a missile going down."
A thick plume of black and gray smoke is seen rising against houses, which were narrowly missed.
The crash left a crater on the road, with flames flickering around it.
What do we know about the Florida plane crash?
The plane had departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.
It was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 10,660 meters) when the pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation. They requested to climb another 2,000 feet (about 610 meters).
Just moments after, the jet dived steeply, at 10,000 feet per minute initially and then at 20,000 feet per minute to reach up to 30,000 feet per minute — a speed exceeding the plane's design limits — as per air traffic control recording and flight tracking data.
Last words from the cockpit — 'We are out of time'
LiveATC, which provides live air traffic control broadcasts, captured the harrowing final moments of the crash in an audio recording from a Miami air traffic control center.
A person from the plane's cockpit is heard saying "Mayday, mayday, we are descending 10,000 feet per minute."
The person declares an "emergency" just seconds later, urgently reporting a descent of 20,000 feet per minute.
"We're going to crash into the ground" the voice from the cockpit says and then goes on to report that the descent was at 22,000 feet and the plane was banking 60 degrees.
A scream is heard before the final words from the cockpit — "We are out of time."
Investigation underway
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that the crash occurred at 12.50 pm local time and described the incident as a "horrific tragedy."
The cause of the crash and the identities of those on board the plane were not immediately known.
The National Transportation Safety Board has launched a probe into the incident.
There are no immediate reports of anyone on the ground being injured or killed.
Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at a press briefing that some 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters.

US: 9 killed in Florida jet crash
November 2, 2026
A private jet crashed in a residential area of Cresthaven in the US state of Florida's Palm Beach County on Sunday, killing all nine people on board.
The Learjet 60 business jet nose-dived into the south Florida neighborhood and exploded.
Videos circulating on social media, recorded by people from their vehicles, shows the plane making a loud whooshing sound as it rapidly descends to hit the side of a road and erupts into a large fireball.
The plane's descent in the footage resembled — as Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described — "a missile going down."
A thick plume of black and gray smoke is seen rising against houses, which were narrowly missed.
The crash left a crater on the road, with flames flickering around it.
What do we know about the Florida plane crash?
The plane had departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.
It was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 10,660 meters) when the pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation. They requested to climb another 2,000 feet (about 610 meters).

title: Apple: iPhone-Geschäft treibt Umsatz auf Rekordniveau
content_c:
Quartalsbericht vorgestellt Apple meldet dank iPhone-Geschäft neue Rekordzahlen
Apple hat im vergangenen Quartal sowohl beim iPhone-Umsatz als auch bei den Konzernerlösen Rekordwerte erreicht: Das sagte der neue Konzernchef John Ternus am Montag. Daher übertreffe auch die Bilanz für das Geschäftsjahr 2025/2026 alles bisher Dagewesene.
Mit dem Ausblick für das laufende Quartal enttäuschte der US-Konzern jedoch: Apple-Aktien gaben daher im nachbörslichen Handel an der Wall Street rund vier Prozent nach.
Behalten Sie den Überblick: Jeden Werktag gegen 18 Uhr beantworten SPIEGEL-Autorinnen und -Autoren die wichtigsten Fragen des Tages im Newsletter »Die Lage am Abend« – hintergründig, kompakt, kostenlos. Hier bestellen Sie Ihr News-Briefing als Mail.
In den vergangenen Monaten lief es für das Unternehmen jedoch rund:
- Der Apple-Quartalsumsatz stieg den Angaben zufolge im Jahresvergleich überraschend deutlich um zwölf Prozent auf 114,5 Milliarden Dollar.
- Der Smartphone-Umsatz des Konzerns wuchs im Jahresvergleich um 17,5 Prozent auf 57,56 Milliarden Dollar. Analysten hatten im Schnitt mit rund einer Milliarde Dollar weniger gerechnet. Das iPhone ist das mit Abstand wichtigste Produkt des Konzerns.
- Die Einnahmen aus dem Verkauf von MacBook-Rechnern hätten mit 10,79 Milliarden Dollar die Markterwartungen ebenfalls um rund eine Milliarde Dollar übertroffen.
- Die Servicesparte, zu der neben dem App Store auch der Streamingdienst Apple TV+ gehört, erwirtschaftete einen Rekorderlös von 31,57 Milliarden Dollar.

title: Massive Cyberattacke auf Linken-Abgeordnete in Berlin
content_c:
Mail-Postfächer geflutet Massive Cyberattacke auf Linken-Abgeordnete
Tausende Nachrichten binnen Minuten: Ein massiver Cyberagriff hat die Mail-Postfächer der Linken im Bundestag lahmgelegt. Wer hinter der Attacke steckt, ist noch unklar. Andere Fraktionen waren nicht betroffen.
Abgeordnete der Linken im Bundestag sind Opfer einer massiven Attacke auf ihre Mail-Postfächer geworden. Diese wurden nach Angaben der Partei durch Tausende E-Mails geflutet und lahmgelegt. Sie konnten nicht mehr benutzt werden.
Die Rede war von einem "Spam-Bombing-Angriff". Die E-Mails kamen den Angaben zufolge von unterschiedlichen Absendern, hatten unterschiedliche Betreffs und waren in unterschiedlichen Sprachen geschrieben.
"Das sind bei jedem Mitglied meiner Fraktion schon über 20.000 E-Mails, die eingegangen sind, in allen möglichen Sprachen aus aller Herren Länder mit ganz vielen verschiedenen Absenderadressen. Minütlich, sekündlich gehen weitere auf dem E-Mail-Postfach ein", sagte Ina Latendorf, parlamentarische Geschäftsführerin der Fraktion, dem ARD-Hauptstadtstudio. "Wir sind jetzt dabei zu löschen, zu löschen, zu löschen, und leider schränkt das die Arbeitsfähigkeit der Büros unserer Fraktionsmitglieder sehr ein."
Andere Fraktionen nicht betroffen
Wer hinter dem Angriff steckt, ist noch unklar. Andere Fraktionen meldeten bislang keine Attacken. "Wir haben abgefragt bei den anderen Fraktionen. Die haben mir am Sonnabend und Sonntag signalisiert, dass bei ihnen keine Mitglieder des Bundestages betroffen sind", so Latendorf.
Im Mailverkehr des Bundestags insgesamt kam es lediglich zu Verzögerungen, da die Server genügend Kapazitäten haben. Die geschädigten Abgeordneten erhielten inzwischen Anleitungen, wie sie die massenhaften E-Mails filtern können. Das Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) wurde eingeschaltet.
Die Cyberattacke hat den Angaben zufolge nichts mit dem möglichen Angriff mit Spähsoftware auf iPhones von Regierungsmitgliedern und Abgeordneten zu tun. Davor hatte der Apple-Konzern gewarnt.
