title: Не кава. П’ять напоїв, які можуть допомогти при розладі шлунка
content_c:
Не кава. П’ять напоїв, які можуть допомогти при розладі шлунка
Які напої варто пити при розладі шлунка (Фото: magnific/8photo)
Коли шлунок протестує, навіть склянка звичайної води може здаватися надто великим випробуванням. Але якщо разом із нудотою з’явилися блювання або діарея, відмовлятися від рідини — погана ідея: організм втрачає не лише воду, а й електроліти.
Втім, універсального напою «від розладу шлунка» не існує. Нудота, блювання, діарея та печія мають різні причини, тому те, що допомагає в одному випадку, може в іншому лише посилити дискомфорт. Головне правило — пити те, що переноситься нормально, і правильно відновлювати рідину, якщо її втрати стали значними.
Вода
Якщо просто нудить, але рідина нормально утримується в шлунку, почати найпростіше з води. Не обов’язково випивати цілу склянку залпом: при нудоті або після блювання краще робити невеликі ковтки через короткі проміжки часу. Саме такий підхід допомагає отримувати рідину, не провокуючи новий напад блювання. При легкому розладі цього може бути достатньо. Але якщо блювання або діарея повторюються часто, однієї води може виявитися замало: разом із рідиною організм втрачає натрій, калій та інші електроліти. У такій ситуації важливіше не просто пити більше, а відновлювати і воду, і солі.
Розчин для пероральної регідратації
Якщо діарея водяниста й часта або блювання не дає нормально пити, на перше місце виходить не чай і не спортивний напій, а розчин для пероральної регідратації (ORS). Його формула не випадкова: розчин містить воду, глюкозу та електроліти у співвідношенні, яке допомагає кишечнику ефективніше всмоктувати натрій і воду. Саме тому ORS використовують для відновлення рідини при значних її втратах. CDC рекомендує такі розчини, зокрема, при тяжчій діареї, тоді як NIDDK зазначає їхню особливу користь для людей із вираженою діареєю або ознаками зневоднення. Пити ORS теж краще невеликими порціями. Якщо після кількох ковтків не виникає блювання, кількість рідини можна поступово збільшувати.
Живчик в банці на зиму: смакує як магазинний
Прозорий бульйон
Теплий прозорий бульйон може бути непоганим варіантом, коли після блювання або діареї хочеться не лише пити, а й отримати трохи солі та енергії. Він містить рідину та певну кількість натрію, хоча концентрація електролітів залежить від рецепта, тому бульйон не варто розглядати як повноцінну заміну ORS при зневодненні.
Бульйон з часниковими галушками: щоб було смачніше та ситніше
Імбирний чай
Імбир давно використовують проти нудоти, і цього разу популярний домашній засіб має під собою певне наукове підґрунтя. Огляд систематичних оглядів і метааналізів 2024 року показав, що імбир може зменшувати нудоту й блювання, зокрема після операцій, під час вагітності та в пацієнтів, які проходять хіміотерапію. Водночас автори оцінили якість попередніх метааналізів як від низької до критично низької, тому називати імбир гарантованим засобом від будь-якої нудоти було б перебільшенням.
Є й інша деталь: більшість клінічних досліджень стосувалася стандартизованих добавок або конкретних доз імбиру, а не чашки домашнього чаю. Тому теплий імбирний настій можна сприймати як комфортний варіант, який може допомогти при легкій нудоті, але не як заміну лікам чи регідратації. Якщо ж після імбиру стає гірше, з’являється печія або дискомфорт, експеримент продовжувати не потрібно.
Імбирний курячий суп з овочами
М'ятний чай — не для всіх
М’ята має репутацію універсального засобу від проблем зі шлунком, але тут варто зробити важливе уточнення. Дослідження справді показують, що капсули з олією перцевої м’яти можуть зменшувати деякі симптоми синдрому подразненого кишечника, зокрема біль. Однак це не те саме, що чашка м’ятного чаю. У метааналізі 2022 року йшлося про концентровану олію м’яти, а якість доказів автори оцінили як дуже низьку.
До того ж м’ята може бути невдалим вибором при печії та гастроезофагеальній рефлюксній хворобі. Американський коледж гастроентерології включає м’яту до потенційних харчових тригерів рефлюксу. Але важливо не перетворювати це на універсальну заборону: харчові тригери дуже індивідуальні, і не кожна людина реагує на м’яту однаково.
Огірково-м'ятний моктейль - незвично та смачно
Що краще поки відкласти
При розладі травлення не існує універсального чорного списку напоїв. Наприклад, фруктовий сік не обов’язково заборонений при діареї — NIDDK навіть допускає його в певних ситуаціях. Проте дуже солодкі напої у великій кількості можуть погіршувати діарею через осмотичний ефект, а кислі напої здатні провокувати симптоми рефлюксу в людей, які до нього чутливі. Газовані напої також можуть бути не найкращим вибором, особливо якщо вони містять багато цукру.
Імбирний ель не варто автоматично зараховувати до «лікувальних» напоїв. Назва може створювати враження, що це рідка версія імбирного чаю, але кількість імбиру в конкретному напої дуже відрізняється, тоді як цукру в ньому може бути чимало. Якщо мета — регідратація після діареї, аптечний ORS значно передбачуваніший. Кофеїн, алкоголь та дуже солодкі напої теж краще тимчасово обмежити, якщо вони посилюють нудоту, діарею або печію.
Правова інформація. Ця стаття містить загальні відомості довідкового характеру і не повинна розглядатися як альтернатива рекомендаціям лікаря. NV не несе відповідальності за будь-який діагноз, поставлений читачем на основі матеріалів сайту. NV також не несе відповідальності за зміст інших інтернет-ресурсів, посилання на які присутні в цій статті. Якщо вас турбує стан вашого здоров’я, зверніться до лікаря.

Але якщо блювання або діарея повторюються часто, однієї води може виявитися замало: разом із рідиною організм втрачає натрій, калій та інші електроліти. У такій ситуації важливіше не просто пити більше, а відновлювати і воду, і солі.
Розчин для пероральної регідратації
Якщо діарея водяниста й часта або блювання не дає нормально пити, на перше місце виходить не чай і не спортивний напій, а розчин для пероральної регідратації (ORS). Його формула не випадкова: розчин містить воду, глюкозу та електроліти у співвідношенні, яке допомагає кишечнику ефективніше всмоктувати натрій і воду. Саме тому ORS використовують для відновлення рідини при значних її втратах. CDC рекомендує такі розчини, зокрема, при тяжчій діареї, тоді як NIDDK зазначає їхню особливу користь для людей із вираженою діареєю або ознаками зневоднення. Пити ORS теж краще невеликими порціями. Якщо після кількох ковтків не виникає блювання, кількість рідини можна поступово збільшувати.
Живчик в банці на зиму: смакує як магазинний
Прозорий бульйон
Теплий прозорий бульйон може бути непоганим варіантом, коли після блювання або діареї хочеться не лише пити, а й отримати трохи солі та енергії. Він містить рідину та певну кількість натрію, хоча концентрація електролітів залежить від рецепта, тому бульйон не варто розглядати як повноцінну заміну ORS при зневодненні.
Бульйон з часниковими галушками: щоб було смачніше та ситніше
Імбирний чай
Імбир давно використовують проти нудоти, і цього разу популярний домашній засіб має під собою певне наукове підґрунтя. Огляд систематичних оглядів і метааналізів 2024 року показав, що імбир може зменшувати нудоту й блювання, зокрема після операцій, під час вагітності та в пацієнтів, які проходять хіміотерапію. Водночас автори оцінили якість попередніх метааналізів як від низької до критично низької, тому називати імбир гарантованим засобом від будь-якої нудоти було б перебільшенням.
Є й інша деталь: більшість клінічних досліджень стосувалася стандартизованих добавок або конкретних доз імбиру, а не чашки домашнього чаю. Тому теплий імбирний настій можна сприймати як комфортний варіант, який може допомогти при легкій нудоті, але не як заміну лікам чи регідратації. Якщо ж після імбиру стає гірше, з’являється печія або дискомфорт, експеримент продовжувати не потрібно.
Імбирний курячий суп з овочами
М'ятний чай — не для всіх
М’ята має репутацію універсального засобу від проблем зі шлунком, але тут варто зробити важливе уточнення. Дослідження справді показують, що капсули з олією перцевої м’яти можуть зменшувати деякі симптоми синдрому подразненого кишечника, зокрема біль. Однак це не те саме, що чашка м’ятного чаю. У метааналізі 2022 року йшлося про концентровану олію м’яти, а якість доказів автори оцінили як дуже низьку.
До того ж м’ята може бути невдалим вибором при печії та гастроезофагеальній рефлюксній хворобі. Американський коледж гастроентерології включає м’яту до потенційних харчових тригерів рефлюксу. Але важливо не перетворювати це на універсальну заборону: харчові тригери дуже індивідуальні, і не кожна людина реагує на м’яту однаково.
Огірково-м'ятний моктейль - незвично та смачно
Що краще поки відкласти
При розладі травлення не існує універсального чорного списку напоїв. Наприклад, фруктовий сік не обов’язково заборонений при діареї — NIDDK навіть допускає його в певних ситуаціях. Проте дуже солодкі напої у великій кількості можуть погіршувати діарею через осмотичний ефект, а кислі напої здатні провокувати симптоми рефлюксу в людей, які до нього чутливі. Газовані напої також можуть бути не найкращим вибором, особливо якщо вони містять багато цукру.
Імбирний ель не варто автоматично зараховувати до «лікувальних» напоїв. Назва може створювати враження, що це рідка версія імбирного чаю, але кількість імбиру в конкретному напої дуже відрізняється, тоді як цукру в ньому може бути чимало. Якщо мета — регідратація після діареї, аптечний ORS значно передбачуваніший. Кофеїн, алкоголь та дуже солодкі напої теж краще тимчасово обмежити, якщо вони посилюють нудоту, діарею або печію.
Правова інформація. Ця стаття містить загальні відомості довідкового характеру і не повинна розглядатися як альтернатива рекомендаціям лікаря. NV не несе відповідальності за будь-який діагноз, поставлений читачем на основі матеріалів сайту. NV також не несе відповідальності за зміст інших інтернет-ресурсів, посилання на які присутні в цій статті. Якщо вас турбує стан вашого здоров’я, зверніться до лікаря.

title: Переговори України та РФ за посередництва США в Абу-Дабі: Німеччина та Британія пояснили свій скептицизм
content_c:
Переговори України та РФ за посередництва США в Абу-Дабі: Німеччина та Британія пояснили свій скептицизм
Очільники оборонних відомств двох країн наголосили, що мир має бути прийнятним для України, а Європа повинна брати участь у переговорах.
Міністри оборони Німеччини та Великої Британії Борис Пісторіус і Вес Стрітінг скептично оцінили перспективи майбутніх переговорів України, США та Росії в Абу-Дабі.
Про це вони заявили на спільній пресконференції в Берліні 2 листопада, повідомляє Укрінформ.
Пісторіус пояснив свою позицію досвідом попередніх років: за його словами, після численних дискусій і переговорів російські бомбардування та атаки на Україну лише посилювалися.
Він також наголосив, що проблема полягає не в Зеленському, а подальших дій тепер мають ужити американський президент і Путін.
На переконання глави Міноборони ФРН, тривалий і справедливий мир, який гарантує суверенітет та територіальну цілісність України, неможливий без участі європейців. Саме від європейських держав очікують участі в реалізації майбутніх домовленостей.
Стрітінг підтримав оцінку німецького колеги. Він зазначив, що партнери прагнуть дипломатичного прориву, однак завершення війни має відбутися на прийнятних для України умовах.
«Не може бути жодного рішення щодо України без України», — наголосив британський міністр.
Він додав, що європейські країни безпосередньо зацікавлені в результатах переговорів, адже братимуть участь у забезпеченні гарантій безпеки. Стрітінг також підкреслив, що саме Путін повинен припинити розв’язану ним агресивну війну.
Нагадаємо, Стів Віткофф повідомив, що переговори на робочому рівні між Україною та Росією за посередництва США відбудуться 10–11 листопада в Абу-Дабі.
Нагадаємо, що раніше йшлося про переговори без Китаю: чому Пекін усунувся від самітів щодо України
На тлі відсутності зовнішнього тиску на Кремль з боку Пекіна та відсутності власної дипломатичної гри, мирні переговори ризикують перетворитися на черговий тупиковий сценарій.

title: Обошел Зинченко: Миколенко стал новым украинским рекордсменом по количеству матчей в АПЛ
content_c:
Футболист сборной Украины Виталий Миколенко, который этим летом продлил контракт с "Эвертоном", стал новым украинским рекордсменом по количеству матчей в английской Премьер-лиге.
Миколенко сыграл в девятом туре АПЛ против "Ньюкасла", а для 27-летнего украинца эта встреча стала 151-й в составе "ирисок" в чемпионате Англии.
Таким образом, Миколенко вышел в единоличные лидеры рейтинга среди украинцев по количеству сыгранных матчей в АПЛ, опередив бывшего футболиста "Манчестер Сити" и "Арсенала" Александра Зинченко.
Топ-10 украинских футболисты по количеству сыгранных матчей в АПЛ
1. Виталий Миколенко (151 матч — "Эвертон")
2. Александр Зинченко (150 — "Манчестер Сити" (76), "Арсенал" (69), "Ноттингем Форест" (5)
3. Егор Ярмолюк (102 — "Брентфорд")
4. Олег Лужный (81 — "Арсенал" (75), "Вулверхэмптон" (6)
5. Илья Забарный (78 — "Борнмут")
6. Андрей Ярмоленко (66 — "Вест Хэм Юнайтед")
7. Сергей Ребров (59 — "Тоттенхэм")
8. Михаил Мудрик (53 — "Челси" (52), "Тоттенхэм" (1)
9. Андрей Шевченко (48 — "Челси")
10. Андрей Воронин (27 — "Ливерпуль")
Напомним, 27-летний Виталий Миколенко выступает за "Эвертон" после трансфера из киевского "Динамо" в январе 2022 года за 23,5 миллиона евро.
Ранее сообщалось о том, что третий украинский футболист в истории провел 100 матчей в чемпионате Англии.

title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
content_c:
Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
- Published
Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country.
Uganda's acting army spokesperson Chris Magezi on Monday said the first group of troops deployed to Somalia through a bilateral arrangement had already arrived back home and others would follow in a few days' time.
He said all forces, including those under the African Union (AU) mission, would exit by the end of 2027 in the phased withdrawal.
Uganda was the first African country to deploy troops to Somalia under the African Union Mission in Somalia (Amisom), established in 2007 to help protect the country's transitional government from attacks by Islamist militants.
A first contingent of 109 Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) troops reportedly left the capital, Mogadishu, on Friday, following an announcement by Uganda's army chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba.
Last week, Kainerugaba said Uganda had begun pulling out its troops and would hand over security responsibilities to Somali forces.
"As we promised, we have started withdrawing UPDF from Somalia. After 20 years of a lot of blood and sacrifice, we are handing over security to our Somali brothers," he wrote on X.
On Monday, Magezi said this would mark the end of Uganda's operations in the Horn of Africa country, with Somalia expected to "assume full responsibility for security".
The withdrawal comes after Somalia President Sheikh Mohamud met his Ugandan counterpart Yoweri Museveni in Kampala last week.
The meeting was planned to discuss Somalia's security situation, as well as trade and economic ties between the two countries.
The Somali president reportedly sought to persuade Uganda to extend its military presence.
In remarks during the visit, Museveni urged Somali leaders and citizens to unite in the fight against the militant insurgency led by al-Shabab, which is part of al-Qaeda.
An estimated 4,500 troops are in Somalia under the Africa Union mission, alongside about 2,000 deployed through bilateral arrangements.
Somalia has been battling a prolonged and deadly insurgency for more than two decades.
After Ugandan forces were first deployed to the country in 2007, they played a key role in driving al-Shabab out of Mogadishu and other major towns.
They fought alongside the Somali National Army to recapture strategic territory and secure key government installations.
Ugandan troops were involved in successive Africa Union missions, including the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia (Atmis), which began with the aim of gradually transferring security responsibilities to Somalia.
This was replaced in 2025 by the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (Aussom), which is focused on strengthening Somalia's security institutions and preparing its forces to take full responsibility for the country's security.
Aussom now faces uncertainty over its future funding, amid plans to wind down US and UN support.
A 12-month transition plan is due to begin in January, giving Somalia and the AU time to seek alternative sources of funding.

Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
- Published
Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country.
Uganda's acting army spokesperson Chris Magezi on Monday said the first group of troops deployed to Somalia through a bilateral arrangement had already arrived back home and others would follow in a few days' time.
He said all forces, including those under the African Union (AU) mission, would exit by the end of 2027 in the phased withdrawal.
Uganda was the first African country to deploy troops to Somalia under the African Union Mission in Somalia (Amisom), established in 2007 to help protect the country's transitional government from attacks by Islamist militants.
A first contingent of 109 Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) troops reportedly left the capital, Mogadishu, on Friday, following an announcement by Uganda's army chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba.
Last week, Kainerugaba said Uganda had begun pulling out its troops and would hand over security responsibilities to Somali forces.
"As we promised, we have started withdrawing UPDF from Somalia. After 20 years of a lot of blood and sacrifice, we are handing over security to our Somali brothers," he wrote on X.
On Monday, Magezi said this would mark the end of Uganda's operations in the Horn of Africa country, with Somalia expected to "assume full responsibility for security".
The withdrawal comes after Somalia President Sheikh Mohamud met his Ugandan counterpart Yoweri Museveni in Kampala last week.
The meeting was planned to discuss Somalia's security situation, as well as trade and economic ties between the two countries.
The Somali president reportedly sought to persuade Uganda to extend its military presence.
In remarks during the visit, Museveni urged Somali leaders and citizens to unite in the fight against the militant insurgency led by al-Shabab, which is part of al-Qaeda.

title: Migration is a moral issue for Burnham – but is he trying to please everyone?
content_c:
While out on the campaign trail in Makerfield, Andy Burnham gave a glimpse into where he might land on Labour’s plans for immigration reform, which had already been decried by the left of the party as unfair while described on the right as electorally necessary.
Asked what he thought of Reform’s attack on “open borders Andy” – Nigel Farage’s early attempt to define him as soft on migration – the then Manchester mayor dismissed the charge as “ridiculous” and went on the defensive.
“I’m not like that. You know me. I was in the Home Office under Tony Blair, and actually, it was my job to return people. That was my specific role,” he said while out knocking on doors in the constituency.
“I used to have to travel to governments around the world and persuade them to take back planes of people who had come here with no basis to stay, so you know, I’ve never have been shy of getting to grips with these difficult issues.”
But Burnham wasn’t just pitching to the Reform-inclined voters he needed to win the seat; he was already charting whatever path he might need to take if he made it to Downing Street.
While he was supportive of attempts by the home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, to limit legal and illegal migration, which had been criticised by some senior Labour figures as un-British, Burnham wanted to reframe the changes.
“I think there’s a different way of thinking about it that might in the end get you to a better position, and one that restores public confidence,” he said.
The prime minister’s political allies say he regards migration as a moral issue, showing people who’ve lost faith in politics that the government does have control over the UK’s borders and is prepared to do something about it.
But he also wants to tell a positive story about the contribution of migration to the country, they say. Weeks after arriving in No 10, the Guardian revealed that social care workers could be exempted from the plans as he looked for ways to relieve pressure on the sector.
In an interview with ITV this week, Burnham again tried to make the case. “When you have planned migration, it’s difficult to say if it’s too high or too low,” he said, arguing that migrants help plug “gaps in the economy”.
In the end, Mahmood’s reforms came with a significant carve-out for almost 300,000 care workers to allow them to apply for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) after five years.
In a further compromise to those on the Labour benches feeling squeamish, those deemed to be making a “strong contribution” to the UK – high earners, those with strong British connections or who work in health and teaching – will also be able to settle in five years.
But that Burnham delivered the bulk of Mahmood’s hardline reforms should not come as a surprise. The prime minister, steeped in the politics of the “red wall”, understands better than many the salience of the issue with voters.
The most rigorous of the new rules first drawn up a year ago by the Home Office – retrospective changes for many migrants, and forcing small boats arrivals to face up to 30 years before applying for settlement – are still there.
How they land with the public (which polling suggests supports a doubling of the waiting time for most migrants to 10 years) now depends in part on whether ministers can convince them it’s about people making a contribution, rather than a U-turn forced by their own side.
The Conservatives and Reform, unsurprisingly, are already pushing the latter narrative, Farage describing the care workers carve-out as “the beginning of the capitulation” on borders.
Burnham is, equally predictably, arguing that it’s about fairness. “It is only fair that those who are making the most valuable contribution to our communities are given the opportunity to settle earlier,” he said.
“Those in other roles should expect to wait longer while people who abuse the system or arrive illegally will be refused or will also have to wait longer.”
But Burnham’s words did not come in the Commons chamber or at a press conference standing alongside Mahmood or even as part of his prolific social media output.
They were instead issued in a press release, after the government chose to push ahead with the sensitive policy announcement while he was out of the country – travelling to the Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua.
The plans are still likely to face criticism from some on either wing of the Labour party – for going too far or not far enough – although plenty of former critics do now appear to be on board. But without an obvious vote to coalesce around, any major rebellion looks unlikely.
Mahmood’s bigger challenge will be convincing the public. She will need Burnham, who has praised her for “gripping this problem”, to help her to do so. But the prime minister will have to accept, on an issue as divisive as this, he won’t be able to please everyone.

title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
content_c:
Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
Published November 2, 2026last updated November 2, 2026
What you need to know
This blog is now closed. It was a round-up of some of the top headlines from and about Germany on November 2, 2026:
- Merz says a woman should become Germany's next president
- Merz calls for 'digital sovereignty' at AI summit
- Education minister says weekend riots raised questions on integration
- Far-right AfD hopes to set up summit with US and Russia
Thank you for reading
We're closing the blog today. Thank you for reading, we'll be back tomorrow again!
Merz says next German president 'must be a woman'
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has spoken out in favor of having a woman succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier as Germany's president.
"I will propose a consensus candidate to the party, a candidate from the political center," Merz said at a non-public meeting of local Christian Democratic Union (CDU) chairs in Berlin, participants told the German DPA news agency.
"I am firm in my belief that it must be a woman," he reportedly added.
Germany's federal president is the country's official head of state, as opposed to the chancellor, who is the head of the government.
Current incumbent Steinmeier, a former Social Democrat (SPD) foreign minister, became president in 2017 and his second term will end in March 2027.
Bavarian premier Markus Söder recently proposed Ilse Aigner from his Christian Social Union (CSU), the CDU's Bavarian sister party.
But the CDU itself may propose an alternative candidate from within its own ranks, with current parliamentary speaker Julia Klöckner, Families Minister Karin Prien and former CDU leader and Defense Minister Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer all having been mentioned.
The CDU's top leadership is expected to propose a candidate on November 9.
Germany must preserve 'digital sovereignty' in AI era, Merz says
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says Germany must speed up its development of artificial intelligence capabilities to protect its "digital sovereignty" in an era of rapid change.
Speaking at a conference on AI in Berlin, the chancellor said countries risked surrendering control to outside providers by failing to keep pace.
"That is why we must, at all costs, avoid becoming entirely dependent on third parties when it comes to developing and using this technology," he said. "And that is why the issue of digital sovereignty in the context of AI becomes a truly existential question."
Merz stressed that people and their dignity must remain central to political efforts to manage rapid technological progress, saying AI development should be guided by human values.
He also said adapting to AI-driven changes required "an enormous technological and organizational effort, a far-reaching modernization of our state and our economy."
Merz pointed to Germany's strength as a business location and home of industrial engineering. He also said international cooperation was crucial, and that Berlin would seek to work with like-minded partners such as France and Canada to share knowledge and diversify supply chains.
Merz appointed a minister for digitalization and modernization last year after taking office. Although many German companies have adopted and integrated AI technology, critics say Germany has been too slow to build the digital infrastructure and skills needed to exploit it fully.
Zverev officially reaches No.1 in men's tennis rankings
Alexander Zverev officially rose to the No. 1 spot in the men's tennis rankings on Monday, becoming only the second German man to hold the title after Boris Becker 35 years ago.
"Today is a historic day for German tennis," said German Tennis Federation President Dietloff von Arnim. "Sascha has earned this spot at the top of the world rankings through extraordinary perseverance and hard work."
The 29-year-old beat Flavio Cobolli to win the French Open title in June, before going on to lift the US Open trophy after defeating Ben Shelton in September.
He also reached the final at Wimbledon this year, ultimately falling to Jannik Sinner, and the Australian Open semifinals.
He is the 30th male player to reach No. 1, and the oldest in more than 50 years to top the rankings for the first time.
"I had to wait," said Zverev, who reached the top spot more than four years after becoming No. 2. "But sometimes you've got to wait for the best things in life. I'm super happy, super thrilled."
Sinner, who had been holding the No.1 spot since April 13, dropped to second, ahead of Carlos Alcaraz.
Far-right AfD hopeful of trilateral Russia-US summit
Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has confirmed that a summit with Russian and American advisers "at the highest possible level" is being planned.
The AfD's foreign policy spokesman, Markus Frohnmaier, said the meeting is likely to take place in Abu Dhabi in early 2027 and will focus on restoring Russian gas deliveries to Germany.
DW understands that AfD leaders Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla would attend the meeting if US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were also present.
Such a meeting would represent a major PR coup for the far-right party, which remains shunned by most of Germany's political establishment despite leading national opinion polls.
"The focus here will be on discussions with the American side, as well as the Russian side, particularly with regard to economic partnership, energy partnership and also the Nord Stream question," Frohnmaier told journalists in Berlin.
According to Frohnmaier, Kirill Dmitriev, a special adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin, is coordinating with contacts in the US administration.
Dmitriev greeted Witkoff, US President Donald Trump's Middle East envoy, when he arrived in Russia for talks last month.
Dmitriev has also been cultivating contacts in Germany. He and Frohnmaier met at an economic forum in St. Petersburg earlier this year.
In September, Dmitriev described the anti-immigration, anti-EU AfD as "the hope for Germany" during regional election campaigns. The party wants to end sanctions on Russia and halt weapons deliveries to Ukraine.
While the Abu Dhabi summit is expected to focus on business and economic ties, Frohnmaier said such formats can "establish a framework for dialogue" and help "work toward peace."
Jewish Academy opens in Frankfurt amid tight security
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier attended the opening of a new Jewish Academy in Frankfurt on Monday.
The €40-million ($45-million) educational institution, which was inaugurated under tight security, is to be a "place of dialogue," Steinmeier said.
He denounced antisemitism and said it must be "put in its place, without loopholes or reservations," whether it comes from the left or the right of the political spectrum.
The president also warned against what he described as the increasing political exploitation of hatred toward Jews.
"All parties have a duty to confront antisemitism throughout their entire sphere of influence — from the party leadership down to the rank and file and among their supporters," he said. "Antisemitism must not be allowed to influence government work anywhere in Germany."
The academy's opening ceremony was also attended by the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, Josef Schuster, who described the center as a "milestone" that would be "dedicated to the full diversity of Jewish thought and Jewish experiences."
He said Jewish life in Germany was under greater threat than at any time since the Holocaust, with an "explosive rise" in antisemitism since the Hamas-led terror attack on Israel on October 7, 2023.
He said the new center could play a role in turning this around, stressing the importance of openness, enlightenment, dialogue and "education, education and yet more education."
The academy is funded by the federal government, the state of Hesse, the city of Frankfurt and the Central Council of Jews.
It is aimed at a wide audience and offers a range of programs and events, including international conferences, educational courses, and panel discussions.
German retailers condemn weekend riots
The German Retail Association says society as a whole has a responsibility to prevent the kind of violence that followed youth protests in several German cities on Saturday.
In Frankfurt, rioters threw stones and petrol bombs, smashed shop windows and looted businesses. Violent confrontations were also reported in other parts of the country.
"We must not tolerate a social climate in which retailers cannot always be certain, wherever they are, that they can go about their business unhindered," association boss Stefan Genth said.
"This applies to society as a whole. We are all called upon to act," he said, adding that it must be clear that violence, or the threat of it, has no place in Germany.
Tens of thousands of young people demonstrated across the country over the weekend calling for better education funding and measures to bring down the cost of living. The protests were largely peaceful, although in some cities they were followed by rioting and looting.
Genth said it was alarming "that some retailers in certain locations felt compelled last Saturday to take extra security measures or, in some cases, to close their shops entirely."
Praise and condemnation from Merz following protests
Chancellor Friedrich Merz is to tell a conference of local party leaders of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) that he saw a positive aspect to weekend youth protests, while condemning violence that occurred in their aftermath.
"I take above all a positive message from the weekend: The young generation is politically engaged and is concerned about its future," he is to say, according to a speech released beforehand to news agencies.
In the planned speech, Merz says the government is making efforts not to burden the younger generation with the costs of an aging society.
"That is why we are carrying out pension reform for young people, why we are concerned about our security, and why we are preparing our economy for the digital future," Merz's speech runs.
'No tolerance' for violence
However, the chancellor has harsh words for those who rioted and attacked police on the sidelines of the mostly peaceful protests.
"Violence has no place on our streets, and my government will show no tolerance in this regard," the speech says.
"Anyone who attacks police officers and emergency service personnel and loots shops is attacking our freedom, mocking society and the legitimate interests of young people," the chancellor emphasizes in the speech.
"The offenders will feel the full force of the law."
Tens of thousands of young people demonstrated across Germany over the weekend, mostly peacefully.
However, several of the protests were followed by sometimes severe riots, such as in Frankfurt, where stones and petrol bombs were thrown, shop windows were smashed and looting took place.
More than 100 police officers were injured.
Major metal and electrical union calls for thousands to strike
The trade union IG Metall, which represents workers in the metalworking, electrical, steel, automotive and industrial manufacturing sectors, has called on thousands of employees to walk out at more than 2,000 workplaces nationwide by the end of the week.
A number of companies are expected to be affected, including carmakers Opel and Rolls-Royce, consumer goods giant Procter & Gamble, e-mobility supplier Vitesco, Daimler Truck AG and precision engineering firm Paul Beier GmbH.
The union, Germany and Europe's largest, is calling for a 5% pay rise over a 12-month period, along with job and site security.
Employers have put forward an offer of a one-off payment next year and a pay rise of 1.3% in July 2028, citing Germany's economic woes and cost pressures on industry to justify not meeting the union's demand.
Riots on weekend raised questions of integration — education minister
Education Minister Karin Prien has said the violence that occurred in the aftermath of youth protests on Saturday evening was in part an indication that the integration of people of migrant background into German society could be improved.
Prien told broadcaster Deutschlandfunk said that the "for the most part peaceful demonstrations" had been followed by rioting by left-wing radicals "but also by others who probably come from migrant milieus."
She said that recognizing this fact was not about stirring up resentments, which she called "politically wrong," but about facing reality and getting a picture of why people resort to such means.
"And if they come from migrant milieus, we should be worried about it and look at the causes," said Prien, a member of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU).
She said one question was why integration succeeds less well in some groups than in others.
"And it's not about the question of a passport. It's about the question: Why have people not been integrated into our society and what can be done so it works better in future," she said.
Her comments came despite the fact that authorities in Frankfurt, which saw the worst of the violence, said that most of the people they arrested in connection with rioting over the weekend were German citizens.
Interior minister blames 'migrant anarchists'
Prien's remarks came after archconservative Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) said the "peaceful demonstrations were hijacked toward the evening by violence-prone left-wing groups and migrant anarchists," without offering evidence for who was behind the violent turn in the demonstrations.
Dobrindt's comment was, however, called into question by Defense Minister Boris Pistorius of the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), the junior partner in Germany's federal coalition government.
"What are migrant groups, then? Are these people living in Germany in the third generation who are German nationals? Where do we stop differentiating here? I think this is going in the wrong direction," he said.
Pistorius said, however, that whoever had been responsible for the rioting had to be punished for it.
His intervention comes as the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) continues, without evidence, to blame migration for most of the country's problems, with Dobrindt seeming to adopt some of the populist party's anti-migrant rhetoric.
Accused in deadly car ramming in Leipzig goes on trial
A 34-year-old man accused of having killed two people while racing with his car through a pedestrian zone in the eastern city of Leipzig in May is going on trial on Monday.
The accused has also been charged with 85 counts of attempted murder.
State prosecutors argue that the man planned the attack with the intent of killing people with his car, which reached speeds of up to 90 kmh (56 mph) during the rampage.
A 63-year-old woman and a 77-year-old man were killed in the incident.
The accused is said to have checked into a psychiatric clinic of his own free will a month before the attack and to have been discharged at his own wish a few days prior to it.
However, a psychiatric assessment has found no indications of diminished capacity on his part.
The trial has been scheduled to last until July of next year.
Germany's gas storage level well below target — AGSI
German natural gas storage facilities are currently only around 61.2% full, according to figures from a European platform that monitors storage levels. AGSI.
That falls well short of the 70% targeted by Sunday.
However, a spokeswoman for Economy Minister Katherina Reiche said there was no cause for concern.
"Germany's gas supply is secure for the coming winter, even with the current storage levels," she said.
"Based on the current assessment, we expect Germany to get through the winter in good shape. Security of supply depends not only on storage levels, but also on actual gas withdrawals, ongoing gas imports and additional precautionary measures," the spokeswoman said.
But Sebastian Heinermann,  Sebastian Heinermann, managing director of the Initiative Energien Speichern (Energy Storage Initiative), a mouthpiece for the sector, said the current storage levels were a "serious warning."
   
"Germany is entering the heating season with smaller safety reserves. This increases the vulnerability of the gas supply, particularly in the event of exceptionally low temperatures or additional disruptions to gas imports," Heinermann said.
The Economy Ministry has said the war in Iran, which has brought a partial blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital transport route for global gas and oil, was one factor behind the current low storage level.
However, it says Germany now has more options to access additional gas than was the case in 2022, when the gas supply from Russia was cut off amid Moscow's launch of its invasion of Ukraine.
AI on the agenda at German-British talks on military cooperation
The German and British defense ministers are also expected to focus on artificial intelligence as a field for enhanced military cooperation at talks on Monday.
"By jointly testing, developing and, finally, introducing AI in our armed forces, we want to deepen our cooperation and keep pace with those who want to hurt us," UK Defense Minister Wes Streeting wrote in the daily Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung ahead of talks with his German counterpart, Boris Pistorius.
"Our opponents' readiness to harm us is not new. What is new is their abilities to do so. This demands an answer from all of us in Europe," he wrote.
Representatives from government and industry from both countries are to meet in the spring of next year to push ahead with the implementation of these plans, he wrote.
Two years ago, Germany and the United Kingdom agreed to cooperate more closely on military matters in the so-called Trinity House Agreement.
A year later, both countries announced that they would be focusing more on cyber defense as part of this cooperation.
Government to open AI-focused Digital Summit in Berlin
A two-day conference in Berlin that will look at ways of enhancing Germany's digital infrastructure, particularly in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), is to be opened by the minister for digital affairs, Karsten Wildberger, on Monday morning.
More than 1,000 guests, including digital ministers from Europe and Canada, are expected to attend the summit, which this year will focus largely on the uses and safety of AI and new developments in the field.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz is scheduled to hold a speech in the afternoon and to meet with a robot from the German company Neura Robotics.
The company develops robots that can see, hear and feel and are potentially utilizable in both industries and households.
The event is being held for the 19th time since its inception in 2006 as the National IT Summit. It did not take place in 2021, an election year in Germany.
Welcome to our coverage
Guten Morgen from DW's newsroom in Bonn as the first, chilly week of November gets underway.
That wintry cold makes a report that gas storage levels are well below what they should be at the start of the heating season sobering reading.
Meanwhile, an annual digital summit in Berlin that will look at ways of boosting the field of artificial intelligence (AI) in Germany and Europe is also kicking off.
It is set to bring a hopefully friendly encounter between Chancellor Merz and a humanoid robot from the German company Neura Robotics.
AI will also be on the agenda at afternoon talks between Defense Minister Boris Pistorius and his UK counterpart Wes Streeting, as the two discuss enhancing German-British military cooperation.
Please read on for more content — not AI-generated, we promise — on these and other stories.
description: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has spoken out in favor of having a woman succeed Frank-Walter Steinmeier as Germany's president.
"I will propose a consensus candidate to the party, a candidate from the political center," Merz said at a non-public meeting of local Christian Democratic Union (CDU) chairs in Berlin, participants told the German DPA news agency.
"I am firm in my belief that it must be a woman," he reportedly added.
Germany's federal president is the country's official head of state, as opposed to the chancellor, who is the head of the government.
Current incumbent Steinmeier, a former Social Democrat (SPD) foreign minister, became president in 2017 and his second term will end in March 2027.
Bavarian premier Markus Söder recently proposed Ilse Aigner from his Christian Social Union (CSU), the CDU's Bavarian sister party.
But the CDU itself may propose an alternative candidate from within its own ranks, with current parliamentary speaker Julia Klöckner, Families Minister Karin Prien and former CDU leader and Defense Minister Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer all having been mentioned.
The CDU's top leadership is expected to propose a candidate on November 9.
Germany must preserve 'digital sovereignty' in AI era, Merz says
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says Germany must speed up its development of artificial intelligence capabilities to protect its "digital sovereignty" in an era of rapid change.
Speaking at a conference on AI in Berlin, the chancellor said countries risked surrendering control to outside providers by failing to keep pace.
"That is why we must, at all costs, avoid becoming entirely dependent on third parties when it comes to developing and using this technology," he said. "And that is why the issue of digital sovereignty in the context of AI becomes a truly existential question."
Merz stressed that people and their dignity must remain central to political efforts to manage rapid technological progress, saying AI development should be guided by human values.
He also said adapting to AI-driven changes required "an enormous technological and organizational effort, a far-reaching modernization of our state and our economy."
Merz pointed to Germany's strength as a business location and home of industrial engineering. He also said international cooperation was crucial, and that Berlin would seek to work with like-minded partners such as France and Canada to share knowledge and diversify supply chains.
Merz appointed a minister for digitalization and modernization last year after taking office. Although many German companies have adopted and integrated AI technology, critics say Germany has been too slow to build the digital infrastructure and skills needed to exploit it fully.
Zverev officially reaches No.1 in men's tennis rankings
Alexander Zverev officially rose to the No. 1 spot in the men's tennis rankings on Monday, becoming only the second German man to hold the title after Boris Becker 35 years ago.
"Today is a historic day for German tennis," said German Tennis Federation President Dietloff von Arnim. "Sascha has earned this spot at the top of the world rankings through extraordinary perseverance and hard work."
The 29-year-old beat Flavio Cobolli to win the French Open title in June, before going on to lift the US Open trophy after defeating Ben Shelton in September.
He also reached the final at Wimbledon this year, ultimately falling to Jannik Sinner, and the Australian Open semifinals.
He is the 30th male player to reach No. 1, and the oldest in more than 50 years to top the rankings for the first time.
"I had to wait," said Zverev, who reached the top spot more than four years after becoming No. 2. "But sometimes you've got to wait for the best things in life. I'm super happy, super thrilled."
Sinner, who had been holding the No.1 spot since April 13, dropped to second, ahead of Carlos Alcaraz.
Far-right AfD hopeful of trilateral Russia-US summit
Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has confirmed that a summit with Russian and American advisers "at the highest possible level" is being planned.
The AfD's foreign policy spokesman, Markus Frohnmaier, said the meeting is likely to take place in Abu Dhabi in early 2027 and will focus on restoring Russian gas deliveries to Germany.
DW understands that AfD leaders Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla would attend the meeting if US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were also present.
Such a meeting would represent a major PR coup for the far-right party, which remains shunned by most of Germany's political establishment despite leading national opinion polls.
"The focus here will be on discussions with the American side, as well as the Russian side, particularly with regard to economic partnership, energy partnership and also the Nord Stream question," Frohnmaier told journalists in Berlin.
According to Frohnmaier, Kirill Dmitriev, a special adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin, is coordinating with contacts in the US administration.
Dmitriev greeted Witkoff, US President Donald Trump's Middle East envoy, when he arrived in Russia for talks last month.
Dmitriev has also been cultivating contacts in Germany. He and Frohnmaier met at an economic forum in St. Petersburg earlier this year.
In September, Dmitriev described the anti-immigration, anti-EU AfD as "the hope for Germany" during regional election campaigns. The party wants to end sanctions on Russia and halt weapons deliveries to Ukraine.
While the Abu Dhabi summit is expected to focus on business and economic ties, Frohnmaier said such formats can "establish a framework for dialogue" and help "work toward peace."
Jewish Academy opens in Frankfurt amid tight security
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier attended the opening of a new Jewish Academy in Frankfurt on Monday.
The €40-million ($45-million) educational institution, which was inaugurated under tight security, is to be a "place of dialogue," Steinmeier said.
He denounced antisemitism and said it must be "put in its place, without loopholes or reservations," whether it comes from the left or the right of the political spectrum.
The president also warned against what he described as the increasing political exploitation of hatred toward Jews.
"All parties have a duty to confront antisemitism throughout their entire sphere of influence — from the party leadership down to the rank and file and among their supporters," he said. "Antisemitism must not be allowed to influence government work anywhere in Germany."
The academy's opening ceremony was also attended by the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, Josef Schuster, who described the center as a "milestone" that would be "dedicated to the full diversity of Jewish thought and Jewish experiences."
He said Jewish life in Germany was under greater threat than at any time since the Holocaust, with an "explosive rise" in antisemitism since the Hamas-led terror attack on Israel on October 7, 2023.
He said the new center could play a role in turning this around, stressing the importance of openness, enlightenment, dialogue and "education, education and yet more education."
The academy is funded by the federal government, the state of Hesse, the city of Frankfurt and the Central Council of Jews.
It is aimed at a wide audience and offers a range of programs and events, including international conferences, educational courses, and panel discussions.
German retailers condemn weekend riots
The German Retail Association says society as a whole has a responsibility to prevent the kind of violence that followed youth protests in several German cities on Saturday.
In Frankfurt, rioters threw stones and petrol bombs, smashed shop windows and looted businesses. Violent confrontations were also reported in other parts of the country.
"We must not tolerate a social climate in which retailers cannot always be certain, wherever they are, that they can go about their business unhindered," association boss Stefan Genth said.
"This applies to society as a whole. We are all called upon to act," he said, adding that it must be clear that violence, or the threat of it, has no place in Germany.
Tens of thousands of young people demonstrated across the country over the weekend calling for better education funding and measures to bring down the cost of living. The protests were largely peaceful, although in some cities they were followed by rioting and looting.
Genth said it was alarming "that some retailers in certain locations felt compelled last Saturday to take extra security measures or, in some cases, to close their shops entirely."
Praise and condemnation from Merz following protests
Chancellor Friedrich Merz is to tell a conference of local party leaders of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) that he saw a positive aspect to weekend youth protests, while condemning violence that occurred in their aftermath.
"I take above all a positive message from the weekend: The young generation is politically engaged and is concerned about its future," he is to say, according to a speech released beforehand to news agencies.
In the planned speech, Merz says the government is making efforts not to burden the younger generation with the costs of an aging society.
"That is why we are carrying out pension reform for young people, why we are concerned about our security, and why we are preparing our economy for the digital future," Merz's speech runs.
'No tolerance' for violence
However, the chancellor has harsh words for those who rioted and attacked police on the sidelines of the mostly peaceful protests.
"Violence has no place on our streets, and my government will show no tolerance in this regard," the speech says.
"Anyone who attacks police officers and emergency service personnel and loots shops is attacking our freedom, mocking society and the legitimate interests of young people," the chancellor emphasizes in the speech.
"The offenders will feel the full force of the law."
Tens of thousands of young people demonstrated across Germany over the weekend, mostly peacefully.
However, several of the protests were followed by sometimes severe riots, such as in Frankfurt, where stones and petrol bombs were thrown, shop windows were smashed and looting took place.
More than 100 police officers were injured.
Major metal and electrical union calls for thousands to strike
The trade union IG Metall, which represents workers in the metalworking, electrical, steel, automotive and industrial manufacturing sectors, has called on thousands of employees to walk out at more than 2,000 workplaces nationwide by the end of the week.
A number of companies are expected to be affected, including carmakers Opel and Rolls-Royce, consumer goods giant Procter & Gamble, e-mobility supplier Vitesco, Daimler Truck AG and precision engineering firm Paul Beier GmbH.
The union, Germany and Europe's largest, is calling for a 5% pay rise over a 12-month period, along with job and site security.
Employers have put forward an offer of a one-off payment next year and a pay rise of 1.3% in July 2028, citing Germany's economic woes and cost pressures on industry to justify not meeting the union's demand.
Riots on weekend raised questions of integration — education minister
Education Minister Karin Prien has said the violence that occurred in the aftermath of youth protests on Saturday evening was in part an indication that the integration of people of migrant background into German society could be improved.
Prien told broadcaster Deutschlandfunk said that the "for the most part peaceful demonstrations" had been followed by rioting by left-wing radicals "but also by others who probably come from migrant milieus."
She said that recognizing this fact was not about stirring up resentments, which she called "politically wrong," but about facing reality and getting a picture of why people resort to such means.
"And if they come from migrant milieus, we should be worried about it and look at the causes," said Prien, a member of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU).
She said one question was why integration succeeds less well in some groups than in others.
"And it's not about the question of a passport. It's about the question: Why have people not been integrated into our society and what can be done so it works better in future," she said.
Her comments came despite the fact that authorities in Frankfurt, which saw the worst of the violence, said that most of the people they arrested in connection with rioting over the weekend were German citizens.
Interior minister blames 'migrant anarchists'
Prien's remarks came after archconservative Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) said the "peaceful demonstrations were hijacked toward the evening by violence-prone left-wing groups and migrant anarchists," without offering evidence for who was behind the violent turn in the demonstrations.
Dobrindt's comment was, however, called into question by Defense Minister Boris Pistorius of the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), the junior partner in Germany's federal coalition government.
"What are migrant groups, then? Are these people living in Germany in the third generation who are German nationals? Where do we stop differentiating here? I think this is going in the wrong direction," he said.
Pistorius said, however, that whoever had been responsible for the rioting had to be punished for it.
His intervention comes as the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) continues, without evidence, to blame migration for most of the country's problems, with Dobrindt seeming to adopt some of the populist party's anti-migrant rhetoric.
Accused in deadly car ramming in Leipzig goes on trial
A 34-year-old man accused of having killed two people while racing with his car through a pedestrian zone in the eastern city of Leipzig in May is going on trial on Monday.
The accused has also been charged with 85 counts of attempted murder.
State prosecutors argue that the man planned the attack with the intent of killing people with his car, which reached speeds of up to 90 kmh (56 mph) during the rampage.
A 63-year-old woman and a 77-year-old man were killed in the incident.
The accused is said to have checked into a psychiatric clinic of his own free will a month before the attack and to have been discharged at his own wish a few days prior to it.
However, a psychiatric assessment has found no indications of diminished capacity on his part.
The trial has been scheduled to last until July of next year.
Germany's gas storage level well below target — AGSI
German natural gas storage facilities are currently only around 61.2% full, according to figures from a European platform that monitors storage levels. AGSI.
That falls well short of the 70% targeted by Sunday.
However, a spokeswoman for Economy Minister Katherina Reiche said there was no cause for concern.
"Germany's gas supply is secure for the coming winter, even with the current storage levels," she said.
"Based on the current assessment, we expect Germany to get through the winter in good shape. Security of supply depends not only on storage levels, but also on actual gas withdrawals, ongoing gas imports and additional precautionary measures," the spokeswoman said.
But Sebastian Heinermann,  Sebastian Heinermann, managing director of the Initiative Energien Speichern (Energy Storage Initiative), a mouthpiece for the sector, said the current storage levels were a "serious warning."
   
"Germany is entering the heating season with smaller safety reserves. This increases the vulnerability of the gas supply, particularly in the event of exceptionally low temperatures or additional disruptions to gas imports," Heinermann said.
The Economy Ministry has said the war in Iran, which has brought a partial blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital transport route for global gas and oil, was one factor behind the current low storage level.
However, it says Germany now has more options to access additional gas than was the case in 2022, when the gas supply from Russia was cut off amid Moscow's launch of its invasion of Ukraine.
AI on the agenda at German-British talks on military cooperation
The German and British defense ministers are also expected to focus on artificial intelligence as a field for enhanced military cooperation at talks on Monday.
"By jointly testing, developing and, finally, introducing AI in our armed forces, we want to deepen our cooperation and keep pace with those who want to hurt us," UK Defense Minister Wes Streeting wrote in the daily Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung ahead of talks with his German counterpart, Boris Pistorius.
"Our opponents' readiness to harm us is not new. What is new is their abilities to do so. This demands an answer from all of us in Europe," he wrote.
Representatives from government and industry from both countries are to meet in the spring of next year to push ahead with the implementation of these plans, he wrote.
Two years ago, Germany and the United Kingdom agreed to cooperate more closely on military matters in the so-called Trinity House Agreement.
A year later, both countries announced that they would be focusing more on cyber defense as part of this cooperation.
Government to open AI-focused Digital Summit in Berlin
A two-day conference in Berlin that will look at ways of enhancing Germany's digital infrastructure, particularly in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), is to be opened by the minister for digital affairs, Karsten Wildberger, on Monday morning.
More than 1,000 guests, including digital ministers from Europe and Canada, are expected to attend the summit, which this year will focus largely on the uses and safety of AI and new developments in the field.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz is scheduled to hold a speech in the afternoon and to meet with a robot from the German company Neura Robotics.
The company develops robots that can see, hear and feel and are potentially utilizable in both industries and households.
The event is being held for the 19th time since its inception in 2006 as the National IT Summit. It did not take place in 2021, an election year in Germany.
Welcome to our coverage
Guten Morgen from DW's newsroom in Bonn as the first, chilly week of November gets underway.
That wintry cold makes a report that gas storage levels are well below what they should be at the start of the heating season sobering reading.
Meanwhile, an annual digital summit in Berlin that will look at ways of boosting the field of artificial intelligence (AI) in Germany and Europe is also kicking off.
It is set to bring a hopefully friendly encounter between Chancellor Merz and a humanoid robot from the German company Neura Robotics.
AI will also be on the agenda at afternoon talks between Defense Minister Boris Pistorius and his UK counterpart Wes Streeting, as the two discuss enhancing German-British military cooperation.

title: Afghanistan: Paris plant Rückführungen, USA prüfen Abschiebung auf Umwegen
content_c:
Flüge nach Afghanistan Frankreich bahnt mit Taliban Abschiebungen an – USA versuchen es durch die Hintertür
Frankreich führt Gespräche mit den Behörden der radikalislamischen Taliban über die Rückführung irregulärer afghanischer Migranten. »Wir versuchen, die Möglichkeit zu schaffen, eine bestimmte Anzahl von Afghanen ohne Aufenthaltsgenehmigung zurückzuführen. Das sind technische Gespräche«, sagte Frankreichs Innenminister Laurent Nuñez am Montag vor dem französischen Parlament. »Andere Länder tun das, Deutschland tut das.«
Wie Frankreich erkennt Deutschland die Taliban-Regierung nicht offiziell an, führt aber hochrangige Gespräche mit ihr. Außerdem ermöglichte die Bundesregierung den Taliban die weitgehende Übernahme der diplomatischen Vertretungen Afghanistans in Deutschland – anders als etwa in Österreich und zahlreichen anderen Staaten. Treibende Kraft ist dabei Bundesinnenminister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU), ausgewiesenes Ziel sind mehr Abschiebungen.
Im Juni flog eine Taliban-Delegation nach Brüssel, um mit Vertretern der EU und 15 Mitgliedstaaten über die Rücknahme abgelehnter Asylsuchender zu verhandeln. Damals hatte es heftige Kritik von Menschenrechtsorganisationen und linken Gruppen gegeben. Auch die EU erkennt die Taliban-Regierung nicht offiziell an.
Ebenfalls am Montag hatte sich die Taliban-Regierung besorgt über mutmaßliche Pläne der USA geäußert, afghanische Migranten über Pakistan abzuschieben. Außenministeriumssprecher Abdul Kahar Balchi forderte Washington am Montag auf, einen »verantwortungsvollen und maßvollen Ansatz« zu wählen. Sämtliche Entscheidungen müssten »die Rechte und legitimen Forderungen« der Betroffenen berücksichtigen. Weiter betonte er Kabuls Bereitschaft, in dieser Angelegenheit auf Basis gegenseitigen Verständnisses praktisch zusammenzuarbeiten. Den Taliban selbst werden immer wieder massive Verletzungen der Grundrechte vieler Menschen angelastet. Vor allem die Situation der Frauen und Mädchen hat sich seit der Machtübernahme drastisch verschlechtert.
Im Heimatland drohen Verfolgung und Gewalt
Die »New York Times« hatte unter Berufung auf drei US-Regierungsmitarbeiter über Pläne berichtet , mehr als 150 Afghanen über Pakistan auszuweisen. Eine direkte Abschiebung nach Afghanistan ist der US-Regierung nicht möglich. Den Betroffenen drohen in ihrem Heimatland Verfolgung und Gewalt. Laut der Menschenrechtsgruppe AfghanEvac betrifft dies auch Menschen, die bis zum Abzug 2021 das US-Militär vor Ort unterstützt haben.

Farbenfrohe Schleier, kein Kopftuch: Frauen in Afghanistan kurzzeitig inhaftiert, Uno übt Kritik1 Min1 Min
Zwar hatten die Taliban nach ihrer Machtübernahme eine Generalamnestie für ehemalige Mitarbeiter westlicher Streitkräfte und Regierungen verkündet, um ihnen eine sichere Rückkehr zu garantieren. Uno-Berichten zufolge kommt es jedoch immer wieder zu außergerichtlichen Tötungen, Willkürjustiz und Misshandlungen.
Das Verhältnis zwischen Pakistan und Afghanistan ist aufgrund wiederholter Zusammenstöße an der gemeinsamen Grenze angespannt. Pakistan wirft den Taliban vor, Kämpfern Schutz zu gewähren, die für Anschläge in Pakistan verantwortlich seien, was Kabul bestreitet. Vor diesem Hintergrund wies die pakistanische Regierung ihre Sicherheitsbehörden an, afghanische Staatsbürger ohne gültiges Visum festzunehmen.

title: AfD und Linke: Warum Extremismus-Vergleiche zu kurz greifen
content_c:
AfD und Linke Warum Extremismus-Vergleiche zu kurz greifen
SPD und Grüne laufen Sturm gegen die Gleichsetzung von AfD und der Linken durch CDU und CSU. Experten betonen deutliche Unterschiede, vor allem bei Ideologie und Bewertung des Verfassungsschutzes.
"Deutschlandtag" der Jungen Union. Auf dem Bildschirm hinter dem Podium prangt in riesigen Lettern: "Nie wieder ist jetzt". Eine Parole, die vor der Wiederkehr des Nationalsozialismus warnt. Flankiert wird der Spruch von einem Wahlkampfaufkleber der Berliner Linken, der für die Spitzenkandidatin Elif Eralp wirbt, und dem Bild eines Vermummten mit Palästinensertuch. Die Botschaft: Die bei der Wahl zum Abgeordnetenhaus siegreiche Linke sei extremistisch und antisemitisch - und somit zu vergleichen mit dem Nationalsozialismus.
"Einen solchen Vergleich halte ich für daneben", sagt Extremismusforscher Hendrik Hansen im Gespräch mit tagesschau.de. Er lehrt an der Hochschule des Bundes für öffentliche Verwaltung in der Abteilung Verfassungsschutz.
Der Politikwissenschaftler Wolfgang Schroeder erklärt die Aktion im tagesschau.de-Interview mit der Defensive, in der sich die Unionsparteien derzeit befänden: "Aus dieser Lage heraus versucht man, neue Gegnerbezüge aufzubauen, um die Reihen zu schließen und zu verhindern, dass es zu einem Bündnis zwischen SPD, Grünen und Linkspartei kommt." Schroeder lehrt an der Uni Kassel und war Mitglied der SPD-Grundwertekommission.
Extremismus: Alles in einen Topf?
Extremismus ist ein politischer Begriff, mit dem man Gegner diskreditieren kann. CDU und CSU sind mit dem Vorwurf konfrontiert, die Linke mit der AfD in einen "Extremismustopf" zu werfen und damit Unterschiede zwischen beiden Parteien einzuebnen. Er finde "es schwer zu ertragen, was die Union derzeit aufführt", entgegnet Bremens Bürgermeister Andreas Bovenschulte (SPD). CDU und CSU wirft er Relativierung vor. Die Abgrenzung zu den "Verfassungsfeinden" der AfD werde "verwischt".
"CDU und CSU müssen enger zusammenstehen denn je", hatte CDU-Chef und Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz kürzlich auf dem CSU-Parteitag gesagt. Die Union werde von "Extremisten" von ganz rechts und von ganz links bekämpft, womit Merz AfD und Linke meinte.
In der Wissenschaft bezeichnet Extremismus das, was sich außerhalb der Grenzen der freiheitlich-demokratischen Grundordnung bewegt. Experten lehnen politische Pauschalurteile ab und plädieren für eine differenzierte Sicht. Hinzu kommt: "Wir haben es bei AfD und der Linken mit Parteien zu tun, die nicht insgesamt extremistisch sind", sagt Hansen.
Hohe Zahl an Rechtsextremisten bei der AfD
Bei der AfD lässt sich der Anteil der Extremisten recht gut überblicken, weil sie großflächig vom Verfassungsschutz beobachtet wird. Die Behörde zählte 2025 28.000 Rechtsextremisten in der Partei - bei einer Mitgliederzahl von damals 70.000.
Im Falle der Linken, sagt Hansen, könnten keine genauen Angaben gemacht werden. Die Linke sei "nicht mehr die eines Gregor Gysi", sagte der CSU-Chef und bayerische Ministerpräsident Markus Söder vor Kurzem. Die Partei sei "eine radikale Linke" geworden, eine Entwicklung, die auch Experten wie Hendrik Hansen erkennen.
Der Grund: In den vergangenen zwei Jahren habe sich die Mitgliederzahl "mehr als verdoppelt", sagt der Extremismusforscher. "Und diese neuen Mitglieder, da gibt es schon erste Anhaltspunkte", seien "deutlich radikaler als die bisherigen Mitglieder". Man müsse also davon ausgehen, "dass die heutige Linke nicht mehr die Linke ist von Dietmar Bartsch oder Bodo Ramelow". Radikale Haltungen können sich allerdings im Rahmen der freiheitlichen Demokratie bewegen. Ob die Partei durch den Mitgliederzulauf auch extremistischer wird, steht also noch nicht fest.
Unterschiedliche Weltanschauungen
Für Wolfgang Schroeder zielen sowohl die Linke als auch die AfD darauf, "das demokratische Zentrum" von den Rändern her unter Druck zu setzen. Allerdings geschehe das auf sehr unterschiedlichen "weltanschaulichen, soziologischen und politischen Grundlagen". Anders als die AfD akzeptiere die Linke "grundsätzlich die Gleichheit der Menschenwürde".
Hansen verweist auf die "ethnokulturelle Politik" der AfD, "die sich darauf fokussiert, eine deutsche Identität zu retten". Das Oberverwaltungsgericht Münster verwies 2024 in seinem Urteil zur Verfassungsfeindlichkeit der AfD auf das "völkische Gesellschaftskonzept" in Teilen der Partei.
Demgegenüber konstruieren Hansen zufolge extremistische Strömungen der Linken ein "Opfer-Kollektiv", das unter anderem auch die islamistische und antisemitische Palästinenserorganisation Hamas einbeziehe und deren Gewalttaten gegen Juden relativiere.
AfD im Osten eine "erhebliche Gefahr" für die Demokratie
Die Experten sind sich einig, dass man im Fall der Linken von Landesverband zu Landesverband unterscheiden muss. Schroeder verweist darauf, dass die Linke in Berlin "in der Tat eine ganze Reihe von Persönlichkeiten und Spektren" in ihren Reihen habe, "die demokratietheoretisch hochumstritten sind". Anders als Berlin gilt zum Beispiel die Linke in den ostdeutschen Bundesländern als gemäßigt. In der Vergangenheit erwies sie sich als verlässlicher Regierungspartner.
Bei der AfD gebe es dagegen praktisch keinen moderaten Landesverband mehr, sagt Hendrik Hansen. Selbst die bislang relativ gemäßigte nordrhein-westfälische AfD ist inzwischen in einen internen Machtkampf verstrickt. Die AfD ist lediglich im Saarland und in Schleswig-Holstein kein Beobachtungsfall; in fünf Bundesländern gilt sie als gesichert rechtsextremistisch.
Demgegenüber tauchen aufseiten der Linken nur interne Strömungen hin und wieder in den Verfassungsschutzberichten auf, unter anderem der Jugendverband Solid. So nennt der nordrhein-westfälische Bericht für 2025 Solid zusammen mit den kommunistischen Parteien DKP und MLPD. Alle drei richteten sich "gegen wesentliche Bestandteile der freiheitlichen Grundordnung". Als Gesamtpartei wird die Linke in keinem Bericht erwähnt.
Hansen verweist darauf, dass die Verfassungsschutzberichte der politischen Entwicklung hinterherhinkten. Ob die Linke künftig stärker in den Berichten Berücksichtigung findet, wird sich zeigen.

content:
AfD und Linke Warum Extremismus-Vergleiche zu kurz greifen
SPD und Grüne laufen Sturm gegen die Gleichsetzung von AfD und der Linken durch CDU und CSU. Experten betonen deutliche Unterschiede, vor allem bei Ideologie und Bewertung des Verfassungsschutzes.
"Deutschlandtag" der Jungen Union. Auf dem Bildschirm hinter dem Podium prangt in riesigen Lettern: "Nie wieder ist jetzt". Eine Parole, die vor der Wiederkehr des Nationalsozialismus warnt. Flankiert wird der Spruch von einem Wahlkampfaufkleber der Berliner Linken, der für die Spitzenkandidatin Elif Eralp wirbt, und dem Bild eines Vermummten mit Palästinensertuch. Die Botschaft: Die bei der Wahl zum Abgeordnetenhaus siegreiche Linke sei extremistisch und antisemitisch - und somit zu vergleichen mit dem Nationalsozialismus.
"Einen solchen Vergleich halte ich für daneben", sagt Extremismusforscher Hendrik Hansen im Gespräch mit tagesschau.de. Er lehrt an der Hochschule des Bundes für öffentliche Verwaltung in der Abteilung Verfassungsschutz.
Der Politikwissenschaftler Wolfgang Schroeder erklärt die Aktion im tagesschau.de-Interview mit der Defensive, in der sich die Unionsparteien derzeit befänden: "Aus dieser Lage heraus versucht man, neue Gegnerbezüge aufzubauen, um die Reihen zu schließen und zu verhindern, dass es zu einem Bündnis zwischen SPD, Grünen und Linkspartei kommt." Schroeder lehrt an der Uni Kassel und war Mitglied der SPD-Grundwertekommission.
Extremismus: Alles in einen Topf?
Extremismus ist ein politischer Begriff, mit dem man Gegner diskreditieren kann. CDU und CSU sind mit dem Vorwurf konfrontiert, die Linke mit der AfD in einen "Extremismustopf" zu werfen und damit Unterschiede zwischen beiden Parteien einzuebnen. Er finde "es schwer zu ertragen, was die Union derzeit aufführt", entgegnet Bremens Bürgermeister Andreas Bovenschulte (SPD). CDU und CSU wirft er Relativierung vor. Die Abgrenzung zu den "Verfassungsfeinden" der AfD werde "verwischt".
"CDU und CSU müssen enger zusammenstehen denn je", hatte CDU-Chef und Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz kürzlich auf dem CSU-Parteitag gesagt. Die Union werde von "Extremisten" von ganz rechts und von ganz links bekämpft, womit Merz AfD und Linke meinte.
In der Wissenschaft bezeichnet Extremismus das, was sich außerhalb der Grenzen der freiheitlich-demokratischen Grundordnung bewegt. Experten lehnen politische Pauschalurteile ab und plädieren für eine differenzierte Sicht. Hinzu kommt: "Wir haben es bei AfD und der Linken mit Parteien zu tun, die nicht insgesamt extremistisch sind", sagt Hansen.
Hohe Zahl an Rechtsextremisten bei der AfD
Bei der AfD lässt sich der Anteil der Extremisten recht gut überblicken, weil sie großflächig vom Verfassungsschutz beobachtet wird. Die Behörde zählte 2025 28.000 Rechtsextremisten in der Partei - bei einer Mitgliederzahl von damals 70.000.
Im Falle der Linken, sagt Hansen, könnten keine genauen Angaben gemacht werden. Die Linke sei "nicht mehr die eines Gregor Gysi", sagte der CSU-Chef und bayerische Ministerpräsident Markus Söder vor Kurzem. Die Partei sei "eine radikale Linke" geworden, eine Entwicklung, die auch Experten wie Hendrik Hansen erkennen.
Der Grund: In den vergangenen zwei Jahren habe sich die Mitgliederzahl "mehr als verdoppelt", sagt der Extremismusforscher. "Und diese neuen Mitglieder, da gibt es schon erste Anhaltspunkte", seien "deutlich radikaler als die bisherigen Mitglieder". Man müsse also davon ausgehen, "dass die heutige Linke nicht mehr die Linke ist von Dietmar Bartsch oder Bodo Ramelow". Radikale Haltungen können sich allerdings im Rahmen der freiheitlichen Demokratie bewegen. Ob die Partei durch den Mitgliederzulauf auch extremistischer wird, steht also noch nicht fest.
Unterschiedliche Weltanschauungen
Für Wolfgang Schroeder zielen sowohl die Linke als auch die AfD darauf, "das demokratische Zentrum" von den Rändern her unter Druck zu setzen. Allerdings geschehe das auf sehr unterschiedlichen "weltanschaulichen, soziologischen und politischen Grundlagen". Anders als die AfD akzeptiere die Linke "grundsätzlich die Gleichheit der Menschenwürde".
Hansen verweist auf die "ethnokulturelle Politik" der AfD, "die sich darauf fokussiert, eine deutsche Identität zu retten". Das Oberverwaltungsgericht Münster verwies 2024 in seinem Urteil zur Verfassungsfeindlichkeit der AfD auf das "völkische Gesellschaftskonzept" in Teilen der Partei.

title: Електролітні напої потрібні не всім: кому популярний тренд може зашкодити
content_c:
Електролітні напої потрібні не всім: кому популярний тренд може зашкодити
Напої з електролітами можуть допомогти після тривалих інтенсивних навантажень, однак щоденне вживання без потреби має ризики.
Популярні електролітні напої не є необхідними для більшості людей у повсякденному житті. Деякі з них містять багато натрію, калію, цукру або кофеїну, тому їх варто обирати з урахуванням стану здоров’я та фізичних навантажень.
Про це йдеться в роз’ясненні Гарвардської школи громадського здоров’я.
Електроліти — це мінерали, які допомагають регулювати баланс рідини, роботу м’язів і нервової системи. Організм втрачає їх, зокрема, з потом.
Спеціальні напої можуть бути корисними після тривалих інтенсивних тренувань або за значних втрат рідини. Водночас для навантажень тривалістю до години невисокої інтенсивності за помірної температури зазвичай достатньо звичайної води. Збалансоване харчування також допомагає поповнювати запас електролітів.
Особливої обережності потребують люди із захворюваннями нирок. Як пояснює Національний інститут діабету, захворювань органів травлення та нирок США, за хронічної хвороби нирки гірше підтримують баланс солей і мінералів. Потреба в обмеженні натрію та інших речовин залежить від стану людини.
Надлишок калію також може становити небезпеку для людей із хронічними захворюваннями нирок або тих, хто приймає певні ліки. Водночас немає підстав стверджувати, що калій зі звичайних продуктів і напоїв шкодить здоровим людям із нормальною функцією нирок.
Нагадаємо, що раніше ми писали про те, як приготувати природний електролітний напій із буряка: рецепт олімпійських атлетів
