title: «Азов» о скандале под Киевом: саботаж в тылу
content_c:
Скандал вокруг дома под Киевом, где, как писали в сети, пытали военных, отвечает интересам России. Ранее командующий Национальной гвардией Украины Александр Пивненко пояснил, что в этом частном доме находился временный пункт пребывания военных. Саботаж в тылу устраивают люди, которые не служат и не помогают армии, заявил командующий группировкой войск «Азов», бригадный генерал Денис Прокопенко.
«В настоящее время люди, которые никоим образом не причастны к защите страны, не служат в армии и не помогают силам обороны, занимаются саботажем в тылу, дискредитируют украинских военных и создают выгодную для России картинку. Россияне заинтересованы в расколе украинского общества и армии, дестабилизации ситуации в Украине и очернении образа военного. То, что происходит в информационном пространстве вокруг событий в Петропавловской Борщаговке, удовлетворяет все эти запросы россиян. В этой ситуации нужно либо защищать страну на фронте, либо помогать фронту в тылу, а не устраивать провокации и играть на руку врагу. «Азов» уже 13 лет защищает Украину и не позволит никому запятнать честь войска», — добавил он.
В 1-м корпусе НГУ «Азов» сообщили, что 2 ноября в соцсетях распространилась непроверенная информация о якобы пытках военных на территории временного пункта дислокации воинской части 3121. У здания собрались люди и требовали выдать им мобилизованных. Получив отказ, они заблокировали работу пункта и пытались несанкционированно проникнуть внутрь. Генерал-майор Александр Пивненко лично провел родственников некоторых военных в здание и показал условия, в которых находятся мобилизованные и те, кого задержали после самовольного оставления части (СОЧ).
Четверо задержанных после СОЧ имели травмы, поэтому их отправили в госпиталь на обследование. Командование НГУ совместно с правоохранителями взяло под контроль расследование. Если подтвердятся незаконные насильственные действия, виновные понесут наказание. В корпусе решительно осудили неправомерные действия в отношении военных, но предостерегли людей от препятствования работе воинских частей и призвали доверять официальным сообщениям Сил обороны и правоохранительных органов. Для командования личный состав — самая большая ценность. «Азов» бережет жизнь и здоровье военных не только на фронте, но и в тылу.
Министр Иван Выговский поручил провести служебное расследование. Условия, в которых находились военные, будут проверять Государственное бюро расследований и офис военного омбудсмена. На место прибыл и глава офиса президента Кирилл Буданов. Он сказал людям возле дома, что заложников там нет, и пообещал выяснить, избили ли 14-летнего подростка, которого нашли на территории.
Тревогу по поводу «заложников» подняла женщина, представившаяся владелицей клиники «Мед-престиж». Журналисты выяснили, что эта клиника не работает с 2023 года, а машину скорой помощи, которая приехала на место, владелец продал еще в 2024-м.
О том, почему военные дезертируют со службы и что с этим должно делать государство, в статье ZN.UA «СОЧ, дезертирство и уклонение от службы во время войны: наказывать или прощать?» пишет кандидат физико-математических наук, юрист, директор аналитико-исследовательского центра «Институт города» Александр Сергиенко.
description: Командующий корпусом заявил, что осуждает насилие в отношении военнослужащих, и призвал не препятствовать работе воинских частей.

О том, почему военные дезертируют со службы и что с этим должно делать государство, в статье ZN.UA «СОЧ, дезертирство и уклонение от службы во время войны: наказывать или прощать?» пишет кандидат физико-математических наук, юрист, директор аналитико-исследовательского центра «Институт города» Александр Сергиенко.

title: Переговори України та Росії за посередництва США відбудуться в Абу-Дабі 10-11 листопада – Віткофф
content_c:
США 10-11 листопада виступатимуть посередниками на переговорах робочого рівня між Україною та Росією в Абу-Дабі, повідомив спецпосланець президента США Стів Віткофф.
"Обговорення зосередяться на питаннях повоєнної безпеки, деескалації, гуманітарних заходах, а також подальших кроках на шляху до миру", – написав він у соцмережі Х.
Крім того, цього тижня в Брюсселі американські переговорники зустрінуться з представниками Франції, Німеччини, Великої Британії, ЄС та НАТО. За словами Віткоффа, вони обговорять гарантії безпеки для України, архітектуру повоєнної безпеки в Європі та економічні можливості для підтримки відбудови України.
"Ми прагнемо розвинути прогрес, досягнутий у Києві, Осло та Санкт-Петербурзі, задля укладення всеосяжної та довготривалої мирної угоди", – додав спецпосланець.

title: Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences
content_c:
Popular Australian children's author jailed over child exploitation offences
- Published
Australian children's author Craig Silvey has been sentenced to seven months in jail for possessing and distributing child exploitation material.
In handing down her sentence, Judge Hayley Cormann called Silvey's actions "repulsive" and "degrading".
In January, Silvey was arrested after police raided his home in Western Australia and seized several electronic devices. In May, the 44-year-old pleaded guilty to possessing and distributing child exploitation material and in October he was jailed pending his sentencing.
The father-of-three is best known for his award-winning young adult novel Jasper Jones and children's book Runt, both of which were later made into movies.
"You have devastated and betrayed the trust of thousands of people, and you've let entire communities down," Cormann said on Monday, according to WA Today.
Police said Silvey had online chats, in which he discussed child exploitation, open at the moment they turned up to raid his house.
In them, the court heard, Silvey had described himself as "extremely open minded" and "obsessed with taboos".
He'd discussed his sexual interest in children as young as five with another user of a pornography site, and detectives found images and videos of other adults abusing children on his devices.
He was initially charged with four offences, but prosecutors later dropped two.
Prosecutors said Silvey contributed to the "cycle of abuse" victimising the children in the images, and argued a harsh sentence was required.
However, the author's defence lawyer said he did not have a "sexual interest in children" and was seeking out "the most depraved material" as a form of "emotional" self harm.
"His behaviour provided temporary relief from psychological agitation," Eloise Barker said.
She said Silvey had displayed genuine remorse for his offending, and that his high profile and the resulting media scrutiny - which led to his former partner and children relocating interstate - was already a form of punishment.
Judge Cormann did not accept many of her arguments, and said Silvey's offending was extremely serious.
"These children, the victims of this type of offending, are real and are traumatised… the consequences for them from these abuses are long lasting and very, very traumatic," she said, according to The Australian.
Silvey was sentenced to seven months in jail, backdated to 22 October. He is eligible for parole.
Silvey's coming-of-age novel Jasper Jones sold more than half a million copies and was awarded the Book of the Year Award by the nation's peak publishing body in 2010.
The novel, set in Western Australia with two teenage boys as the main characters, was also shortlisted for the International Dublin Literary Awards and the Miles Franklin Literary Award.
It was later turned into a film starring Toni Collette and Hugo Weaving in 2017 as well as a stage play.
Another of his acclaimed works is 2022's Runt, about the adventures of an 11-year-old girl and her stray dog and set in the Australia outback. It was also adapted for film in 2024, featuring Celeste Barber.
Since his arrest, publishers and book shops have pulled his works from shelves while schools in some states have removed Jasper's books from teaching lists.

title: Russell Brand is not a ‘psychopath who rapes people and thinks it’s normal’, court told
content_c:
Russell Brand is not a “psychopath who rapes people and thinks it’s normal” and is respectful when women say no, a court has heard.
In his closing speech at Southwark crown court, Brand’s barrister, Ian Winter KC, questioned why Brand’s accusers had not fought back when they were allegedly raped, saying “not one of them resisted or screamed or even tried to leave”.
Winter said allegations about the comedian’s sexual conduct in 2023 had “poisoned the wells” of justice. He also said there had been “monstrous delays” in the women in the criminal trial coming forward to police.
He also questioned why Brand had been accused of “only three rapes in 10 years” out of all the women he had slept with.
He said: “It is an extremely curious feature of this case that out of the many, many women that Mr Brand had sex with during this period only three of them say they did not consent to anal, oral or vaginal sex.”
Brand, 51, is accused of seven offences, including rape and sexual assault, against six women in allegations spanning 10 years from 1999. He denies all the charges.
Winter began his closing speech by reciting an 1864 quote from the theologian and philosopher John Henry Newman, saying: “What I insist upon here, now that I am bringing this portion of my discussion to a close, is this unmanly attempt of his, in his concluding pages, to cut the ground from under my feet … this I call poisoning the wells.”
He said the 2023 reporting of sexual misconduct allegations in a Channel 4 Dispatches documentary and Times and Sunday Times stories had “poisoned the well of justice” in Brand’s case by prompting the women to come forward with accusations afterwards.
Winter told jurors: “They poisoned the wells in the hope and intention that other people come forward and make allegations against him.”
In her closing speech on Friday, the prosecutor, Riel Karmy-Jones KC, denied that the 2023 reporting had had “such a subliminal hold on the minds of six perfectly rational women” to make them “invent, reimagine, recharacterise, recast” their encounters with the comedian.
Winter told jurors on Monday that Brand had an “immense amount of sex” and none of it was unlawful.
“The question for you is, can you possibly be sure in this case that out of the many, many women who voluntarily had sex with Mr Brand between 1999 and 2009, he raped just three of them?” he asked.
“Living a highly promiscuous life is entirely lawful however morally distasteful you may find it,” he continued. “Disgusting, distasteful, immoral – who cares? It’s irrelevant to your consideration.”
Winter said another “curious feature” of the case was that the three rape complainants had alleged Brand was “normal” after the alleged incidents.
“That, we suggest, is something that simply cannot have occurred if he is guilty,” the barrister said. “He obviously genuinely believed that they were consenting because that’s the only thing that would explain why his behaviour was normal.”
The barrister said there was “no evidence he is some sort of psychopath who rapes people and thinks it’s normal”.
He also questioned why the women had not screamed, kicked out or slapped Brand during the alleged attacks. He asked why a woman who accuses Brand of anal rape “didn’t just roll over and kick out in any way” and said she “didn’t scream or resist or call out”. He also questioned why a woman who says she was orally raped did not “slap [Brand] in the face” and suggested she had not “sufficiently” resisted.
He also questioned how none of the women came forward during the #MeToo movement.
Winter said: “How is it that it’s only three out of the many, many women, how is it that not even these ones, not even these allegations on this indictment came to light during #MeToo?
“Many women were questioning whether they had a bad experience sexually at the hands of a famous person. It could not have been more publicised.
“How is it that not one of them thought what happened to them involved a crime during the #MeToo movement?”
The court has heard the earliest allegation dated back to 1999, when a woman accused Brand of raping her after he had performed in a fringe cabaret event during the Labour party conference in Bournemouth.
The woman told the court Brand had left his email address after raping her, while asking her if she was enjoying herself.
Winter said the woman was not a “naive and wilting flower” as he questioned her account of events. “You would have to be a psychopath to be raping someone and asking them if they were enjoying it,” Winter said. “He [Brand] said he was trying to please her but he wasn’t successful.”
Winter said rapists did not try to please their victims. He also said Brand respected when a woman said no, and sought “approbation and adoration” from women.
“He respects it when a woman says no so that makes him someone who is not a rapist,” Winter said. “He was seeking the approval in the sex, it’s the approval, it’s the ‘Yes I will have sex with you’, and that’s what he said in his evidence.”
Brand is accused of three counts of rape and three counts of sexual assault. On Tuesday, an allegation of indecent assault was changed to a charge of attempted indecent assault. Brand has pleaded not guilty to all charges.
The trial continues.

title: India news: Gandhi vows to step up pressure on Modi at protest rally
content_c:
India news: Gandhi vows to step up pressure on Modi at protest rally
Published November 2, 2026last updated November 2, 2026
What you need to know
- Thousands attended the Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc's rally against top poll official Gyanesh Kumar
- Authorities in Delhi collected more than €60,000 in fines during an anti-pollution drive
- Protests against Indian government's plan to build a massive dam in northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh have intensified
Here is a roundup of the biggest headlines from India on Monday, November 2.
Thank you for reading
This is all we got for you today. We will be back with more news from India tomorrow.
Amitabh Bachchan meets fans from behind bulletproof shield after bomb threat
Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan made his regular weekly appearance on Sunday outside his Mumbai home, but this time from behind a bullet proof glass with heavy security, following a bomb threat.
Bachchan was seen waving to his fans with his son Abhishek Bachchan standing beside him.
The tightened security comes after a threatening email was reported to Mumbai police last week.
Reportedly, the email was sent to a school in the Bandra-Kurla Complex area in Mumbai.
The email allegedly threatened to target Bachchan's house with a bomb and named October 31 and November 27 as possible dates for attacks.
The police has launched an investigation and it is still to be ascertained whether the email specifically mentioned Bachchan's residence.
Cyclone Murasu likely to make landfall in Andhra Pradesh
After cyclone Arnab, India is bracing for cyclone Murasu which is moving along the coast of the southeastern state of Andhra Pradesh, packing winds ranging between 100 and 120 kilometers per hour (75 miles per hour).
According to the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD), Murasu is expected to make landfall on Tuesday.
Thousands of people have been evacuated along India's eastern coast. Schools and colleges have been closed as heavy rainfall is expected.
Meanwhile, the IMD has issued an orange alert for six districts and a yellow alert for five districts in the neighboring state of Telangana. An orange alert means heavy rainfall of 11-20 cm.
IMD has also warned of the possibility of Murasu intensifying further into a very severe cyclonic storm before reaching the Andhra Pradesh coastline.
Temporary shutdown announced in Arunachal Pradesh over controversial dam project
A local youth organization, protesting against the dam construction in northeastern state of Arunachal Pradesh's Siang district, announced a 36-hour long shutdown, local newspaper the Assam Tribune reported on Monday.
The protests over the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), an 11,000–11,200 MW mega-dam planned on the Siang River, have intensified in recent day.
Protesters burnt tires while bus services and other public transport facilities remained shut in the district, according to the report.
The state wing of Indian National Congress has demanded the scrapping of the proposed dam project.
The party said, "Different groups but one voice; different organisations but one collective resolve – Stop SUMP, Save Siang."
Locals are demanding the release of protesters arrested for opposing the dam construction, deployment of security forces and suspension of ongoing surveys for the proposed mega hydropower project on the Siang river.
The dam, envisioned as India's biggest hydropower project, has been facing opposition from sections of the indigenous Adi community over concerns about displacement, loss of agricultural land, identity and culture.
Delhi's anti-pollution drive collects €64,500 on first day
With pollution levels soaring as winter is arriving across northern India, authorities collected fines amounting to nearly €64,500 on the first day of the anti-pollution drive on Sunday.
Nearly 15,000 vehicles were checked by authorities, while more than 1,500 vehicles were sent back to Delhi's borders and more than 500 tickets were issued for failing to comply with the Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) norms.
The Delhi government has imposed several restrictions as the time when pollution levels peak in Delhi approaches.
The authorities in Delhi have imposed a ban on non-Delhi vehicles that do not meet emission standards from November 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027.
Vehicles running on compressed natural gas (CNG), electric vehicles (EVs) and those involved in essential services were exempted from the restrictions, according to a report by Indian news channel NDTV.
According to the report, 300 construction sites were inspected, of which 32 were reported to be violating dust control norms.
Rahul Gandhi steps up attacks on Modi, Shah at INDIA bloc rally
Leader of the opposition Indian National Congress (INC) party, Rahul Gandhi, dialed up the pressure against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah as thousands joined the INDIA bloc rally held at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, demanding India's election chief Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
Addressing the crowd, Gandhi said, "Narendra Modi ji and Amit Shah ji, understand this: after Gyanesh Kumar, we will stand against you and don’t forget that for the vote chori (vote theft) you have done, there will be legal action against you and Narendra Modi."
Gandhi said the resignation of Kumar as the Chief Election Commission would be "the first step to getting the country on the right track."
He alleged that "without Gyanesh Kumar, Narendra Modi wouldn’t have become PM and Amit Shah wouldn’t be home minister."
The rally follows a series of protests in more than a month against Kumar and the controversial mass voter roll revision, which removed more than 130 million names from voter lists.
Opposition parties have alleged the exercise disproportionately affected Muslims and other minorities.
The rally was attended by several opposition leaders including senior INC leaders Sonia Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge along with leaders of regional parties such as Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Mehbooba Mufti, and Tejashwi Yadav.
Welcome to our coverage
Hi! This is Midhat from DW's New Delhi bureau bringing you all that's creating a buzz in India.
The chill is slowly settling in Delhi's air, so is pollution and protest. It is that time of the year when the pleasant temperatures make going out in Delhi an absolute delight but the air quality keeps worsening with AQI already crossing the 400-mark.
It is also turning out to be a season of protest in Delhi. The opposition alliance INDIA bloc, building on the preceding protests, held a massive rally yesterday at the Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, demanding the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar.
Leader of the opposition, Rahul Gandhi, has stepped up his pressure campaign against the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party-led government and said after Kumar, the opposition will stand against PM Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.
Stay tuned with us as we bring you all this and more from India.
description: Rahul Gandhi said the removal of election chief Gyanesh Kumar will be the first step to getting the country on the right track. Follow DW for more.

The dam, envisioned as India's biggest hydropower project, has been facing opposition from sections of the indigenous Adi community over concerns about displacement, loss of agricultural land, identity and culture.
Delhi's anti-pollution drive collects €64,500 on first day
With pollution levels soaring as winter is arriving across northern India, authorities collected fines amounting to nearly €64,500 on the first day of the anti-pollution drive on Sunday.
Nearly 15,000 vehicles were checked by authorities, while more than 1,500 vehicles were sent back to Delhi's borders and more than 500 tickets were issued for failing to comply with the Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) norms.
The Delhi government has imposed several restrictions as the time when pollution levels peak in Delhi approaches.
The authorities in Delhi have imposed a ban on non-Delhi vehicles that do not meet emission standards from November 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027.
Vehicles running on compressed natural gas (CNG), electric vehicles (EVs) and those involved in essential services were exempted from the restrictions, according to a report by Indian news channel NDTV.
According to the report, 300 construction sites were inspected, of which 32 were reported to be violating dust control norms.
Rahul Gandhi steps up attacks on Modi, Shah at INDIA bloc rally
Leader of the opposition Indian National Congress (INC) party, Rahul Gandhi, dialed up the pressure against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah as thousands joined the INDIA bloc rally held at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, demanding India's election chief Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
Addressing the crowd, Gandhi said, "Narendra Modi ji and Amit Shah ji, understand this: after Gyanesh Kumar, we will stand against you and don’t forget that for the vote chori (vote theft) you have done, there will be legal action against you and Narendra Modi."
Gandhi said the resignation of Kumar as the Chief Election Commission would be "the first step to getting the country on the right track."
He alleged that "without Gyanesh Kumar, Narendra Modi wouldn’t have become PM and Amit Shah wouldn’t be home minister."
The rally follows a series of protests in more than a month against Kumar and the controversial mass voter roll revision, which removed more than 130 million names from voter lists.
Opposition parties have alleged the exercise disproportionately affected Muslims and other minorities.
The rally was attended by several opposition leaders including senior INC leaders Sonia Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge along with leaders of regional parties such as Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Mehbooba Mufti, and Tejashwi Yadav.
Welcome to our coverage
Hi! This is Midhat from DW's New Delhi bureau bringing you all that's creating a buzz in India.
The chill is slowly settling in Delhi's air, so is pollution and protest. It is that time of the year when the pleasant temperatures make going out in Delhi an absolute delight but the air quality keeps worsening with AQI already crossing the 400-mark.
It is also turning out to be a season of protest in Delhi. The opposition alliance INDIA bloc, building on the preceding protests, held a massive rally yesterday at the Ramlila Maidan in Delhi, demanding the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar.
Leader of the opposition, Rahul Gandhi, has stepped up his pressure campaign against the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party-led government and said after Kumar, the opposition will stand against PM Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah.
Stay tuned with us as we bring you all this and more from India.

title: Podcast »Im Verhör«: Korrupte Justiz (2): Der letzte Bluff des V-Manns - SPIEGEL TV
content_c:
Podcast »Im Verhör«: Korrupte Justiz (2): Der letzte Bluff des V-Manns
Der Jurist hat dem »Typen« Geld für einen großen Deal geliehen. Doch der zahlt nicht zurück. Benjamin D. ist so tief verstrickt in seine kriminellen Geschäfte, dass er die verfassungsmäßige Ordnung zu wahren, wie er mal geschworen hatte, längst vergessen hat. Jemanden kaltzumachen, zu töten, scheint möglich.
Was der kriminelle Advokat aber nicht weiß: Der säumige Geschäftspartner ist ein Spitzel der Polizei, ein sogenannter »Snitch«: Aleksander Kolundzic wird als Vertrauensperson bei der Frankfurter Dienststelle K30 geführt. 
Unter mysteriösen Bedingungen kommt der Spitzel, dessen Ableben der Rechtsanwalt Benjamin D. herbeifantasiert, in Spanien tatsächlich zu Tode. Davon existieren sogar Kryptohandy-Fotos. Darauf sitzt Kolundzic gefesselt auf einem Stuhl, Oberkörper und Arme mit Frischhaltefolie fixiert. 20 Stunden wird er in Marbella gefoltert. Nach seinem Tod löscht sein VP-Führer das Handy, auf dem er mit seiner Vertrauensperson kommunizierte.
Protokolle der Unterwelt
Claas Meyer-Heuer
Ein Staatsanwalt, der ein Koks-Kartell mit geheimen Informationen versorgt. 
Ein Rechtsanwalt, der aus dem Gerichtssaal heraus im großen Stil mit Drogen dealt. 
Das ist nicht etwa der Plot einer neuen Streamingserie, auch stammen die Geschichten nicht aus einem fernen Narco-Staat: Sie spielen in Deutschland. Wenn die Verbrecher nicht so offen über ihre Kryptohandys kommuniziert hätten, wären diese Fälle wahrscheinlich nie ans Tageslicht gekommen. 
In der vierteiligen Podcast-Serie enthüllt SPIEGEL-TV-Reporter Claas Meyer-Heuer, wer der Mörder ist. Der Bestsellerautor hat Tausende Kryptohandy-Nachrichten studiert. Der Fall des korrupten Juristen und dem Polizeiskandal stammt aus seinem neuen Buch »Protokolle der Unterwelt«. En détail analysiert er gemeinsam mit Host Christina Pohl die Chats der Organisierten Kriminalität.

Und abonnieren Sie dann den Podcast, um keine Folge zu verpassen. Wenn Sie lieber eine andere Podcast-App nutzen, suchen Sie dort einfach nach »Im Verhör«. Den Link zum RSS-Feed finden Sie hier .

title: Ministerin Reiche legt ersten Entwurf für Spritpreisdeckel-Gesetz vor
content_c:
Maßnahme gegen hohe Kraftstoffpreise Erster Entwurf zum Spritpreisdeckel liegt vor
Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche ist keine Befürworterin eines Spritpreisdeckels. Doch die Koalition will das Instrument einführen. Nun liegt ein erster Gesetzentwurf ihres Ministeriums vor. Er beschreibt, wann der Spritpreisdeckel gelten soll und wann nicht.
Das Bundeswirtschaftsministerium von Katherina Reiche (CDU) hat einen ersten Entwurf zum geplanten Spritpreisdeckel fertiggestellt. Der Gesetzentwurf für ein "Kraftstoffhöchstpreisgesetz", der auch dem ARD-Hauptstadtstudio vorliegt, sieht vor, dass die Bundesregierung "im äußersten Notfall als Kriseninstrument" per Verordnung einen Höchstpreis für die Abgabe von Kraftstoffen an öffentlichen Tankstellen festlegen kann.
Ein Preisdeckel würde demnach erst gelten, wenn Benzin und Diesel in drei aufeinanderfolgenden Wochen jeweils um mehr als fünf Prozentpunkte über den durchschnittlichen Preissteigerungen der übrigen EU-Staaten liegen. Grundlage dafür sollen Zahlen der EU-Kommission sein.
Zudem soll die Höchstpreisregelung auf maximal drei Monate befristet sein. Bei einer drohenden Gefährdung der Versorgungssicherheit könne ihre Anwendung ausgesetzt werden.
Laut Entwurf sollen die Bundesländer abweichende Höchstpreise festlegen können, um den jeweiligen Bedingungen vor Ort Rechnung zu tragen.
Kraftstofflieferungen sollen wirtschaftlich bleiben
Aus dem Ministerium hieß es gegenüber der Nachrichtenagentur dpa: "Werden Höchstpreise zu niedrig angesetzt, können Kraftstofflieferungen unwirtschaftlich werden. Importe könnten ausbleiben und Versorgungsengpässe entstehen." Es solle sichergestellt werden, dass Kraftstofflieferungen auch bei einer staatlichen Preisbegrenzung wirtschaftlich möglich bleiben.
Kritik aus Reihen der SPD
Aus den Reihen der SPD kommt Kritik am Entwurf des Ministeriums. Der Vorschlag sei "ein Spritpreisdeckel-Verhinderungsgesetz", sagte die saarländische Ministerpräsidentin Anke Rehlinger dem Tagesspiegel. "Wenn unzulässige Preisanstiege erst drei Wochen andauern sollen, bevor Reiche handelt, ist niemandem geholfen."
Der wirtschaftspolitische Sprecher der SPD im Bundestag, Sebastian Roloff, fordert, das Konzept nachzubessern. Das sei nicht, was die Koalition vereinbart habe. Es brauche einen Spritpreisdeckel, der kurzfristig die Menschen und Unternehmen entlaste.
Mit dem neuen Instrument des Spritpreisdeckels will die Bundesregierung auf die zuletzt stark erhöhten Benzin- und Dieselpreise reagieren. Der Entwurf befindet sich in der sogenannten Frühkoordinierung - das ist der erste Schritt der Abstimmung innerhalb der Bundesregierung. Zuerst hatten das Portal The Pioneer und das Handelsblatt über die Pläne berichtet.
Reiche warnte im September vor Spritpreisdeckel
Mitte September hatten sich die Spitzen der schwarz-roten Koalition darauf verständigt, Gespräche mit der Mineralölwirtschaft zu führen - mit dem Ziel, spätestens zum 1. Januar 2027 einen Spritpreisdeckel nach dem Vorbild Luxemburgs oder Belgiens einzuführen. Ende Dezember läuft der "Tankrabatt" aus. Eine Verlängerung wird in dem Entwurf wegen der Haushaltslage ausgeschlossen.
Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche hatte sich ursprünglich gegen den Spritpreisdeckel ausgesprochen. Ein solcher Deckel schwäche die mittelständische Raffineriewirtschaft, hatte Reiche im September gesagt.
Mit Informationen von Philipp Eckstein, ARD-Hauptstadtstudio

title: Британія, Італія та Японія створюють винищувач нового покоління: що про нього відомо
content_c:
Британія, Італія та Японія створюють винищувач нового покоління: що про нього відомо
Новий бойовий літак розробляють із застосуванням штучного інтелекту та технологій малопомітності, а його надходження на озброєння планують від 2035 року.
Велика Британія, Італія та Японія спільно розробляють бойовий літак шостого покоління в межах програми Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP).
Про це йдеться в повідомленні британського уряду.
За задумом розробників, винищувач використовуватиме технології малопомітності, штучний інтелект і передові цифрові системи. У складі британських Повітряних сил він має діяти разом із літаками Typhoon, F-35 та автономними системами.
Цільовий термін надходження нового літака на озброєння — 2035 рік.
Промислову співпрацю забезпечує спільне підприємство Edgewing, створене британською BAE Systems, італійською Leonardo та японською Japan Aircraft Industrial Enhancement Co. Кожен із партнерів має рівну частку — 33,3%.
Програму GCAP започаткували у грудні 2022 року. Вона об’єднує уряди та оборонні підприємства трьох країн для створення бойової авіації, здатної протидіяти майбутнім загрозам.
У липні 2026 року партнери уклали контракт на 4,6 млрд фунтів стерлінгів для наступного етапу проєктування літака. Він передбачає визначення ключових вимог і проведення випробувань. Фінансування спільно забезпечують три держави.
Нагадаємо, що раніше Велика Британія одночасно розгорнула три атомні підводні човни: такого не було роками
Нетипове розгортання відбувається на тлі посилення російської військової активності біля британських берегів.

title: События в Петропавловской Борщаговке: в корпусе "Азов" осудили неправомерные действия в отношении военнослужащих
content_c:
В первом корпусе Национальной гвардии "Азов" прокомментировали инцидент, произошедший в Петропавловской Борщаговке в Киевской области. Там подтвердили, что четверо из военнослужащих, задержанных после самовольного оставления части, имели травмы. Их отправили в госпиталь для проведения обследования, говорится в официальном заявлении корпуса в Telegram.
В корпусе отметили, что 2 ноября в соцсетях начала распространяться непроверенная информация о якобы пытках военнослужащих на территории временного пункта дислокации в/ч 3121 Национальной гвардии Украины, которая относится к 1-му корпусу НГУ “Азов”.
В заявлении подчеркивается, что командование НГУ в сотрудничестве с правоохранительными органами взяло под контроль расследование ситуации. В “Азове” заверили, что в случае незаконных насильственных действий на территории военного городка виновные понесут справедливое наказание.
“Для командования 1-го корпуса НГУ «Азов» личный состав — это самая большая ценность. «Азов» бережет жизнь и здоровье своих военнослужащих в чрезвычайно сложных условиях на фронте. Подразделение руководствуется теми же принципами и в тылу: это касается всех военнослужащих корпуса и не зависит от продолжительности их службы”, — говорится в заявлении.
Командование 1-го корпуса НГУ «Азов» решительно осудило неправомерные действия в отношении военнослужащих. В то же время в корпусе предостерегли от препятствования работе воинских частей и призвали доверять официальным сообщениям Сил обороны Украины и правоохранительных органов.
Напомним, что сообщение о незаконном удержании военных в доме в Петропавловской Борщаговке распространила 49-летняя Валентина Молодая. Она представилась владелицей клиники «Мед-престиж» и, по словам Бориса Бреуса из полиции Киевской области, вызвала правоохранителей. Журналисты выяснили, что компания не работает с 2023 года, а автомобиль скорой помощи продали в 2024-м.
Вечером 2 ноября возле дома вспыхнули столкновения. Люди разгромили полицейскую машину и автобус, на котором привезли спецназовцев. На этом автобусе также должны были вывезти с места происшествия мужчин, которых, по этим данным, удерживали в доме.
В Нацгвардии заявили, что назначат служебное расследование по данному инциденту.
description: «Азов» заботится о здоровье своих военнослужащих на фронте и руководствуется теми же принципами и в тылу.
content:
В первом корпусе Национальной гвардии "Азов" прокомментировали инцидент, произошедший в Петропавловской Борщаговке в Киевской области. Там подтвердили, что четверо из военнослужащих, задержанных после самовольного оставления части, имели травмы. Их отправили в госпиталь для проведения обследования, говорится в официальном заявлении корпуса в Telegram.
В корпусе отметили, что 2 ноября в соцсетях начала распространяться непроверенная информация о якобы пытках военнослужащих на территории временного пункта дислокации в/ч 3121 Национальной гвардии Украины, которая относится к 1-му корпусу НГУ “Азов”.
В заявлении подчеркивается, что командование НГУ в сотрудничестве с правоохранительными органами взяло под контроль расследование ситуации. В “Азове” заверили, что в случае незаконных насильственных действий на территории военного городка виновные понесут справедливое наказание.
“Для командования 1-го корпуса НГУ «Азов» личный состав — это самая большая ценность. «Азов» бережет жизнь и здоровье своих военнослужащих в чрезвычайно сложных условиях на фронте. Подразделение руководствуется теми же принципами и в тылу: это касается всех военнослужащих корпуса и не зависит от продолжительности их службы”, — говорится в заявлении.
Командование 1-го корпуса НГУ «Азов» решительно осудило неправомерные действия в отношении военнослужащих. В то же время в корпусе предостерегли от препятствования работе воинских частей и призвали доверять официальным сообщениям Сил обороны Украины и правоохранительных органов.
Напомним, что сообщение о незаконном удержании военных в доме в Петропавловской Борщаговке распространила 49-летняя Валентина Молодая. Она представилась владелицей клиники «Мед-престиж» и, по словам Бориса Бреуса из полиции Киевской области, вызвала правоохранителей. Журналисты выяснили, что компания не работает с 2023 года, а автомобиль скорой помощи продали в 2024-м.
Вечером 2 ноября возле дома вспыхнули столкновения. Люди разгромили полицейскую машину и автобус, на котором привезли спецназовцев. На этом автобусе также должны были вывезти с места происшествия мужчин, которых, по этим данным, удерживали в доме.
В Нацгвардии заявили, что назначат служебное расследование по данному инциденту.

title: Shabana Mahmood softens immigration plans in face of cabinet backlash
content_c:
Shabana Mahmood rowed back on her most hardline plans to make care workers wait 15 years for settlement in the UK, but told MPs on Monday that many migrants would still face retrospective rule changes to make them wait a decade.
Under pressure from a cabinet backlash and health unions, the home secretary has offered a carve-out for care workers to allow them to apply for indefinite leave to remain after five years.
But most of the rigorous new rules drawn up by Mahmood’s office last year remain, including plans to force those who arrived in the UK by irregular means such as small boats to face up to 30 years before being able to apply for settlement.
The changes drew cries of betrayal from the Conservatives and the Reform UK leader, Nigel Farage, who said it was “the beginning of the capitulation”.
But Mahmood told the Commons she would still enact sweeping changes that will mean many migrant workers will wait double the time they had expected for settlement.
She said settlement was “one of most valuable rights this country can offer. Until now it has been given almost automatically. From today it must be earned. Those who contribute will settle fastest. Those who don’t play by the rules will be refused or wait much longer.”
In particular, the wait for those earning under £50,000 will double to 10 years. This was criticised by some Labour MPs who said vital workers such as research scientists and chefs would be caught by the changes.
The Law Society said the changing rules could threaten the rule of law, saying it “retrospectively undermines the legal certainty that individuals, families and employers rely on”.
Some MPs suggested they would continue to press the home secretary to rethink the retrospective nature of the changes – though the new policies do not require a vote in parliament, so MPs have limited means to block them.
Abtisam Mohamed, the Labour MP for Sheffield Central, said: “Retrospectively uprooting someone’s plans, sometimes made at the most vulnerable time in their lives, is unfair. I’ll be pressing for those already here to be protected.”
The former shadow home secretary Diane Abbott also criticised the retrospective changes. “You can come in legally, you can work legally and then have your residency rights turned upside down,” she said, warning of another potential Windrush scandal.
The Walthamstow MP Stella Creasy said there was a “partial recognition” of the contribution migrants made but there were thousands of people “facing 10 years of limbo with many businesses unclear if talent will stay or not as a result”.
She said: “The economic consequences of those people walking away from the UK will far outweigh any savings in entitlement to benefits, given many of them don’t claim anyway, so the home secretary still has work to do to make these reforms work for our national interest.”
Refugees will also face a longer wait of 10 years, with an additional 10-year penalty for those who do not enter legally – and those who do not find employment will face a wait of up to 30 years.
Andy Burnham, who promised voters in his Makerfield byelection that he would support Mahmood’s migration agenda, endorsed the plans and said the home secretary was “gripping this problem” by introducing the earned element.
“People want to see an immigration system based on control, contribution, and which rewards those who play by the rules,” the prime minister said. “It is only fair that those who are making the most valuable contribution to our communities are given the opportunity to settle earlier. Those in other roles should expect to wait longer while people who abuse the system or arrive illegally will be refused or will also have to wait longer.”
But migrant rights organisations accused the government of “moving the goalposts” for those who had played by the rules. “People who have built their lives around the government’s requirements deserve better than decisions that turn their own and their families’ lives upside down,” said Amnesty International.
The key climbdown from the home secretary was an exemption for care workers – something which the housing secretary, Angela Rayner, had explicitly criticised. The energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, also repeatedly refused to say she backed proposals to prolong the qualifying period for settlement.
Under pressure from health unions to make an exception for care workers, the home secretary has moved to allow an estimated 280,000 care workers and their dependents to apply for indefinite leave to remain after five years.
In the revised set of proposals, care workers earning more than £25,000 will be able to apply for indefinite leave to remain after five years, a third of the time that was announced last year.
Home Office officials calculate that about 500,000 migrants will have to wait longer than the current five years. But critics of Mahmood’s softening point out that 1.4 million out of the 1.9 million migrants who came to Britain under the so-called “Boriswave” surge in legal migrants will still be eligible for indefinite leave after five years.
Highest earners – those earning more than £125,000 – will be able to settle within three years. Those earning more than £50,271 and some public service workers such as doctors, nurses and teachers will be able to settle after five years.
The exception will be the small number of refugees who enter through designated safe and legal routes such as the reopening of the scheme for Afghan women and girls and Palestinians. No other refugees will be eligible for settlement if they have accessed any public funds.
Mahmood met union general secretaries to map out the changes on Monday morning, before presenting them to MPs. The Unison general secretary, Andrea Egan, said it was welcome that Mahmood had not implemented her original plans, which were “morally bankrupt and a threat to public services”.
Egan said the obligations placed on care workers to qualify for the five-year path were still onerous. “The government must make sure it isn’t unjustly denied to them. Thousands of migrant care workers have had their employment patterns and pay disrupted by rogue employers,” she said. “The power of employers to threaten workers with deportation or disrupt their route to settlement must end.”
Business groups warned that the retrospective nature of the changes would still cause far-reaching damage in some sectors. The CBI said the exemption for some care workers meant the policy risked “being higher costs for the relatively small number of businesses using skilled worker visas, without addressing the problem the policy was originally designed to solve”.
Make UK said it would make it far more difficult for businesses to retain skilled workers and industries would “undoubtedly lose talent to countries that welcome skilled workers rather than moving the goalposts”.
The shadow home secretary, Chris Philp, said Mahmood’s decision to allow a carve-out for care workers who arrived on the visa before May 2025 would cost the country up to £10bn, a figure Mahmood has cited in support of her original plans. The home secretary said the longer wait for settlement for more than half a million people would mean a cut to the projected benefits bill.
Other Conservative MPs acknowledged that it was the previous government who had allowed numbers to rise so significantly. The backbencher Edward Leigh said to Philp that “anybody who was serving as a Home Office minister at that time should wear sackcloth and ashes”.

title: Deep Purple müssen gesamte Europa-Tour verschieben
content_c:
Notfall bei Sänger Ian Gillan Deep Purple müssen gesamte Europa-Tour verschieben
Die britische Rockband Deep Purple hat nach den kurzfristigen Absagen in Leipzig und Hamburg auch alle weiteren Konzerte ihrer Europa- und UK-Tour verschoben. Grund ist ein medizinischer Notfall von Sänger Ian Gillan, 81, der während des Aufenthalts in Leipzig im Krankenhaus behandelt werden musste. Auf ärztlichen Rat habe die Band entschieden, die Tour bis auf Weiteres zu unterbrechen, teilte sie mit.
Betroffen sind neben den bereits ausgefallenen Auftritten in Leipzig (31. Oktober) und Hamburg (1. November) auch die Konzerte am 3. November in Dortmund, am 4. November in Berlin, am 6. November in Frankfurt am Main und am 7. November in Nürnberg.
In einer persönlichen Erklärung bedankte sich Gillan für die zahlreichen Genesungswünsche. Er habe gehofft, die Tour noch beenden zu können. Dies wäre jedoch mit »sehr ernsten Risiken« verbunden gewesen. Deshalb sei die Entscheidung zur Unterbrechung gemeinsam mit seinem Ärzteteam und dem Management gefallen. Zugleich entschuldigte sich der Sänger bei den Fans für die Unannehmlichkeiten.
Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung.
Die Stellungnahme veröffentlichte die Band erneut auf Instagram. Darunter äußerten zahlreiche Fans ihre Anteilnahme und wünschten Gillan eine schnelle Genesung.
Deep Purple, eine der bekanntesten britischen Hardrockbands, arbeitet nach eigenen Angaben bereits an Nachholterminen. Wann diese stattfinden, ist jedoch noch offen. Bereits gekaufte Tickets sollen für die Ersatzkonzerte ihre Gültigkeit behalten.
description: Die Europa-Tour der britischen Rockband Deep Purple kann nicht stattfinden. Hintergrund ist ein Krankenhausaufenthalt des 81-jährigen Frontmanns Ian Gillan. Die Konzerte sollen nachgeholt werden.

title: Cyberangriffe haben Supermärkte in Europa offenbar lahmgelegt
content_c:
Verdacht auf Cyberangriff Kühlsysteme in Supermärkten mehrerer Länder gestört
Cyberkriminelle haben offenbar wieder Supermärkte angegriffen. Sie sorgten besonders in Belgien und Schweden dafür, dass Kühlschränke und Tiefkühltruhen wärmer wurden. Es ist nicht das erste Mal.
In mehreren europäischen Ländern sind Supermärkte in der Nacht auf Montag mutmaßlich Ziel eines Cyberangriffs geworden. So wurden in Belgien, Schweden, Irland, Luxemburg, Estland, Finnland und den Niederlanden Kühlschränke und Tiefkühltruhen wärmer. Das berichteten die Nachrichtenagenturen Belga und TT sowie mehrere Medien.
In Belgien waren demnach unter anderem Supermärkte von Delhaize, Carrefour und SPAR betroffen sowie die IKEA-Filiale in der belgischen Stadt Mons. Nach Angaben des Unternehmens waren die Auswirkungen dort aber begrenzt. Wie Belga berichtete, sprach Delhaize von einem "IT-Vorfall" in rund 40 Filialen. Carrefour meldete demnach 15 betroffene Filialen, bei SPAR waren es fünf Geschäfte.
Alle Supermärkte meldeten einen plötzlichen Temperaturanstieg in den Kühlanlagen. Nach Angaben des Kühltechnik-Dienstleisters Sabcobel wurden die Anlagen aus der Ferne in den Abtaumodus versetzt. "Wir haben heute Nacht ab 1.00 Uhr damit begonnen, Techniker zu mobilisieren, um die Situation unter Kontrolle zu bringen", sagte Sabcobel-Vorstandschef Stephan Moelans. Die belgische Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt.
Weitere Länder betroffen
In Schweden waren am Montag die Ketten ICA und Coop betroffen. Ein schwedischer Supermarkt teilte in den sozialen Medien mit, die Temperatur in seinen Kühl- und Gefriergeräten sei auf bis zu 50 Grad hochgeregelt worden. Mehrere Filialen seien von dem nächtlichen Ausfall betroffen gewesen, hieß es vom Unternehmen ICA. Von einem Hackerangriff will die Supermarktkette aber noch nicht sprechen. Auch sieben Supermärkte der Kette Coop meldeten Probleme mit den Kühlsystemen.
In Irland waren nach Angaben des Senders RTÉ 13 Supermärkte betroffen. Vorsorglich wurden gekühlte und gefrorene Lebensmittel in den betroffenen Filialen aus dem Verkauf genommen. In den Niederlanden seien mindestens 17 kleinere Geschäfte betroffen, teilte das Kühltechnik-Unternehmen Danfoss mit. In Estland wurde ein Fall bekannt.
Auch aus Estland wurde ein Fall bekannt. Ein Supermarkt und das zuständige Kühltechnik-Unternehmen bestätigten den Vorfall. Demnach verschafften sich Angreifer Zugang zum Steuercomputer eines älteren Kühlsystems von Danfoss, dessen Software bisher nicht aktualisiert worden war. Nach Angaben des finnischen Rundfunks waren auch wenige kleinere Geschäfte in Finnland von einer Störung der Kühlsysteme betroffen.
Experte: Wohl keine finanziellen Motive
Bekannt hat sich bisher niemand zu den Angriffen. Es sei schwierig einzuschätzen, wer dahinter stehe, sagte Pontus Johnson, Leiter des Zentrums für Cyberabwehr an der Königlich Technischen Hochschule in Stockholm. Finanzielle Motive seien in diesem Fall wahrscheinlich ausgeschlossen - eher gehe es darum, für Unruhe in der Gesellschaft zu sorgen.
"Es könnten zum Beispiel prorussische Gruppen dahinterstehen", so Johnson. "Sie haben solche Dinge schon früher getan. Gruppen, die nicht unbedingt zum russischen Staatsapparat gehören, sondern verschiedene Störaktionen gegen westliche Staaten durchführen, um ihre Unterstützung für Russland zu zeigen."
Das Geschehen ähnelt einem großangelegten Angriff in Frankreich im vergangenen Monat. Dort hatten Hacker laut Polizei die Kontrolle über die Kühlanlagen Hunderter Supermärkte übernommen, was zum Verderb von Lebensmitteln und zu Bränden führte.
Gefahr für Deutschland?
EU-Agrarkommissar Christophe Hansen äußerte sich besorgt über die wiederholten Cyberangriffe: Es handele sich um den gezielten Versuch, Lebensmittelversorgungsketten zu stören und das Vertrauen der Verbraucher zu untergraben.
Laut IT-Sicherheitsexperten kommen vergleichbare Kühlsysteme auch in Deutschland zum Einsatz. Doch nicht alle Lebensmittelhändler nutzen dieselbe Soft- oder Hardware. Aber: Für Angreifer ist es durch den Einsatz Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) einfacher geworden, Sicherheitslücken zu finden. Bislang meldeten große deutsche Händler keine vergleichbaren Vorfälle wie in Frankreich, Belgien oder Schweden.

content:
Verdacht auf Cyberangriff Kühlsysteme in Supermärkten mehrerer Länder gestört
Cyberkriminelle haben offenbar wieder Supermärkte angegriffen. Sie sorgten besonders in Belgien und Schweden dafür, dass Kühlschränke und Tiefkühltruhen wärmer wurden. Es ist nicht das erste Mal.
In mehreren europäischen Ländern sind Supermärkte in der Nacht auf Montag mutmaßlich Ziel eines Cyberangriffs geworden. So wurden in Belgien, Schweden, Irland, Luxemburg, Estland, Finnland und den Niederlanden Kühlschränke und Tiefkühltruhen wärmer. Das berichteten die Nachrichtenagenturen Belga und TT sowie mehrere Medien.
In Belgien waren demnach unter anderem Supermärkte von Delhaize, Carrefour und SPAR betroffen sowie die IKEA-Filiale in der belgischen Stadt Mons. Nach Angaben des Unternehmens waren die Auswirkungen dort aber begrenzt. Wie Belga berichtete, sprach Delhaize von einem "IT-Vorfall" in rund 40 Filialen. Carrefour meldete demnach 15 betroffene Filialen, bei SPAR waren es fünf Geschäfte.
Alle Supermärkte meldeten einen plötzlichen Temperaturanstieg in den Kühlanlagen. Nach Angaben des Kühltechnik-Dienstleisters Sabcobel wurden die Anlagen aus der Ferne in den Abtaumodus versetzt. "Wir haben heute Nacht ab 1.00 Uhr damit begonnen, Techniker zu mobilisieren, um die Situation unter Kontrolle zu bringen", sagte Sabcobel-Vorstandschef Stephan Moelans. Die belgische Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt.
Weitere Länder betroffen
In Schweden waren am Montag die Ketten ICA und Coop betroffen. Ein schwedischer Supermarkt teilte in den sozialen Medien mit, die Temperatur in seinen Kühl- und Gefriergeräten sei auf bis zu 50 Grad hochgeregelt worden. Mehrere Filialen seien von dem nächtlichen Ausfall betroffen gewesen, hieß es vom Unternehmen ICA. Von einem Hackerangriff will die Supermarktkette aber noch nicht sprechen. Auch sieben Supermärkte der Kette Coop meldeten Probleme mit den Kühlsystemen.
In Irland waren nach Angaben des Senders RTÉ 13 Supermärkte betroffen. Vorsorglich wurden gekühlte und gefrorene Lebensmittel in den betroffenen Filialen aus dem Verkauf genommen. In den Niederlanden seien mindestens 17 kleinere Geschäfte betroffen, teilte das Kühltechnik-Unternehmen Danfoss mit. In Estland wurde ein Fall bekannt.
Auch aus Estland wurde ein Fall bekannt. Ein Supermarkt und das zuständige Kühltechnik-Unternehmen bestätigten den Vorfall. Demnach verschafften sich Angreifer Zugang zum Steuercomputer eines älteren Kühlsystems von Danfoss, dessen Software bisher nicht aktualisiert worden war. Nach Angaben des finnischen Rundfunks waren auch wenige kleinere Geschäfte in Finnland von einer Störung der Kühlsysteme betroffen.
Experte: Wohl keine finanziellen Motive
Bekannt hat sich bisher niemand zu den Angriffen. Es sei schwierig einzuschätzen, wer dahinter stehe, sagte Pontus Johnson, Leiter des Zentrums für Cyberabwehr an der Königlich Technischen Hochschule in Stockholm. Finanzielle Motive seien in diesem Fall wahrscheinlich ausgeschlossen - eher gehe es darum, für Unruhe in der Gesellschaft zu sorgen.
"Es könnten zum Beispiel prorussische Gruppen dahinterstehen", so Johnson. "Sie haben solche Dinge schon früher getan. Gruppen, die nicht unbedingt zum russischen Staatsapparat gehören, sondern verschiedene Störaktionen gegen westliche Staaten durchführen, um ihre Unterstützung für Russland zu zeigen."

title: Росіяни атакували Запоріжжя: перші подробиці
content_c:
Росіяни атакували Запоріжжя: перші подробиці
Унаслідок російської атаки постраждала 71-річна жінка, пошкоджені приватні будинки та автомобілі.
Російські війська атакували Запоріжжя. Внаслідок удару поранена 71-річна жінка, один із приватних житлових будинків частково зруйнований.
Про це повідомив очільник Запорізької ОВА Михайло Семікін.
Після атаки у приватному житловому будинку спалахнула пожежа. Ще кілька будинків та два автомобілі пошкоджені вибуховою хвилею й уламками.
Інформація про наслідки атаки уточнюється.
Нагадаємо, що раніше РФ вгатила по Запоріжжю: були постраждалі та пошкоджені будинки та пожежі

title: В ближайшее время нацгвардейцев переведут из Петропавловской Борщаговки — Музычук
content_c:
Нацгвардейцев из временного пункта размещения в селе Петропавловская Борщаговка Бучанского района Киевской области в ближайшее время переместят и распределят по местам дислокации из соображений безопасности. По словам командующего НГУ Александра Пивненко, там находились военные, возвращенные после самовольного оставления части, и мобилизованные, которые ожидали распределения. Об этом сообщил пресс-секретарь Национальной гвардии Украины Руслан Музычук.
Родственники военнослужащих Нацгвардии Украины в Петропавловской Борщаговке под Киевом смогли ознакомиться с условиями их пребывания. В то же время самих военных в ближайшее время переведут оттуда. В понедельник вечером Музычук рассказал журналистам, что некоторым родственникам разрешили зайти в место размещения. Они осмотрели условия, проверили, как обстоят дела, и пообщались с военными.
"И напряжение частично спало благодаря тому, что они своими глазами увидели, что люди находятся не в таком состоянии, как об этом распространялась информация в социальных сетях", — отметил Музычук.
Информацию о тяжких телесных повреждениях, которые якобы были у некоторых нацгвардейцев, пресс-секретарь назвал противоречивой. Он отметил, что поступают сообщения о людях, которым требуется помощь. Музычук обратил внимание журналистов на то, что некоторые люди, которые, возможно, нуждались в помощи, уже покинули место происшествия в машине скорой помощи.
В то же время выводы о необходимости оказания помощи этим людям будут делать врачи, подчеркнул он. Количество людей, находившихся на месте дислокации, Музычук отказался обнародовать, прежде всего из соображений безопасности. Он подчеркнул, что военные в любом случае вскоре покинут эту локацию и не будут находиться в этом здании.
"Я могу сказать, что в любом случае они покинут это место в ближайшее время, они здесь не будут находиться. Однозначно не будет этого здания, и я думаю, что в ближайшее время мы все отсюда рассеемся, если говорить военным языком. Мы не можем создавать условия, при которых 200–300 человек находятся в одной точке, потому что очень быстро этот участок становится заметным", — подчеркнул Музычук.
По словам пресс-секретаря, ситуации, подобные той, что сложилась в Петропавловской Борщаговке, будут учитываться для улучшения условий пребывания военнослужащих. Он подчеркнул, что страна находится в состоянии войны. Музычук отметил, что в условиях войны многие подходы к работе с мобилизационным ресурсом требуют совершенствования.
Напомним, что сообщение о незаконном удержании военных в доме в Петропавловской Борщаговке распространила 49-летняя Валентина Молодая. Она представилась владелицей клиники «Мед-престиж» и, по словам Бориса Бреуса из полиции Киевской области, вызвала правоохранителей. Журналисты выяснили, что компания не работает с 2023 года, а автомобиль скорой помощи продали в 2024-м.
Кроме того, на территории этого дома обнаружили 14-летнего подростка. Буданов связался с сестрой подростка и договорился, чтобы родственники приехали и забрали его домой. Один из присутствующих заявил об избиении подростка, после чего руководитель ОП пообещал выяснить обстоятельства и взял вопрос под личный контроль. По словам Буданова, дело об этом инциденте будет находиться под надзором ГБР, Генеральной прокуратуры и других правоохранительных органов.

title: СБУ заборонила польському журналісту Важесі в'їзд в Україну на три роки
content_c:
Польському журналісту Лукашу Важесі, відомому своєю антиукраїнською позицією, Служба безпеки України на три роки заборонила в'їзд до країни. Про це сам Важеха повідомив у соцмережі X у понеділок, 2 листопада.
"Кілька хвилин тому я отримав рішення СБУ: заборона на в'їзд в Україну терміном на три роки. Цьому передував цілий день очікування та втручання на високому рівні", – написав він у соцмережі Х.
Водночас польський історик Лукаш Адамський з Центру імені Мєрошевського повідомив, що Важеха був учасником навчального візиту польських журналістів до України, який центр організував спільно з Українським інститутом при МЗС України. За його словами, список учасників заздалегідь узгодили обидві установи та передали відповідним українським органам, і заперечень він не викликав.
Після проблем на кордоні центр поінформував МЗС України та Польщі. Попри запевнення, що питання переглянуть, після семи годин очікування рішення СБУ залишилося чинним, і Важеха повертається до Варшави.
"Визнаючи право України суверенно вирішувати, кому дозволяти в'їзд на свою територію, хочу зазначити, що обмеження діяльності журналістів – навіть якщо воно обґрунтоване міркуваннями національної безпеки – неминуче привертає значну увагу медіа та створює сприятливий ґрунт для негативних коментарів", – написав Адамський.
Між тим, агентство "Інтерфакс-Україна" наразі не має офіційного підтвердження цієї інформації від СБУ.

title: Trump loses supreme court bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots as justices refuse to take up emergency request – as it happened
content_c:
Supreme Court rejects request to intervene in California election case
The US supreme court on Monday quickly rejected the Trump administration’s request to force California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump’s administration claims are noncitizens, the Associated Press reports.
The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state’s voter rolls. The decision came just hours after the administration asked the supreme court to intervene.
The ruling was the latest judicial rebuke in the face of a wave of unprecedented efforts from the Trump administration to intervene in the elections process of multiple states. The midterm elections are expected to bring nationwide victories for Democrats and impose more Congressional checks on Trump’s power.
In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters’ citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters.
The high court did not detail its reasoning for rejecting the Trump administration’s request, as is common in emergency decisions. The justices previously rejected Trump’s push to restrict mail ballots around the country in September, even though the justices have sided with his administration in a series of other emergency docket appeals.
Here’s an updated evening summary of US politics news. The US midterm elections, expected to deliver significant if not historic wins for Democrats as voters’ rebuke to Donald Trump, are tomorrow. We’ll have round-the-clock-coverage for you then. In the meantime:
Trump’s justice department asked the supreme court to force Califronia election officials to set aside 20,000 mail ballotsthat the administration claims were submitted by non-citizens. Within hours, the supreme court had made its decision: No.
Elected officials in California celebrated the supreme court decision, which was one of two major court losses for the justice department that day: in a separate, related case, a federal judgeordered the Trump administration to stop demanding that California election officials set aside ballots, writing that “the Executive Branch has likely violated the Constitution’s Elections Clause, which commits authority over election rules to the states and Congress alone.”
But California governor Gavin Newsom said the state remained vigilant about additional inteference from Trump or his allies with the voting or ballot counting, and promised to prosecute anyone who tried to interfere with the election.
As Trump faced voter approval ratings of just 32%, close to his historic low, he posted a video reiterating his promise to all adult citizens that “If the Republicans win, you will each have $5,000 in your pocket,” a payout that would cost the government $1.2tn.
Asked about how soon the war with Iran would end, Trump gave a rambling answer that included his assertion, “this isn’t war”. And his claim that “there hasn’t been shooting for months.” Meanwhile, early news reports suggested that the US had in fact just conducted defensive strikes on some Iranian targets in the strait of Hormuz on the eve of the midterm elections.
Haley Stevens, the Democratic congresswoman who said she would now back the Republican nominee for US Senate in Michigan, defended her decision in an interview today. The representative who has faced fierce backlash for her eleventh-hour defection, also rejected any notion that she was “forced” into her decision to pull her endorsement and support Mike Rogers, the former GOP congressman.
Meanwhile,El-Sayed’s campaign announced that it received $2.4m in donations on Sunday, the day that Stevens announced she would now support Rogers. El-Sayed’s campaign that the amount is a single-day fundraising record for his Senate bid. His staff also noted that more than 26,000 people contributed for the first time on Sunday. The Cook Political Report changed its evaluation of the race from a “toss-up” to “Leans Democratic.” Fox News analysts were left hoping polling was overestimating El-Sayed’s lead, as it had during the Democratic primary earlier this year.
In Austin, Democratic senate candiate James Talarico is earning enthusiastic cheers from a crowd that seems to believe he is on the verge of a historic Texas win. The Democrat’s speech offers a mix of Texas history, music and sporting references. The ghost of Beto O’Rourke is nowhere to be seen.
Like Gina Hinojosa, the Democratic candidate for governor, Talarico identified tech mogul Elon Musk, who is building datacenters in Texas as a catalyst of corruption.
He said: “Paxton is funded by one dude. Elon Musk wants our land. He wants our water. He wants our tax dollars. He wants his very own personal United States senator. He is trying to buy Texas. But tomorrow we’re going to deliver a crystal clear message to the world’s first trillionaire. Texas is not for sale.”
Talarico said he and his campaign are the underdogs. “We are literally going up against the richest man in the world. We’re going up against the most powerful man in the world. This election is a battle between the powers that be and the powers that ought to be… They may have the money but we have the majority.”
Sara Cook, a longtime CBS News White House reporter, has highlighted one of Trump’s comments in his long response tonight to a question from Sean Hannity about what he could tell Americans about how soon the war with Iran will end.
Rather than reassurance, Trump provided something of a to-do list:
Trump told Hannity that “‘we might have to go after’ Pickaxe Mountain in Iran, calling it ‘not a big deal’ and saying could be done ‘in an hour,’” Cook noted on X.
She wrote that Trump had recently made a similar comment to her: “On Saturday Trump told me ‘we still have to take care of’ 1 or 2 sites, naming Pickaxe Mountain. ‘You have to take care of that.’”
Trump has made repeated public threats about targeting this same Iranian site before. As the Associated Press reported in July, “The site, known as Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La, or “Pickaxe Mountain,” lies on the south side of Iran’s Natanz nuclear enrichment site, which was bombed by the United States during Operation Midnight Hammer in 2025’s 12-day war between Iran and Israel. But Pickaxe Mountain has remained untouched as Iran continues to dig at the site.”
Down in the Des Moines suburbs in the early evening, as rain poured down and the sun set before 6 p.m., Sarah Booz knocked doors for Democratic candidates. On the doors, there were still a lot of undecided voters. Some told her they’d be voting for Sand and the rest of the downballot Dems, while others said they needed to do more research. One man who said he normally votes red said the gubernatorial race would probably be a last-minute decision. Another man and his daughter said they were looking up the candidates online and on ChatGPT.
And in the evening, at a Holiday Inn by the Des Moines airport, much of the Republican ticket rallied, culminating in a pitch from US Senate candidate Ashley Hinson.
Chuck Grassley, the Republican US senator and the oldest sitting US senator, took digs at Democratic gubernatiorial candidate Rob Sand, saying that the state government is well-run and “we don’t need Sand in that machinery”. He also called Democrats running across the country “outlandish socialists” who want to “transform America” instead of preserve it.
“I hope that you’ll do everything you can to make sure that I have a colleague from Iowa that won’t neutralize my vote,” he said, advocating for Hinson.
Hinson, taking the stage in front of a bus she’s been campaigning in that was signed all over by her supporters, called her opponent, Zach Turek, “Too Liberal Turek”.
“We fire liberal phonies, we don’t promote them,” she said.
In Texas, Democratic senate candidate James Talarico joined Hinojosa on stage and they held hands aloft. The crowd cheered. He began his speech with the analogy of a high school American football game.
Talarico said big money donors and super PACs have spent more money on this Senate race than any other in history. “They are scared. They are terrified. They see what we see: that we’re about to win this election tomorrow night.”
The Democrat went on to lambast his opponent, the Republican Ken Paxton. “We have an affordability crisis because we have a corruption crisis, but Austin, we can change that. In this election, in this state, in this race, we are running against the embodiment of this corrupt system.
“We are running against the most corrupt politician in Texas history. Ken Paxton represents everything that’s wrong with our politics. He doesn’t serve us. He serves himself.”
Talarico, a state representative, added: “I have a legislative record; Ken Paxton has a criminal record.”
Across Iowa on Monday, candidates and their supporters made final pitches in a set of toss-up races up and down the ballot, noting just how close these contests are - and just how pivotal the state could be for the nation’s politics.
In a standing-room-only town hall in Waverly, Iowa, Democratic gubernatorial hopeful Rob Sand started off by asking people in their crowd which political party they belong to, then having people clap for all of them, followed by directing the crowd to sing “America the Beautiful” together. The bipartisan tone underscores Sand’s pitch to Iowa voters, including those who would need to cross party lines to support him: “not redder or bluer, but better and truer”.
Wearing shirts that called to “rotate the crops” and vote for Democrats and saying “Iowa needs Sand”, about 150 voters turned out to the rally in the Republican-leaning area. Sand told the Guardian that he has seen throughout the hundreds of town halls he’s done a “yearning” from people that their politicians work together to solve problems, even as voters are generally angry this year.
“We need to focus that anger and point it at where it ought to be pointed, which is at a broken two-choice political system that is too easily abused to allow elected officials to be corrupt and to be lazy and still hold power,” he said. “A lot of politicians want people to be angry with their neighbors.”
Greetings from a “concert rally” on a warm evening at Stubbs Waller Creek Amphitheater in Austin, an open air venue with wood floor, neon-lit bars and a classic Texan barbecue. Politicians and musicians have been appearing on a stage beneath a curving white canopy. When the crowd was asked who had voted early, many hands went up.
Gina Hinojosa, the Democratic candidate for governor of Texas, walked on stage to chants of “Gina! Gina!” and told supporters that her election against incumbent Greg Abbott is “neck and neck”.
She then took aim at tech titan Elon Musk: “We have the world’s only trillionaire right here in our state. Elon Musk does billions of dollars in business with the state of Texas. It is why I fought a lawsuit here in Travis County District Court to demand that Greg Abbott release the emails between him and Elon Musk.”
Hinojosa added: “The Greg Abbott corruption tax is why data centers have descended upon Texas and we have more than any other state in the union… Greg Abbott is the most corrupt governor in all Texas history.”
In talking live to Trump tonight, Fox News host Sean Hannity gave Trump the ultimate softball: he asked the president to recap his accomplishments in the past two years, which he did at length.
What Hannity did not do at any point was ask Trump for comment on the high-profile supreme court decision today rejecting the administration’s request to have the court intervene in California’s election process on the side of Trump’s Justice Department.
Asked about when Iran war will end, Trump says, 'This isn’t war'
Asked about how soon the war with Iran would end, Donald Trump gave a rambling answer that included his assertion, “This isn’t war.”
“We’re not fighting a war. When was the last time we fired? …This is a very soft war,” Trump said, echoing comments he had made previously. He called $30bn spent on the war with Iran “peanuts” and later added, “There hasn’t been shooting for months.”
Fox News host Sean Hannity, who was speaking to the president live, did not ask Trump about the reports emerging this evening that directly contradicted those comments.
The US has conducted defensive strikes on some Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz on the eve of crucial midterm elections, the Associated Press reported, citing an unnamed US official. From the Associated Press:
Iranian state television reported that explosions were heard on Qeshm Island. The official, who wasn’t authorized to comment publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity, said “Iranians using surface to air missiles against US assets” had been targeted.
The strikes appeared to be limited as opposed to a return to full hostilities but followed Trump previously saying the US wouldn’t launch strikes on Iran before Tuesday’s midterms. The strikes were reported earlier by The Wall Street Journal.
As Donald Trump begins to speak live over the phone to Sean Hannity, in what he said would be his last public comment of the day, the Fox News host has asked the president to tout his accomplishments over the past two years.
But a poll released today suggests that Americans are not pleased with the president’s current performance. Trump’s current approval rating of 32%is close to his recent career low of 31%, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday.
It’s not a new observation, but it continues to be striking how Twitch streamer Hasan Piker is being talked about on the right as if he were a major Democratic leader, or, as Sean Hannity just put it on his show, the spiritual leader of the Democratic Party.
If you’re reading this liveblog, you probably have your on thoughts on Piker and the ways the socialist streamer has been invoked by both Democrats and Republicans this cycle. But if you’re like many Americans, and don’t really know who he is, read my colleague Rachel Leingang’s profile of him from September:
On Fox News, as Sean Hannity prepares to speak with Donald Trump about the midterm elections, a Fox analyst is suggesting-slash-hoping that current polls might once again be overestimating El-Sayed’s support in the Michigan senate race, as they did in the Democratic primary, which El-Sayed won very narrowly.
Astronauts for America, a nonpartisan group of more than 100 former NASA astronauts, has released a statement calling for free and fair elections in which “every lawful vote is counted.”
The statement, a clear criticism of the Trump administration’s Justice Department and its lawsuits attempting to influence how California, Alaska, and other states conduct their elections, notes that “The states have the central responsibility for conducting elections.”
This statement is a constitutional point that a federal judge emphasized today in ruling against the Trump administration’s attempt to interfere in the midterm elections in California.
This evening, California politicians celebrated the Trump administration’s failure to convince the supreme court to interve in their state’s election process over allegations of noncitizen voting. But election officials are still bracing for new attempts from the Trump administration to meddle with the election, or interfere with days of ballot-counting that will follow.
Democratic governor Gavin Newsom has made repeated public warnings that he will respond forcefully to any attempts to interfere with California’s vote or its ballot-counting.
Newsom reiterated those warnings in a video posted today, writing, “Let me be clear to anyone thinking about helping Trump interfere with California elections: If you interfere with voters or tamper with ballots, you will be prosecuted with a FELONY. And don’t count on a pardon from the President. He can’t pardon you out of California justice.”
In May, Newson signed new election-protection measures into law in anticipation of potentialTrump administration interference during the midterms. The law “prohibits any person – including federal agents – from accessing voter rolls or election technology without a court order” and makes clear that “law enforcement officers are restricted from disrupting election workers, except in public safety emergencies.”
Abdul El-Sayed mocked officials in the Trump administration during his final rally of his Michigan senate campaign, an event with the rapper Common at the Majestic Theater downtown Detroit, in front of over a thousand supporters.
On Trump, who make several Islamophobic remarks about El-Sayed today, and who keeps calling him “Mohammed,” he said: “Donald Trump can’t seem to remember what my name is, despite his incredibly high score on his cognitive test.”
He called vice president JD Vance “JV Dance.”
On health secretary Robert F Kennedy, who recently came to Michigan and disparaged the accomplishments of the Arab world, El-Sayed said: “His only expertise is that he understands what it means to have zero scientific contributions.”
“I’m like, habibi, listen, at the end of the day, I got two doctorates, you got none.”
“We beat their 70 million in the primary, they might as well have set their money on fire,” El Sayed said. “And we’re going to beat their 250 million in the general. Go ahead and set your money on fire.”
US envoy Steve Witkoff said the United States will bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 to discuss ending Moscow’s war against Ukraine, post-war security agreements and de-escalation, Reuters reports.
US negotiators have been seeking a breakthrough in the long-running conflict before the winter sets in. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran.
